decls.name: TauCeti.ClassGroup.ElementaryTwoQuotient
decls.doc:
**The maximal elementary-2 quotient `Cl(R)/Cl(R)²` of the class group**, the general
`TauCeti.ElementaryTwoQuotient` specialized to `ClassGroup R`.
decls.title: The maximal elementary-2 quotient `Cl(R)/Cl(R)²` of the class group
decls.statement: abbrev ElementaryTwoQuotient : Type _

decls.name: TauCeti.ClassGroup.elementaryTwoQuotientMk
decls.doc: The class of an ideal class in the maximal elementary-2 quotient `Cl(R)/Cl(R)²`.
decls.statement: def elementaryTwoQuotientMk (C : ClassGroup R) : ElementaryTwoQuotient R

decls.name: TauCeti.ClassGroup.elementaryTwoQuotientMk_eq_zero_iff
decls.doc: An ideal class has trivial class in `Cl(R)/Cl(R)²` iff it is a square.
decls.statement:
theorem elementaryTwoQuotientMk_eq_zero_iff (C : ClassGroup R) :
    elementaryTwoQuotientMk R C = 0 ↔ IsSquare C

decls.name: TauCeti.ClassGroup.elementaryTwoQuotientMk_mul
decls.doc: The class map to `Cl(R)/Cl(R)²` sends a product of ideal classes to the sum of the classes.
decls.statement:
theorem elementaryTwoQuotientMk_mul (C D : ClassGroup R) :
    elementaryTwoQuotientMk R (C * D) = elementaryTwoQuotientMk R C + elementaryTwoQuotientMk R D

decls.name: TauCeti.ClassGroup.elementaryTwoQuotientMk_one
decls.doc: The class map to `Cl(R)/Cl(R)²` sends the trivial ideal class to `0`.
decls.statement:
theorem elementaryTwoQuotientMk_one :
    elementaryTwoQuotientMk R (1 : ClassGroup R) = 0

decls.name: TauCeti.ClassGroup.elementaryTwoQuotientMk_inv
decls.doc: The class map to `Cl(R)/Cl(R)²` sends inverses to negatives.
decls.statement:
theorem elementaryTwoQuotientMk_inv (C : ClassGroup R) :
    elementaryTwoQuotientMk R C⁻¹ = -elementaryTwoQuotientMk R C

decls.name: TauCeti.ClassGroup.elementaryTwoQuotientMk_div
decls.doc: The class map to `Cl(R)/Cl(R)²` sends quotients to differences.
decls.statement:
theorem elementaryTwoQuotientMk_div (C D : ClassGroup R) :
    elementaryTwoQuotientMk R (C / D) =
      elementaryTwoQuotientMk R C - elementaryTwoQuotientMk R D

decls.name: TauCeti.ClassGroup.elementaryTwoQuotientMk_pow
decls.doc: The class map to `Cl(R)/Cl(R)²` sends powers to scalar multiples.
decls.statement:
theorem elementaryTwoQuotientMk_pow (C : ClassGroup R) (n : ℕ) :
    elementaryTwoQuotientMk R (C ^ n) = n • elementaryTwoQuotientMk R C

decls.name: TauCeti.ClassGroup.elementaryTwoQuotientMk_prod
decls.doc:
The class map to `Cl(R)/Cl(R)²` sends a finite product of ideal classes to the sum of the
classes.
decls.statement:
theorem elementaryTwoQuotientMk_prod {ι : Type*} (S : Finset ι) (C : ι → ClassGroup R) :
    elementaryTwoQuotientMk R (∏ i ∈ S, C i) = ∑ i ∈ S, elementaryTwoQuotientMk R (C i)

decls.name: TauCeti.ClassGroup.elementaryTwoQuotientMk_surjective
decls.doc: Every element of `Cl(R)/Cl(R)²` is the class of some ideal class.
decls.statement:
theorem elementaryTwoQuotientMk_surjective :
    Function.Surjective (elementaryTwoQuotientMk R)

decls.name: TauCeti.ClassGroup.elementaryTwoQuotientMk_eq_iff
decls.doc: Two ideal classes have the same class in `Cl(R)/Cl(R)²` iff they differ by a square.
decls.statement:
theorem elementaryTwoQuotientMk_eq_iff (C D : ClassGroup R) :
    elementaryTwoQuotientMk R C = elementaryTwoQuotientMk R D ↔ IsSquare (C / D)

decls.name: TauCeti.ClassGroup.elementaryTwoQuotientCongr
decls.doc:
A multiplicative equivalence of class groups induces a `ZMod 2`-linear equivalence on the
maximal elementary-2 quotients. This is the transport API used when genus-field constructions
identify class groups through canonical isomorphisms.
decls.statement:
def elementaryTwoQuotientCongr {S : Type*} [CommRing S] [IsDomain S]
    (e : ClassGroup R ≃* ClassGroup S) :
    ElementaryTwoQuotient R ≃ₗ[ZMod 2] ElementaryTwoQuotient S

decls.name: TauCeti.ClassGroup.elementaryTwoQuotientCongr_mk
decls.doc:
The induced equivalence on `Cl/Cl²` sends the class of an ideal class to the class of its
image.
decls.statement:
theorem elementaryTwoQuotientCongr_mk {S : Type*} [CommRing S] [IsDomain S]
    (e : ClassGroup R ≃* ClassGroup S) (C : ClassGroup R) :
    elementaryTwoQuotientCongr e (elementaryTwoQuotientMk R C) =
      elementaryTwoQuotientMk S (e C)

decls.name: TauCeti.ClassGroup.elementaryTwoQuotientCongr_symm_mk
decls.doc:
The inverse induced equivalence on `Cl/Cl²` sends the class of an ideal class to the class
of its inverse image.
decls.statement:
theorem elementaryTwoQuotientCongr_symm_mk {S : Type*} [CommRing S] [IsDomain S]
    (e : ClassGroup R ≃* ClassGroup S) (C : ClassGroup S) :
    (elementaryTwoQuotientCongr e).symm (elementaryTwoQuotientMk S C) =
      elementaryTwoQuotientMk R (e.symm C)

decls.name: TauCeti.ClassGroup.elementaryTwoQuotientCongr_refl_apply
decls.doc: The identity equivalence of class groups induces the identity equivalence on `Cl/Cl²`.
decls.statement:
theorem elementaryTwoQuotientCongr_refl_apply (x : ElementaryTwoQuotient R) :
    elementaryTwoQuotientCongr (MulEquiv.refl (ClassGroup R)) x = x

decls.name: TauCeti.ClassGroup.elementaryTwoQuotientCongr_trans_apply
decls.doc: Induced class-group equivalences on `Cl/Cl²` compose functorially.
decls.statement:
theorem elementaryTwoQuotientCongr_trans_apply {S T : Type*} [CommRing S] [IsDomain S]
    [CommRing T] [IsDomain T] (e : ClassGroup R ≃* ClassGroup S)
    (e' : ClassGroup S ≃* ClassGroup T) (x : ElementaryTwoQuotient R) :
    elementaryTwoQuotientCongr (e.trans e') x =
      elementaryTwoQuotientCongr e' (elementaryTwoQuotientCongr e x)

decls.name: TauCeti.ClassGroup.twoRank
decls.doc:
**The 2-rank of the class group**: the `ZMod 2` dimension of the maximal elementary-2
quotient `Cl(R)/Cl(R)²` (zero, by convention of `Module.finrank`, when the quotient is
infinite-dimensional). In genus-theory applications the `t - 1` formula belongs to the narrow
class group; for imaginary fields the narrow and ordinary class groups coincide.
decls.title: The 2-rank of the class group
decls.statement: def twoRank : ℕ

decls.name: TauCeti.ClassGroup.twoRank_def
decls.doc:
The 2-rank of the class group is the `ZMod 2` dimension of its maximal elementary-2 quotient
`Cl(R) / Cl(R)²`.
decls.statement:
theorem twoRank_def :
    twoRank R = Module.finrank (ZMod 2) (ElementaryTwoQuotient R)

decls.name: TauCeti.ClassGroup.card_elementaryTwoQuotient_eq_two_pow_twoRank
decls.doc:
The maximal elementary-2 quotient has cardinality `2 ^ twoRank`: it is a finite `𝔽₂`-vector
space of dimension the 2-rank.
decls.statement:
theorem card_elementaryTwoQuotient_eq_two_pow_twoRank
    [Module.Finite (ZMod 2) (ElementaryTwoQuotient R)] :
    Nat.card (ElementaryTwoQuotient R) = 2 ^ twoRank R

decls.name: TauCeti.ClassGroup.finrank_elementaryTwoQuotient_eq_of_mulEquiv
decls.doc:
Multiplicatively equivalent class groups have `Cl/Cl²` quotients with the same `ZMod 2`
finrank.
decls.statement:
theorem finrank_elementaryTwoQuotient_eq_of_mulEquiv {S : Type*} [CommRing S] [IsDomain S]
    (e : ClassGroup R ≃* ClassGroup S) :
    Module.finrank (ZMod 2) (ElementaryTwoQuotient R) =
      Module.finrank (ZMod 2) (ElementaryTwoQuotient S)

decls.name: TauCeti.ClassGroup.twoRank_eq_of_mulEquiv
decls.doc: Multiplicatively equivalent class groups have the same elementary-2 rank.
decls.statement:
theorem twoRank_eq_of_mulEquiv {S : Type*} [CommRing S] [IsDomain S]
    (e : ClassGroup R ≃* ClassGroup S) :
    twoRank R = twoRank S

decls.name: TauCeti.ClassGroup.card_elementaryTwoQuotient_dvd_card
decls.doc:
The cardinality of `Cl(R)/Cl(R)²` divides the cardinality of `Cl(R)` when the class group is
finite, and more generally in Mathlib's cardinal arithmetic.
decls.statement:
theorem card_elementaryTwoQuotient_dvd_card :
    Nat.card (ElementaryTwoQuotient R) ∣ Nat.card (ClassGroup R)

decls.name: TauCeti.ClassGroup.two_pow_twoRank_dvd_card
decls.doc:
Rank form of `TauCeti.ClassGroup.card_elementaryTwoQuotient_dvd_card`:
`2 ^ TauCeti.ClassGroup.twoRank R` divides the cardinality of `Cl(R)` when `Cl(R)/Cl(R)²`
is finite-dimensional.
decls.statement:
theorem two_pow_twoRank_dvd_card [Module.Finite (ZMod 2) (ElementaryTwoQuotient R)] :
    2 ^ twoRank R ∣ Nat.card (ClassGroup R)

decls.name: TauCeti.ClassGroup.instFiniteZModOfNatNatElementaryTwoQuotient
decls.doc: A finite class group has finite-dimensional elementary-2 quotient.
decls.statement: instance : Module.Finite (ZMod 2) (ElementaryTwoQuotient R)

decls.name: TauCeti.ClassGroup.card_elementaryTwoQuotient_le_card
decls.doc:
The elementary-2 quotient of a finite class group has cardinality at most the class-group
cardinality.
decls.statement:
theorem card_elementaryTwoQuotient_le_card :
    Nat.card (ElementaryTwoQuotient R) ≤ Nat.card (ClassGroup R)

decls.name: TauCeti.ClassGroup.two_pow_twoRank_le_card
decls.doc:
Rank form of `TauCeti.ClassGroup.card_elementaryTwoQuotient_le_card`:
`2 ^ TauCeti.ClassGroup.twoRank R` is bounded by the cardinality of `Cl(R)`.
decls.statement:
theorem two_pow_twoRank_le_card :
    2 ^ twoRank R ≤ Nat.card (ClassGroup R)

decls.name: TauCeti.ClassGroup.card_elementaryTwoQuotient_eq_card_twoTorsion
decls.doc:
**The maximal elementary-2 quotient and the 2-torsion subgroup have the same cardinality.**
`|Cl(R)/Cl(R)²| = |Cl(R)[2]|`.
decls.title: The maximal elementary-2 quotient and the 2-torsion subgroup have the same cardinality
decls.statement:
theorem card_elementaryTwoQuotient_eq_card_twoTorsion :
    Nat.card (ElementaryTwoQuotient R) = Nat.card {C : ClassGroup R // C ^ 2 = 1}

decls.name: ClassGroup.mulEquiv_mk_fractionRing
decls.doc:
`ClassGroup.mulEquiv f` sends the class of a unit fractional ideal `I` to the class of its
image under `FractionalIdeal.ringEquivOfRingEquiv f`. This is the characteristic computation of the
induced map on ideal classes; the functorial laws below are corollaries. Its fully-determined
left-hand side makes it the `simp`-usable form; `mulEquiv_mk` is the general `rw`-form over
arbitrary fraction fields.
decls.statement:
theorem mulEquiv_mk_fractionRing (f : R ≃+* S)
    (I : (FractionalIdeal R⁰ (FractionRing R))ˣ) :
    ClassGroup.mulEquiv f (ClassGroup.mk (FractionRing R) I) =
      ClassGroup.mk (FractionRing S)
        (Units.mapEquiv (FractionalIdeal.ringEquivOfRingEquiv
          (FractionRing R) (FractionRing S) f) I)

decls.name: ClassGroup.canonicalEquiv_eq_ringEquivOfRingEquiv
decls.doc:
The canonical equivalence between the fractional ideals of two fraction fields of `R` is
transport along the identity ring equivalence. This lets a change of fraction field and a transport
along a ring equivalence be composed by `FractionalIdeal.ringEquivOfRingEquiv_trans_apply`.
decls.statement:
theorem canonicalEquiv_eq_ringEquivOfRingEquiv (K K' : Type*) [Field K] [Field K']
    [Algebra R K] [Algebra R K'] [IsFractionRing R K] [IsFractionRing R K'] :
    FractionalIdeal.canonicalEquiv R⁰ K K' =
      FractionalIdeal.ringEquivOfRingEquiv K K' (RingEquiv.refl R)

decls.name: ClassGroup.mulEquiv_mk
decls.doc:
`ClassGroup.mulEquiv f` sends the class of a unit fractional ideal `I` to the class of its
image under `FractionalIdeal.ringEquivOfRingEquiv f`. This is independent of the chosen fraction
fields.
decls.statement:
theorem mulEquiv_mk {K : Type*} (L : Type*) [Field K] [Field L] [Algebra R K]
    [Algebra S L] [IsFractionRing R K] [IsFractionRing S L] (f : R ≃+* S)
    (I : (FractionalIdeal R⁰ K)ˣ) :
    ClassGroup.mulEquiv f (ClassGroup.mk K I) =
      ClassGroup.mk L
        (Units.mapEquiv (FractionalIdeal.ringEquivOfRingEquiv K L f) I)

decls.name: ClassGroup.mulEquiv_refl
decls.doc: The identity ring equivalence induces the identity class-group equivalence.
decls.statement:
theorem mulEquiv_refl :
    ClassGroup.mulEquiv (RingEquiv.refl R) = MulEquiv.refl (ClassGroup R)

decls.name: ClassGroup.mulEquiv_trans
decls.doc:
Composition of ring equivalences is carried to composition of the induced class-group
equivalences.
decls.statement:
theorem mulEquiv_trans (f : R ≃+* S) (g : S ≃+* T) :
    ClassGroup.mulEquiv (f.trans g) =
      (ClassGroup.mulEquiv f).trans (ClassGroup.mulEquiv g)

decls.name: ClassGroup.mulEquiv_trans_apply
decls.doc:
Pointwise form of `ClassGroup.mulEquiv_trans`. This is not a simp lemma because
`ClassGroup.mulEquiv_apply` already rewrites its left-hand side.
decls.statement:
theorem mulEquiv_trans_apply (f : R ≃+* S) (g : S ≃+* T) (x : ClassGroup R) :
    ClassGroup.mulEquiv (f.trans g) x = ClassGroup.mulEquiv g (ClassGroup.mulEquiv f x)

decls.name: ClassGroup.mulEquiv_refl_apply
decls.doc:
Pointwise form of `ClassGroup.mulEquiv_refl`. This is not a simp lemma because
`ClassGroup.mulEquiv_refl` already proves the bundled normal form.
decls.statement:
theorem mulEquiv_refl_apply (x : ClassGroup R) :
    ClassGroup.mulEquiv (RingEquiv.refl R) x = x

decls.name: ClassGroup.mulEquiv_symm
decls.doc: The inverse of the class-group equivalence induced by `f` is induced by `f.symm`.
decls.statement:
theorem mulEquiv_symm (f : R ≃+* S) :
    (ClassGroup.mulEquiv f).symm = ClassGroup.mulEquiv f.symm

decls.name: ClassGroup.mulEquiv_symm_apply'
decls.doc:
Pointwise form of `ClassGroup.mulEquiv_symm`. This is not a simp lemma because
`ClassGroup.mulEquiv_apply` already rewrites its left-hand side.
decls.statement:
theorem mulEquiv_symm_apply' (f : R ≃+* S) (x : ClassGroup S) :
    (ClassGroup.mulEquiv f).symm x = ClassGroup.mulEquiv f.symm x

decls.name: ClassGroup.mulEquivHom
decls.doc:
The action of ring automorphisms of `R` on `ClassGroup R`, bundled as a monoid homomorphism
`(R ≃+* R) →* MulAut (ClassGroup R)`. This is the object the roadmap's Galois action on ideal
classes transports along; it is the class-group analogue of
`IsFractionRing.ringEquivOfRingEquivHom`.
decls.statement: def mulEquivHom : (R ≃+* R) →* MulAut (ClassGroup R)

decls.name: ClassGroup.mulEquivHom_apply
decls.doc: `ClassGroup.mulEquivHom` acts as `ClassGroup.mulEquiv` on each ring automorphism.
decls.statement:
theorem mulEquivHom_apply (f : R ≃+* R) :
    mulEquivHom f = ClassGroup.mulEquiv f

decls.name: ClassGroup.mulEquiv_involutive
decls.doc:
An involutive ring equivalence induces an involution on the class group. This is the form
used for quadratic conjugation; it is the pointwise specialization of `ClassGroup.mulEquivHom`
at an order-two automorphism.
decls.statement:
theorem mulEquiv_involutive {f : R ≃+* R} (hf : Function.Involutive f) :
    Function.Involutive (ClassGroup.mulEquiv f)

decls.name: TauCeti.DedekindDomain.ncard_primesOver_eq_natCard_iff_of_isGaloisGroup
decls.doc:
Deprecated compatibility wrapper for the old Dedekind-domain signature of
`TauCeti.RamificationInertia.ncard_primesOver_eq_natCard_iff_of_isGaloisGroup`.
decls.statement:
theorem ncard_primesOver_eq_natCard_iff_of_isGaloisGroup {A B : Type*} [CommRing A]
    [IsDedekindDomain A] [CommRing B] [IsDedekindDomain B] [Algebra A B] [Module.Finite A B]
    [IsTorsionFree A B] (G : Type*) [Group G] [Finite G] [MulSemiringAction G B]
    [IsGaloisGroup G A B] (P : Ideal A) [P.IsMaximal] (_hP : P ≠ ⊥) :
    (primesOver P B).ncard = Nat.card G ↔
      P.ramificationIdxIn B = 1 ∧ P.inertiaDegIn B = 1

decls.name: TauCeti.DedekindDomain.isPrime_not_dvd_prod
decls.doc:
A nonzero prime ideal of a Dedekind domain does not divide a finite product of nonzero
prime ideals unless it equals one of the factors.
decls.statement:
theorem isPrime_not_dvd_prod (p : IsDedekindDomain.HeightOneSpectrum R)
    {T : Finset (IsDedekindDomain.HeightOneSpectrum R)} (hpT : p ∉ T) :
    ¬ p.asIdeal ∣ ∏ q ∈ T, q.asIdeal

decls.name: TauCeti.DedekindDomain.notMem_pair_of_apply_involutive
decls.doc:
Under an involutive `f` with `q = f p`, the image `f x` of an element outside the pair
`{p, q}` again lies outside `{p, q}`.

decls.name: TauCeti.DedekindDomain.asIdeal_equivOfRingEquiv
decls.doc:
Transporting a height-one prime along a ring equivalence `σ` maps its ideal to the image
ideal: `(equivOfRingEquiv σ p).asIdeal = Ideal.map σ p.asIdeal`.
decls.statement:
lemma asIdeal_equivOfRingEquiv (σ : R ≃+* R)
    (p : IsDedekindDomain.HeightOneSpectrum R) :
    (IsDedekindDomain.HeightOneSpectrum.equivOfRingEquiv σ p).asIdeal =
      Ideal.map σ p.asIdeal

decls.name: TauCeti.DedekindDomain.disjoint_image_mul_asIdeal
decls.doc:
For a distinct prime `q ≠ p` and a family `G'` no member of which is divisible by `p.asIdeal`,
multiplying `G'` by `p.asIdeal` and by `q.asIdeal` gives disjoint images.

decls.name: TauCeti.DedekindDomain.two_pow_div_two_le_two_mul_two_pow_div_two_of_le_add_two
decls.statement:
lemma two_pow_div_two_le_two_mul_two_pow_div_two_of_le_add_two {m n : ℕ} (hmn : n ≤ m + 2) :
    2 ^ (n / 2) ≤ 2 * 2 ^ (m / 2)

decls.name: TauCeti.DedekindDomain.mul_map_eq_prod_of_mem_image_union
decls.doc:
Every ideal in the union `G'.image (· * P) ∪ G'.image (· * Q)` has conjugate product `prodS`,
given the conjugate-pair relations `Q = Ideal.map σ P` and `Ideal.map σ Q = P`, the factorisation
`prodS = prodS' * P * Q` of the product through the pair, and the product property
`a * Ideal.map σ a = prodS'` of every `a ∈ G'`. This is a pure identity about ideals under a ring
homomorphism `σ`, valid over any commutative semiring (no Dedekind structure needed).

decls.name: TauCeti.DedekindDomain.two_pow_le_card_union_image_mul
decls.doc:
**Two shifted copies double the family.** Multiplying a family of ideals by each of two
height-one primes gives images of the same size, and if those images are disjoint the union has
twice the cardinality. That is exactly enough to carry a bound `2 ^ (m / 2)` up to `2 ^ (n / 2)`
whenever `n ≤ m + 2` — the two primes removed from the index set at each induction step. No
relationship between the primes is assumed beyond disjointness of the images; the caller
supplies a conjugate pair, but the estimate does not need that.
decls.title: Two shifted copies double the family

decls.name: TauCeti.DedekindDomain.mem_sdiff_pair_of_invariant
decls.doc:
**The complement of a conjugate pair is still invariant.** Removing `p` and its image `q`
from `S` leaves a set the involution still maps to itself: an element outside the pair cannot be
sent into it, since applying the involution twice returns it.
decls.title: The complement of a conjugate pair is still invariant

decls.name: TauCeti.DedekindDomain.exists_transversal_family
decls.doc:
**Conjugate-transversal ideal family.** For a fixed-point-free involution `σ` of a finite set
`S` of height-one primes of a Dedekind domain, there are at least `2 ^ (S.card / 2)` ideals `A`
with `A * σ A = ∏ p ∈ S, p.asIdeal`.
decls.title: Conjugate-transversal ideal family
decls.statement:
theorem exists_transversal_family (σ : R ≃+* R)
    (S : Finset (IsDedekindDomain.HeightOneSpectrum R))
    (hinv : ∀ p ∈ S, IsDedekindDomain.HeightOneSpectrum.equivOfRingEquiv σ p ∈ S)
    (hinvol : ∀ p ∈ S,
      IsDedekindDomain.HeightOneSpectrum.equivOfRingEquiv σ
        (IsDedekindDomain.HeightOneSpectrum.equivOfRingEquiv σ p) = p)
    (hfree : ∀ p ∈ S, IsDedekindDomain.HeightOneSpectrum.equivOfRingEquiv σ p ≠ p) :
    ∃ G : Finset (Ideal R), 2 ^ (S.card / 2) ≤ G.card ∧
      ∀ A ∈ G, A * Ideal.map σ A = ∏ p ∈ S, p.asIdeal

decls.name: TauCeti.NumberField.minkowski_factor_sq_mul_two_pow_le_four_pow
decls.doc:
The squared Minkowski covolume factor, times `2 ^ n`, is at most `4 ^ n` whenever
`2 * s ≤ n`.
decls.statement:
lemma minkowski_factor_sq_mul_two_pow_le_four_pow {n s : ℕ} (h : 2 * s ≤ n) :
    (4 / Real.pi) ^ (2 * s) * ((n.factorial / n ^ n : ℝ)) ^ 2 * 2 ^ n ≤ 4 ^ n

decls.name: TauCeti.NumberField.classNumber_le_bound
decls.doc:
**Class number bound.** The class number of a number field `F` is at most
`|discr F| * 4 ^ [F : ℚ]`.
decls.title: Class number bound
decls.statement:
theorem classNumber_le_bound (F : Type*) [Field F] [NumberField F] :
    (NumberField.classNumber F : ℝ) ≤
      |(NumberField.discr F : ℝ)| * 4 ^ Module.finrank ℚ F

decls.name: TauCeti.NumberField.classNumber_le_of_abs_discr_le_of_finrank_le
decls.doc:
If a number field has discriminant bounded by `D` and degree bounded by `n`, then its class
number is bounded by `D * 4^n`.

This is the monotone form of `TauCeti.NumberField.classNumber_le_bound`, useful when the
discriminant and degree have already been bounded separately.
decls.statement:
theorem classNumber_le_of_abs_discr_le_of_finrank_le (F : Type*) [Field F] [NumberField F]
    {D : ℝ} {n : ℕ} (hD : |(NumberField.discr F : ℝ)| ≤ D)
    (hn : Module.finrank ℚ F ≤ n) :
    (NumberField.classNumber F : ℝ) ≤ D * 4 ^ n

decls.name: TauCeti.NumberField.classNumber_le_nat_of_abs_discr_le_of_finrank_le
decls.doc:
A version of `classNumber_le_of_abs_discr_le_of_finrank_le` with a natural-number
discriminant bound and a natural-number conclusion.

Here `|NumberField.discr F|` is the integer absolute value of the discriminant, compared with
the natural-number bound `D` coerced to `ℤ`, so this is the form to use when the available
discriminant estimate is stated in `ℕ`.
decls.statement:
theorem classNumber_le_nat_of_abs_discr_le_of_finrank_le (F : Type*) [Field F] [NumberField F]
    {D n : ℕ} (hD : |NumberField.discr F| ≤ D) (hn : Module.finrank ℚ F ≤ n) :
    NumberField.classNumber F ≤ D * 4 ^ n

decls.name: TauCeti.NumberField.classNumber_le_of_abs_discr_le
decls.doc: If `|d_F| ≤ D`, then `h_F ≤ D * 4^[F:ℚ]`.

decls.name: TauCeti.NumberField.classNumber_le_nat_of_abs_discr_le
decls.doc: Natural-number version of `classNumber_le_of_abs_discr_le`.

decls.name: TauCeti.NumberField.abs_discr_le_natAbs
decls.statement:
lemma abs_discr_le_natAbs (F : Type*) [Field F] [NumberField F] :
    |NumberField.discr F| ≤ (NumberField.discr F).natAbs

decls.name: TauCeti.NumberField.four_pow_mul_two_pow
decls.statement: lemma four_pow_mul_two_pow (n : ℕ) : 4 ^ n * 2 ^ n = 8 ^ n

decls.name: TauCeti.NumberField.classNumber_mul_units_sq_index_le
decls.doc:
**Class-number/unit-square product bound.** For a number field `F`, the product of its class
number and the index of squares in its unit group is at most `|d_F| * 8^[F:ℚ]`.
decls.title: Class-number/unit-square product bound
decls.statement:
theorem classNumber_mul_units_sq_index_le (F : Type*) [Field F] [NumberField F] :
    NumberField.classNumber F * (Subgroup.square (𝓞 F)ˣ).index ≤
      (NumberField.discr F).natAbs * 8 ^ finrank ℚ F

decls.name: TauCeti.NumberField.classNumber_mul_units_sq_index_le_of_abs_discr_le_of_finrank_le
decls.doc:
Monotone form of `TauCeti.NumberField.classNumber_mul_units_sq_index_le`: if `|d_F| ≤ D`
and `[F : ℚ] ≤ n`, then
`h_F * [O_F^× : (O_F^×)^2] ≤ D * 8^n`.
decls.statement:
theorem classNumber_mul_units_sq_index_le_of_abs_discr_le_of_finrank_le
    (F : Type*) [Field F] [NumberField F] {D n : ℕ}
    (hD : |NumberField.discr F| ≤ D) (hn : finrank ℚ F ≤ n) :
    NumberField.classNumber F * (Subgroup.square (𝓞 F)ˣ).index ≤ D * 8 ^ n

decls.name: TauCeti.NumberField.classNumber_mul_units_sq_index_le_of_abs_discr_le
decls.statement:
theorem classNumber_mul_units_sq_index_le_of_abs_discr_le
    (F : Type*) [Field F] [NumberField F] {D : ℕ}

      D * 8 ^ finrank ℚ F

decls.name: TauCeti.NumberField.classNumber_mul_units_sq_index_le_of_finrank_le
decls.statement:
theorem classNumber_mul_units_sq_index_le_of_finrank_le
    (F : Type*) [Field F] [NumberField F] {n : ℕ} (hn : finrank ℚ F ≤ n) :

decls.statement:

decls.statement:

decls.name: TauCeti.NumberField.intCast_four_mul_natAbs

lemma intCast_four_mul_natAbs (a : ℤ) :

decls.name: TauCeti.NumberField.classNumber_le_of_sq_intCast
decls.doc:
**Quadratic square-root class-number bound.** If `K` is a quadratic number field
generated by an algebraic integer `x` with `x² = a ∈ ℤ` and `x ∉ ℚ`, then
`h_K ≤ 64·|a|`. This is the specialization of the general effective class-number bound
using the square-root discriminant estimate `|d_K| ≤ 4·|a|` and `[K : ℚ] = 2`.
decls.title: Quadratic square-root class-number bound
decls.statement:
theorem classNumber_le_of_sq_intCast {K : Type*} [Field K] [NumberField K]
    {x : K} {a : ℤ} (hfin : finrank ℚ K = 2)
    (hx2 : x ^ 2 = algebraMap ℤ K a) (hx : x ∉ (algebraMap ℚ K).range) :
    (NumberField.classNumber K : ℝ) ≤ 64 * |(a : ℝ)|

decls.name: TauCeti.NumberField.classNumber_le_natAbs_of_sq_intCast

    NumberField.classNumber K ≤ 64 * a.natAbs

decls.name: TauCeti.NumberField.classNumber_le_of_sq_intCast_of_natAbs_le
decls.doc:
A version of `TauCeti.NumberField.classNumber_le_of_sq_intCast` with a separate
natural-number bound for `|a|`.
decls.statement:

    (hx2 : x ^ 2 = algebraMap ℤ K a) (hx : x ∉ (algebraMap ℚ K).range)
    (hA : a.natAbs ≤ A) :
    NumberField.classNumber K ≤ 64 * A

decls.name: TauCeti.NumberField.abs_discr_le_of_basis_isIntegral
decls.doc:
If `b` is a `ℚ`-basis of a number field `K` consisting of algebraic integers, then
`|d_K| ≤ |disc b|`.
decls.statement:
theorem abs_discr_le_of_basis_isIntegral {K : Type*} [Field K] [NumberField K]
    {ι : Type*} [Fintype ι] [DecidableEq ι] (b : Module.Basis ι ℚ K)
    (hb : ∀ i, IsIntegral ℤ (b i)) :
    |(NumberField.discr K : ℚ)| ≤ |Algebra.discr ℚ (b : ι → K)|

decls.name: TauCeti.NumberField.abs_discr_le_of_basis_isIntegral_of_abs_discr_le
decls.doc:
If the discriminant of an algebraic-integer basis is bounded by `B`, then the number-field
discriminant is bounded by the same rational number.
decls.statement:
theorem abs_discr_le_of_basis_isIntegral_of_abs_discr_le {K : Type*} [Field K] [NumberField K]
    {ι : Type*} [Fintype ι] [DecidableEq ι] (b : Module.Basis ι ℚ K)
    (hb : ∀ i, IsIntegral ℤ (b i)) {B : ℚ}
    (hB : |Algebra.discr ℚ (b : ι → K)| ≤ B) :
    |(NumberField.discr K : ℚ)| ≤ B

decls.name: TauCeti.NumberField.natAbs_discr_le_of_basis_isIntegral_of_discr_eq_int
decls.doc:
If the trace-form discriminant of an algebraic-integer basis computes to the integer `d`, then
the natural absolute discriminant of the number field is at most `d.natAbs`.
decls.statement:
theorem natAbs_discr_le_of_basis_isIntegral_of_discr_eq_int {K : Type*} [Field K] [NumberField K]
    {ι : Type*} [Fintype ι] [DecidableEq ι] (b : Module.Basis ι ℚ K)
    (hb : ∀ i, IsIntegral ℤ (b i)) {d : ℤ}
    (hdisc : Algebra.discr ℚ (b : ι → K) = (d : ℚ)) :
    (NumberField.discr K).natAbs ≤ d.natAbs

decls.name: TauCeti.NumberField.natAbs_discr_le_of_basis_isIntegral_of_discr_eq_int_of_natAbs_le
decls.doc:
If the trace-form discriminant of an algebraic-integer basis computes to the integer `d`, and
`d.natAbs ≤ D`, then `(NumberField.discr K).natAbs ≤ D`.
decls.statement:
theorem natAbs_discr_le_of_basis_isIntegral_of_discr_eq_int_of_natAbs_le
    {K : Type*} [Field K] [NumberField K] {ι : Type*} [Fintype ι] [DecidableEq ι]
    (b : Module.Basis ι ℚ K) (hb : ∀ i, IsIntegral ℤ (b i)) {d : ℤ} {D : ℕ}
    (hdisc : Algebra.discr ℚ (b : ι → K) = (d : ℚ)) (hd : d.natAbs ≤ D) :
    (NumberField.discr K).natAbs ≤ D

decls.name: TauCeti.NumberField.natAbs_discr_le_of_basis_isIntegral_of_discr_eq_nat
decls.doc:
If the trace-form discriminant of an algebraic-integer basis computes to the natural number
`D`, then `(NumberField.discr K).natAbs ≤ D`.
decls.statement:
theorem natAbs_discr_le_of_basis_isIntegral_of_discr_eq_nat
    {K : Type*} [Field K] [NumberField K] {ι : Type*} [Fintype ι] [DecidableEq ι]
    (b : Module.Basis ι ℚ K) (hb : ∀ i, IsIntegral ℤ (b i)) {D : ℕ}
    (hdisc : Algebra.discr ℚ (b : ι → K) = (D : ℚ)) :
    (NumberField.discr K).natAbs ≤ D

decls.name: TauCeti.NumberField.abs_discr_le_int_of_basis_isIntegral_of_discr_eq_int_of_natAbs_le
decls.doc:
If the trace-form discriminant of an algebraic-integer basis computes to an integer `d` with
`d.natAbs ≤ D`, the same natural-number discriminant bound may be read as an integer absolute-value
bound.
decls.statement:
theorem abs_discr_le_int_of_basis_isIntegral_of_discr_eq_int_of_natAbs_le
    {K : Type*} [Field K] [NumberField K] {ι : Type*} [Fintype ι] [DecidableEq ι]
    (b : Module.Basis ι ℚ K) (hb : ∀ i, IsIntegral ℤ (b i)) {d : ℤ} {D : ℕ}
    (hdisc : Algebra.discr ℚ (b : ι → K) = (d : ℚ)) (hd : d.natAbs ≤ D) :
    |NumberField.discr K| ≤ (D : ℤ)

decls.name: TauCeti.NumberField.abs_discr_le_of_sq_intCast
decls.doc:
For a quadratic number field `K` and an element `x : K` whose square is an integer
`a` and which is not rational, the field discriminant satisfies `|d_K| ≤ 4·|a|`.
decls.statement:
theorem abs_discr_le_of_sq_intCast {K : Type*} [Field K] [NumberField K]
    {x : K} {a : ℤ} (hfin : finrank ℚ K = 2)
    (hx2 : x ^ 2 = algebraMap ℤ K a) (hx : x ∉ (algebraMap ℚ K).range) :
    |(NumberField.discr K : ℚ)| ≤ 4 * |(a : ℚ)|

decls.name: TauCeti.NumberField.abs_discr_le_int_of_sq_intCast
decls.doc:
The integer form of the quadratic discriminant bound: `|d_K| ≤ 4·|a|` over `ℤ`, for a
quadratic field `K` with `x² = a ∈ ℤ` and `x ∉ ℚ`.
decls.statement:
theorem abs_discr_le_int_of_sq_intCast {K : Type*} [Field K] [NumberField K]
    {x : K} {a : ℤ} (hfin : finrank ℚ K = 2)
    (hx2 : x ^ 2 = algebraMap ℤ K a) (hx : x ∉ (algebraMap ℚ K).range) :
    |NumberField.discr K| ≤ 4 * |a|

decls.name: TauCeti.NumberField.discr_eq_of_integralBasis
decls.doc:
**An integral basis attains the discriminant bound.** For a `ℤ`-basis `c` of the ring of
integers `𝒪_K`, the rational discriminant of the induced `ℚ`-basis of `K` is exactly the field
discriminant `d_K`.
decls.title: An integral basis attains the discriminant bound
decls.statement:
theorem discr_eq_of_integralBasis (c : Basis ι ℤ (𝓞 K)) :
    Algebra.discr ℚ (fun i => algebraMap (𝓞 K) K (c i)) = (NumberField.discr K : ℚ)

decls.name: TauCeti.NumberField.discr_eq_of_basis_isIntegral_of_span_eq_top
decls.doc:
**The discriminant bound is an equality for a spanning integral basis.** If `b` is a
`ℚ`-basis of `K` consisting of algebraic integers whose `ℤ`-span inside `𝒪_K` is all of `𝒪_K`,
then `disc b = d_K` exactly (over `ℚ`).
decls.title: The discriminant bound is an equality for a spanning integral basis
decls.statement:
theorem discr_eq_of_basis_isIntegral_of_span_eq_top
    (b : Basis ι ℚ K) (hb : ∀ i, IsIntegral ℤ (b i))
    (hspan : Submodule.span ℤ (Set.range fun i => (⟨b i, hb i⟩ : 𝓞 K)) = ⊤) :
    Algebra.discr ℚ (b : ι → K) = (NumberField.discr K : ℚ)

decls.name: TauCeti.NumberField.abs_discr_eq_of_basis_isIntegral_of_span_eq_top
decls.doc:
**The equality companion of the effective discriminant bound.** For a `ℚ`-basis of algebraic
integers that generates `𝒪_K`, the effective bound `|d_K| ≤ |disc b|` is an equality.
decls.title: The equality companion of the effective discriminant bound
decls.statement:
theorem abs_discr_eq_of_basis_isIntegral_of_span_eq_top
    (b : Basis ι ℚ K) (hb : ∀ i, IsIntegral ℤ (b i))
    (hspan : Submodule.span ℤ (Set.range fun i => (⟨b i, hb i⟩ : 𝓞 K)) = ⊤) :
    |(NumberField.discr K : ℚ)| = |Algebra.discr ℚ (b : ι → K)|

decls.name: TauCeti.NumberField.discr_eq_of_basis_isIntegral_of_span_eq_top_of_discr_eq_int
decls.doc:
**Evaluating the discriminant through a spanning integral basis.** If the discriminant of a
generating basis of algebraic integers computes to an integer `d`, then `d_K = d` exactly. This is
the consumer form used to read off `d_K` from a concrete trace-form computation, as in the
roadmap's `ℚ(i)` example (`disc {1, i} = -4`, whence `d_{ℚ(i)} = -4`).
decls.title: Evaluating the discriminant through a spanning integral basis
decls.statement:
theorem discr_eq_of_basis_isIntegral_of_span_eq_top_of_discr_eq_int
    (b : Basis ι ℚ K) (hb : ∀ i, IsIntegral ℤ (b i))
    (hspan : Submodule.span ℤ (Set.range fun i => (⟨b i, hb i⟩ : 𝓞 K)) = ⊤)
    {d : ℤ} (hd : Algebra.discr ℚ (b : ι → K) = (d : ℚ)) :
    NumberField.discr K = d

decls.name: TauCeti.NumberField.natAbs_discr_eq_of_basis_isIntegral_of_span_eq_top_of_discr_eq_int
decls.doc:
**The absolute value of the discriminant from a spanning integral basis.** The `natAbs`
corollary of `discr_eq_of_basis_isIntegral_of_span_eq_top_of_discr_eq_int`, reading off `|d_K|`
from an evaluated integer basis discriminant (in the `ℚ(i)` example, `(d_{ℚ(i)}).natAbs = 4`).
decls.title: The absolute value of the discriminant from a spanning integral basis
decls.statement:
theorem natAbs_discr_eq_of_basis_isIntegral_of_span_eq_top_of_discr_eq_int
    (b : Basis ι ℚ K) (hb : ∀ i, IsIntegral ℤ (b i))
    (hspan : Submodule.span ℤ (Set.range fun i => (⟨b i, hb i⟩ : 𝓞 K)) = ⊤)
    {d : ℤ} (hd : Algebra.discr ℚ (b : ι → K) = (d : ℚ)) :
    (NumberField.discr K).natAbs = d.natAbs

decls.name: TauCeti.NumberField.coeffBoundOfDiscrBdd
decls.doc:
An explicit height bound for the integer minimal polynomial of a primitive generator of a number
field of discriminant `≤ N`. It is `⌈M ^ D * (D.choose (D / 2))⌉₊` where `D = rankOfDiscrBdd N` is
Mathlib's degree bound and `M = max √(1 + boundOfDiscBdd N ^ 2) 1` dominates the per-conjugate bound
of both the real and complex primitive elements of `finite_of_discr_bdd`.
decls.statement: def coeffBoundOfDiscrBdd (N : ℕ) : ℕ

decls.name: TauCeti.NumberField.exists_primitive_element_infinitePlace_le
decls.doc:
**Effective Hermite--Minkowski, generating element.** A number field `K` with `|discr K| ≤ N`
has a primitive integral generator `a` all of whose infinite places are at most
`max √(1 + boundOfDiscBdd N ^ 2) 1`.
decls.title: Effective Hermite--Minkowski, generating element
decls.statement:
theorem exists_primitive_element_infinitePlace_le {K : Type*} [Field K] [NumberField K]
    {N : ℕ} (hK : |discr K| ≤ (N : ℤ)) :
    ∃ a : 𝓞 K, ℚ⟮(a : K)⟯ = ⊤ ∧
      ∀ w : InfinitePlace K, w (a : K) ≤ max (Real.sqrt (1 + (boundOfDiscBdd N : ℝ) ^ 2)) 1

decls.name: TauCeti.NumberField.abs_coeff_minpoly_le_coeffBoundOfDiscrBdd
decls.doc:
The `ℤ`-minimal polynomial of an algebraic integer `a` of a number field `K` with
`finrank ℚ K ≤ rankOfDiscrBdd N`, all of whose conjugates have norm at most
`max √(1 + boundOfDiscBdd N ^ 2) 1`, has every coefficient bounded in absolute value by
`coeffBoundOfDiscrBdd N`.
decls.statement:
theorem abs_coeff_minpoly_le_coeffBoundOfDiscrBdd {K : Type*} [Field K] [NumberField K]
    {N : ℕ} {a : 𝓞 K} (hrank : finrank ℚ K ≤ rankOfDiscrBdd N)
    (hnorm : ∀ φ : K →+* ℂ, ‖φ (a : K)‖ ≤ max (Real.sqrt (1 + (boundOfDiscBdd N : ℝ) ^ 2)) 1)
    (i : ℕ) : |(minpoly ℤ (a : K)).coeff i| ≤ (coeffBoundOfDiscrBdd N : ℤ)

decls.name: TauCeti.NumberField.exists_mem_rootSet_eq_adjoin_of_abs_discr_le
decls.doc:
**Effective Hermite--Minkowski, generating step.** Each number field `K` (a finite extension of
`ℚ` inside `A`) with `|discr K| ≤ N` is generated over `ℚ` by a root in `A` of an integer polynomial
of degree at most `rankOfDiscrBdd N` and all coefficients of absolute value at most
`coeffBoundOfDiscrBdd N`. This is `NumberField.hermiteTheorem.finite_of_discr_bdd` recast to expose
its explicit generating set.
decls.title: Effective Hermite--Minkowski, generating step
decls.statement:
theorem exists_mem_rootSet_eq_adjoin_of_abs_discr_le [DecidableEq A] {N : ℕ}
    (K : IntermediateField ℚ A) (hK₀ : FiniteDimensional ℚ K)
    (hK : haveI : _root_.NumberField K := @NumberField.mk _ _ inferInstance hK₀
      |discr K| ≤ (N : ℤ)) :
    ∃ x ∈ (⋃ (f : ℤ[X]) (_ : f.natDegree ≤ rankOfDiscrBdd N ∧
        ∀ i, |f.coeff i| ≤ (coeffBoundOfDiscrBdd N : ℤ)),
        ((f.map (algebraMap ℤ A)).roots.toFinset : Set A)),
      (K : IntermediateField ℚ A) = ℚ⟮x⟯

decls.name: TauCeti.NumberField.ncard_setOf_finiteDimensional_abs_discr_le_le
decls.doc:
**Effective Hermite--Minkowski.** Inside a fixed extension `A / ℚ`, the number of number fields
`K` (finite extensions of `ℚ`) with `|discr K| ≤ N` is at most
`(2 * coeffBoundOfDiscrBdd N + 1) ^ (rankOfDiscrBdd N + 1) * rankOfDiscrBdd N`, an explicit function
of `N` alone. This upgrades Mathlib's `NumberField.finite_of_discr_bdd` from finiteness to an
explicit count.
decls.title: Effective Hermite--Minkowski
decls.statement:
theorem ncard_setOf_finiteDimensional_abs_discr_le_le :
    {K : {F : IntermediateField ℚ A // FiniteDimensional ℚ F} |
        haveI : _root_.NumberField K := @NumberField.mk _ _ inferInstance K.prop
        |discr K| ≤ (N : ℤ)}.ncard ≤
      (2 * coeffBoundOfDiscrBdd N + 1) ^ (rankOfDiscrBdd N + 1) * rankOfDiscrBdd N

decls.name: TauCeti.NumberField.hermiteCountBound
decls.doc:
The elementary polynomial count appearing in effective Hermite--Minkowski: if every field is
generated by a root of an integer polynomial of degree at most `D` and coefficient height at most
`C`, then the number of possible generated fields is bounded by
`(2 * C + 1) ^ (D + 1) * D`.
decls.statement: def hermiteCountBound (D C : ℕ) : ℕ

decls.name: TauCeti.NumberField.hermiteCountBound_def
decls.statement:
theorem hermiteCountBound_def (D C : ℕ) :
    hermiteCountBound D C = (2 * C + 1) ^ (D + 1) * D

decls.name: TauCeti.NumberField.hermiteCountBound_zero_left
decls.statement: theorem hermiteCountBound_zero_left (C : ℕ) : hermiteCountBound 0 C = 0

decls.name: TauCeti.NumberField.hermiteCountBound_zero_right
decls.statement: theorem hermiteCountBound_zero_right (D : ℕ) : hermiteCountBound D 0 = D

decls.name: TauCeti.NumberField.hermiteCountBound_mono
decls.doc:
The Hermite-count expression is monotone in the degree bound and the coefficient-height
bound.
decls.statement:
theorem hermiteCountBound_mono {D₁ D₂ C₁ C₂ : ℕ} (hD : D₁ ≤ D₂) (hC : C₁ ≤ C₂) :
    hermiteCountBound D₁ C₁ ≤ hermiteCountBound D₂ C₂

decls.name: TauCeti.NumberField.ncard_setOf_finiteDimensional_abs_discr_le_le_hermiteCountBound
decls.doc:
The effective Hermite--Minkowski count with the exact constants packaged as
`hermiteCountBound`.
decls.statement:
theorem ncard_setOf_finiteDimensional_abs_discr_le_le_hermiteCountBound (N : ℕ) :
    {K : {F : IntermediateField ℚ A // FiniteDimensional ℚ F} |
        haveI : _root_.NumberField K := @NumberField.mk _ _ inferInstance K.prop
        |discr K| ≤ (N : ℤ)}.ncard ≤
      hermiteCountBound (rankOfDiscrBdd N) (coeffBoundOfDiscrBdd N)

decls.name: TauCeti.NumberField.ncard_setOf_finiteDimensional_abs_discr_le_le_of_bounds
decls.doc:
**Monotone effective Hermite--Minkowski.** If `D` and `C` are any explicit bounds above
Mathlib's degree bound `rankOfDiscrBdd N` and the coefficient bound `coeffBoundOfDiscrBdd N`, then
the number of finite-dimensional subfields of an ambient extension `A / ℚ` with discriminant at
most `N` is bounded by `(2 * C + 1) ^ (D + 1) * D`.

This is the usable form for later explicit estimates, where `D` and `C` are often replaced by
simpler closed-form upper bounds.
decls.title: Monotone effective Hermite--Minkowski
decls.statement:
theorem ncard_setOf_finiteDimensional_abs_discr_le_le_of_bounds (N D C : ℕ)
    (hD : rankOfDiscrBdd N ≤ D) (hC : coeffBoundOfDiscrBdd N ≤ C) :
    {K : {F : IntermediateField ℚ A // FiniteDimensional ℚ F} |
        haveI : _root_.NumberField K := @NumberField.mk _ _ inferInstance K.prop
        |discr K| ≤ (N : ℤ)}.ncard ≤
      hermiteCountBound D C

decls.name: TauCeti.NumberField.setOf_finiteDimensional_abs_discr_le_subset_of_le
decls.doc:
The bounded-discriminant subfields at threshold `N` form a subset of those at threshold `M`
whenever `N ≤ M`.
decls.statement:
theorem setOf_finiteDimensional_abs_discr_le_subset_of_le {N M : ℕ} (hNM : N ≤ M) :
    {K : {F : IntermediateField ℚ A // FiniteDimensional ℚ F} |
        haveI : _root_.NumberField K := @NumberField.mk _ _ inferInstance K.prop
        |discr K| ≤ (N : ℤ)} ⊆
      {K : {F : IntermediateField ℚ A // FiniteDimensional ℚ F} |
        haveI : _root_.NumberField K := @NumberField.mk _ _ inferInstance K.prop
        |discr K| ≤ (M : ℤ)}

decls.name: TauCeti.NumberField.ncard_setOf_finiteDimensional_abs_discr_le_le_of_threshold_le
decls.doc:
**Threshold-monotone effective Hermite--Minkowski.** If `N ≤ M`, then the number of
finite-dimensional subfields of an ambient extension `A / ℚ` with absolute discriminant at most `N`
is bounded by the explicit Hermite-count expression attached to the larger threshold `M`.
decls.title: Threshold-monotone effective Hermite--Minkowski
decls.statement:
theorem ncard_setOf_finiteDimensional_abs_discr_le_le_of_threshold_le {N M : ℕ}
    (hNM : N ≤ M) :
    {K : {F : IntermediateField ℚ A // FiniteDimensional ℚ F} |
        haveI : _root_.NumberField K := @NumberField.mk _ _ inferInstance K.prop
        |discr K| ≤ (N : ℤ)}.ncard ≤
      hermiteCountBound (rankOfDiscrBdd M) (coeffBoundOfDiscrBdd M)

decls.name: TauCeti.NumberField.ncard_setOf_finiteDimensional_abs_discr_le_le_of_threshold_bounds
decls.doc:
**Threshold-monotone effective Hermite--Minkowski with coarser constants.** If `N ≤ M`, and
`D` and `C` bound the degree and coefficient-height constants attached to `M`, then the number of
finite-dimensional subfields of an ambient extension `A / ℚ` with absolute discriminant at most `N`
is at most `hermiteCountBound D C`.
decls.title: Threshold-monotone effective Hermite--Minkowski with coarser constants
decls.statement:
theorem ncard_setOf_finiteDimensional_abs_discr_le_le_of_threshold_bounds {N M D C : ℕ}
    (hNM : N ≤ M) (hD : rankOfDiscrBdd M ≤ D) (hC : coeffBoundOfDiscrBdd M ≤ C) :
    {K : {F : IntermediateField ℚ A // FiniteDimensional ℚ F} |
        haveI : _root_.NumberField K := @NumberField.mk _ _ inferInstance K.prop
        |discr K| ≤ (N : ℤ)}.ncard ≤ hermiteCountBound D C

decls.name: TauCeti.NumberField.setOf_finiteDimensional_natAbs_discr_le_subset_abs_discr_le
decls.doc:
The subfields whose discriminant has natural absolute value at most `N` are contained in the
integer-absolute-value family used by Mathlib's Hermite theorem.
decls.statement:
theorem setOf_finiteDimensional_natAbs_discr_le_subset_abs_discr_le (N : ℕ) :
    {K : {F : IntermediateField ℚ A // FiniteDimensional ℚ F} |
        haveI : _root_.NumberField K := @NumberField.mk _ _ inferInstance K.prop
        (discr K).natAbs ≤ N} ⊆
      {K : {F : IntermediateField ℚ A // FiniteDimensional ℚ F} |
        haveI : _root_.NumberField K := @NumberField.mk _ _ inferInstance K.prop
        |discr K| ≤ (N : ℤ)}

decls.name: TauCeti.NumberField.ncard_setOf_finiteDimensional_natAbs_discr_le_le_of_threshold_le
decls.doc:
**Threshold-monotone effective Hermite--Minkowski, natural-discriminant form.** If `N ≤ M`,

decls.title: Threshold-monotone effective Hermite--Minkowski, natural-discriminant form
decls.statement:
theorem ncard_setOf_finiteDimensional_natAbs_discr_le_le_of_threshold_le {N M : ℕ}

        (discr K).natAbs ≤ N}.ncard ≤
      hermiteCountBound (rankOfDiscrBdd M) (coeffBoundOfDiscrBdd M)

decls.name: TauCeti.NumberField.ncard_setOf_finiteDimensional_natAbs_discr_le_le_hermiteCountBound
decls.doc:
**Effective Hermite--Minkowski, natural-discriminant form.** Inside a fixed extension

decls.title: Effective Hermite--Minkowski, natural-discriminant form
decls.statement:
theorem ncard_setOf_finiteDimensional_natAbs_discr_le_le_hermiteCountBound (N : ℕ) :
    {K : {F : IntermediateField ℚ A // FiniteDimensional ℚ F} |

decls.name: TauCeti.NumberField.ncard_setOf_finiteDimensional_natAbs_discr_le_le_of_threshold_bounds
decls.doc:
**Threshold-monotone effective Hermite--Minkowski with coarser constants,
natural-discriminant form.** If `N ≤ M`, and `D` and `C` bound the degree and coefficient-height
constants attached to `M`, then the number of finite-dimensional subfields of an ambient extension

decls.statement:
theorem ncard_setOf_finiteDimensional_natAbs_discr_le_le_of_threshold_bounds {N M D C : ℕ}
    (hNM : N ≤ M) (hD : rankOfDiscrBdd M ≤ D) (hC : coeffBoundOfDiscrBdd M ≤ C) :

decls.doc:
**Monotone effective Hermite--Minkowski, natural-discriminant form.** If `D` and `C` bound the

decls.title: Monotone effective Hermite--Minkowski, natural-discriminant form
decls.statement:
theorem ncard_setOf_finiteDimensional_natAbs_discr_le_le_of_bounds (N D C : ℕ)

decls.name: TauCeti.NumberField.prodLeTuples
decls.doc: The set of `n`-tuples of positive naturals with real product at most `X`.
decls.statement: def prodLeTuples (n : ℕ) (X : ℝ) : Set (Fin n → ℕ)

decls.name: TauCeti.NumberField.mem_prodLeTuples
decls.statement:
theorem mem_prodLeTuples {n : ℕ} {X : ℝ} {d : Fin n → ℕ} :
    d ∈ prodLeTuples n X ↔ (∀ i, 0 < d i) ∧ (∏ i, (d i : ℝ)) ≤ X

decls.name: TauCeti.NumberField.prodLeTuples_finite
decls.doc: The tuple set is finite: every coordinate lies in `[1, ⌊X⌋]`.
decls.statement: theorem prodLeTuples_finite (n : ℕ) (X : ℝ) : (prodLeTuples n X).Finite

decls.name: TauCeti.NumberField.sum_one_div_sq_le_two
decls.doc: `∑_{j=1}^{N} 1/j² ≤ 2`, from the Basel sum `π²/6 < 2`.
decls.statement:
theorem sum_one_div_sq_le_two (N : ℕ) :
    ∑ j ∈ Finset.Icc 1 N, (1 : ℝ) / (j : ℝ) ^ 2 ≤ 2

decls.name: TauCeti.NumberField.prodLeTuples_succ_eq_iUnion
decls.doc:
Splitting off the last coordinate `j`, which ranges over `{1, …, ⌊X⌋}`: an `(n+1)`-tuple
with product at most `X` is an `n`-tuple with product at most `X / j` followed by `j`.
decls.statement:
theorem prodLeTuples_succ_eq_iUnion (n : ℕ) (X : ℝ) :
    prodLeTuples (n + 1) X = ⋃ j ∈ Finset.Icc 1 ⌊X⌋₊,
      (fun e => Fin.snoc e j) '' (prodLeTuples n (X / j))

decls.name: TauCeti.NumberField.prodLeTuples_succ_ncard_le
decls.doc:
The number of `(n+1)`-tuples with product at most `X` is at most the sum, over the last
coordinate `j ∈ {1, …, ⌊X⌋}`, of the counts of `n`-tuples with product at most `X / j`.
decls.statement:
theorem prodLeTuples_succ_ncard_le (n : ℕ) (X : ℝ) :
    (prodLeTuples (n + 1) X).ncard ≤
      ∑ j ∈ Finset.Icc 1 ⌊X⌋₊, (prodLeTuples n (X / j)).ncard

decls.name: TauCeti.NumberField.prodLeTuples_ncard_le
decls.doc:
The number of positive `n`-tuples of natural numbers whose real product is at most `X` is
at most `X² * 2ⁿ`, for `X ≥ 1`.
decls.statement:
theorem prodLeTuples_ncard_le (n : ℕ) {X : ℝ} (hX : 1 ≤ X) :
    ((prodLeTuples n X).ncard : ℝ) ≤ X ^ 2 * 2 ^ n

decls.name: TauCeti.NumberField.absNormUnder
decls.doc: The norm of the rational prime below a prime ideal `P` of `𝓞 F`.
decls.statement: def absNormUnder (P : Ideal (𝓞 F)) : ℕ

decls.name: TauCeti.NumberField.primeCoord
decls.doc:
The coordinate (index in `Fin [F:ℚ]`) assigned to a prime ideal `P`: its
position in the list of primes above the rational prime below `P`.
decls.statement: def primeCoord (P : Ideal (𝓞 F)) : ℕ

decls.name: TauCeti.NumberField.encodeIdeal
decls.doc: The `i`-th coordinate of the tuple encoding the ideal `I`.
decls.statement: def encodeIdeal (I : Ideal (𝓞 F)) (i : Fin (Module.finrank ℚ F)) : ℕ

decls.name: TauCeti.NumberField.mem_primesOverFinset_under
decls.statement:
theorem mem_primesOverFinset_under {P : Ideal (𝓞 F)} (hP : P.IsPrime) (hP0 : P ≠ ⊥) :
    P ∈ IsDedekindDomain.primesOverFinset (Ideal.under ℤ P) (𝓞 F)

decls.name: TauCeti.NumberField.primeCoord_lt
decls.statement:
theorem primeCoord_lt {P : Ideal (𝓞 F)} (hP : P.IsPrime) (hP0 : P ≠ ⊥) :
    primeCoord F P < Module.finrank ℚ F

decls.name: TauCeti.NumberField.under_eq_of_absNormUnder_eq
TauCeti.NumberField.prime_eq_of_absNormUnder_eq_of_primeCoord_eq
decls.statement:
theorem prime_eq_of_absNormUnder_eq_of_primeCoord_eq {P Q : Ideal (𝓞 F)}
    (hP : P.IsPrime) (hP0 : P ≠ ⊥) (hQ : Q.IsPrime) (hQ0 : Q ≠ ⊥)
    (hr : absNormUnder F P = absNormUnder F Q)
    (hc : primeCoord F P = primeCoord F Q) : P = Q

decls.name: TauCeti.NumberField.encodeIdeal_pos
decls.statement:
theorem encodeIdeal_pos {I : Ideal (𝓞 F)}
    (i : Fin (Module.finrank ℚ F)) : 0 < encodeIdeal F I i

decls.name: TauCeti.NumberField.prod_encodeIdeal_eq
decls.statement:
theorem prod_encodeIdeal_eq {I : Ideal (𝓞 F)} :
    ∏ i, encodeIdeal F I i =
      ∏ P ∈ (normalizedFactors I).toFinset,
        (absNormUnder F P) ^ ((normalizedFactors I).count P)

decls.name: TauCeti.NumberField.prod_encodeIdeal_le_absNorm
decls.statement:
theorem prod_encodeIdeal_le_absNorm {I : Ideal (𝓞 F)} (hI : I ≠ ⊥) :
    ∏ i, encodeIdeal F I i ≤ Ideal.absNorm I

decls.name: TauCeti.NumberField.count_eq_padicValNat
decls.statement:
theorem count_eq_padicValNat {I : Ideal (𝓞 F)} {P : Ideal (𝓞 F)}
    (hP : P.IsPrime) (hP0 : P ≠ ⊥) :
    (normalizedFactors I).count P =
      padicValNat (absNormUnder F P)
        (encodeIdeal F I ⟨primeCoord F P, primeCoord_lt F hP hP0⟩)

decls.name: TauCeti.NumberField.encodeIdeal_injOn
decls.statement:
theorem encodeIdeal_injOn :
    Set.InjOn (encodeIdeal F) {I : Ideal (𝓞 F) | I ≠ ⊥}

decls.name: TauCeti.NumberField.ideal_ncard_le_prodLeTuples_ncard
decls.doc:
The nonzero integral ideals of norm at most `X` inject into the positive
`[F:ℚ]`-tuples whose product is at most `X`. The encoding assigns each prime ideal `P`
one coordinate and contributes `absNorm (Ideal.under ℤ P) ^ count` there; the coordinate
product is bounded by `Ideal.absNorm I`, and injectivity follows by recovering each count
from a `padicValNat`.
decls.statement:
theorem ideal_ncard_le_prodLeTuples_ncard (F : Type*) [Field F] [NumberField F]
    {X : ℝ} :
    {I : Ideal (𝓞 F) | I ≠ ⊥ ∧ (Ideal.absNorm I : ℝ) ≤ X}.ncard ≤
      (prodLeTuples (Module.finrank ℚ F) X).ncard

decls.name: TauCeti.NumberField.card_ideal_absNorm_le
decls.doc:
In any number field `F`, the set of nonzero integral ideals with norm at most `X` is
finite, and for `X ≥ 1` its cardinality is at most `X² * 2^[F:ℚ]`.
decls.statement:
theorem card_ideal_absNorm_le (F : Type*) [Field F] [NumberField F]
    {X : ℝ} (hX : 1 ≤ X) :
    {I : Ideal (𝓞 F) | I ≠ ⊥ ∧ (Ideal.absNorm I : ℝ) ≤ X}.Finite ∧
      (({I : Ideal (𝓞 F) | I ≠ ⊥ ∧ (Ideal.absNorm I : ℝ) ≤ X}.ncard : ℝ)) ≤
        X ^ 2 * 2 ^ Module.finrank ℚ F

decls.name: TauCeti.NumberField.idealsWithAbsNormNatLe
decls.doc: The set of nonzero integral ideals of `𝓞 F` with natural norm at most `N`.
decls.statement:
abbrev idealsWithAbsNormNatLe (F : Type*) [Field F] [NumberField F] (N : ℕ) :
    Set (Ideal (𝓞 F))

decls.name: TauCeti.NumberField.idealsWithAbsNormRealLe
decls.doc: The set of nonzero integral ideals of `𝓞 F` with real norm at most `X`.
decls.statement:
abbrev idealsWithAbsNormRealLe (F : Type*) [Field F] [NumberField F] (X : ℝ) :
    Set (Ideal (𝓞 F))

decls.name: TauCeti.NumberField.idealsWithAbsNormNatLe_finite
decls.statement:
theorem idealsWithAbsNormNatLe_finite (F : Type*) [Field F] [NumberField F] (N : ℕ) :
    (idealsWithAbsNormNatLe F N).Finite

decls.name: TauCeti.NumberField.idealsWithAbsNormNatLe_eq_real
decls.statement:
theorem idealsWithAbsNormNatLe_eq_real (F : Type*) [Field F] [NumberField F] (N : ℕ) :
    idealsWithAbsNormNatLe F N = idealsWithAbsNormRealLe F (N : ℝ)

decls.name: TauCeti.NumberField.idealsWithAbsNormNatLe_zero
decls.statement:
theorem idealsWithAbsNormNatLe_zero (F : Type*) [Field F] [NumberField F] :
    idealsWithAbsNormNatLe F 0 = ∅

decls.name: TauCeti.NumberField.ncard_idealsWithAbsNormNatLe_real_le
decls.statement:
theorem ncard_idealsWithAbsNormNatLe_real_le (F : Type*) [Field F] [NumberField F]
    {N : ℕ} (hN : (1 : ℝ) ≤ N) :
    ((idealsWithAbsNormNatLe F N).ncard : ℝ) ≤ (N : ℝ) ^ 2 * 2 ^ finrank ℚ F

decls.name: TauCeti.NumberField.ncard_ideal_absNorm_le_nat
decls.doc:
**Natural-number ideal count.** The number of nonzero integral ideals of `𝓞 F` with norm at
most `N` is at most `N² * 2^[F:ℚ]`.
decls.title: Natural-number ideal count
decls.statement:
theorem ncard_ideal_absNorm_le_nat (F : Type*) [Field F] [NumberField F]
    (N : ℕ) :
    {I : Ideal (𝓞 F) | I ≠ ⊥ ∧ Ideal.absNorm I ≤ N}.ncard ≤
      N ^ 2 * 2 ^ finrank ℚ F

decls.name: TauCeti.NumberField.ncard_ideal_absNorm_le_of_finrank_le
decls.doc:
If `1 ≤ X` and `[F : ℚ] ≤ n`, then the number of nonzero integral ideals of norm at most
`X` is at most `X² * 2^n`. This is the degree-monotone form of
`TauCeti.NumberField.card_ideal_absNorm_le`.
decls.statement:
theorem ncard_ideal_absNorm_le_of_finrank_le (F : Type*) [Field F] [NumberField F]
    {X : ℝ} {n : ℕ} (hX : 1 ≤ X) (hn : finrank ℚ F ≤ n) :
    (({I : Ideal (𝓞 F) | I ≠ ⊥ ∧ (Ideal.absNorm I : ℝ) ≤ X}.ncard : ℝ)) ≤
      X ^ 2 * 2 ^ n

decls.name: TauCeti.NumberField.ncard_ideal_absNorm_le_of_nat_le_of_finrank_le
decls.doc:
Monotone natural-number ideal count: if all ideals under consideration have norm at most
`N`, and `N ≤ B`, and `[F : ℚ] ≤ n`, then there are at most `B² * 2^n` of them.
decls.statement:
theorem ncard_ideal_absNorm_le_of_nat_le_of_finrank_le
    (F : Type*) [Field F] [NumberField F] {N B n : ℕ}
    (hN : N ≤ B) (hn : finrank ℚ F ≤ n) :
    {I : Ideal (𝓞 F) | I ≠ ⊥ ∧ Ideal.absNorm I ≤ N}.ncard ≤ B ^ 2 * 2 ^ n

decls.name: TauCeti.NumberField.ncard_ideal_absNorm_le_nat_of_finrank_le
decls.doc:
If `[F : ℚ] ≤ n`, then the number of nonzero integral ideals of norm at most `N` is at most
`N² * 2^n`.
decls.statement:
theorem ncard_ideal_absNorm_le_nat_of_finrank_le
    (F : Type*) [Field F] [NumberField F] {N n : ℕ}
    (hn : finrank ℚ F ≤ n) :
    {I : Ideal (𝓞 F) | I ≠ ⊥ ∧ Ideal.absNorm I ≤ N}.ncard ≤ N ^ 2 * 2 ^ n

decls.name: TauCeti.NumberField.Units.regulator_eq_one_of_rank_eq_zero
decls.doc:
**The regulator of a number field of unit rank zero is `1`.** When the unit rank is zero,
the unit lattice sits inside the zero-dimensional log space, and the regulator — its covolume,
computed by `NumberField.Units.regulator_eq_det'` as a determinant indexed by the infinite
places other than the distinguished one — is the determinant of the empty matrix, `1`.
decls.title: The regulator of a number field of unit rank zero is `1`
decls.statement: theorem regulator_eq_one_of_rank_eq_zero (h : rank K = 0) : regulator K = 1

decls.name: TauCeti.NumberField.Units.rank_eq_zero_of_card_infinitePlace_le_one
decls.doc:
A number field with at most one infinite place has unit rank zero. This covers `ℚ` (one real
place) and the imaginary quadratic fields (one complex place), and is stated in the monotone
form consumed by effective lower-bound arguments.
decls.statement:
theorem rank_eq_zero_of_card_infinitePlace_le_one
    (h : Fintype.card (InfinitePlace K) ≤ 1) : rank K = 0

decls.name: TauCeti.NumberField.Units.rank_eq_zero_of_card_infinitePlace_eq_one
decls.doc: A number field with a single infinite place has unit rank zero.
decls.statement:
theorem rank_eq_zero_of_card_infinitePlace_eq_one
    (h : Fintype.card (InfinitePlace K) = 1) : rank K = 0

decls.name: TauCeti.IntermediateField.finite_boundedRoots
decls.doc:
The root set in `A` of the integer polynomials of degree at most `d` whose coefficients all have
absolute value at most `B` is finite.
decls.statement:
theorem finite_boundedRoots (d B : ℕ) :
    (⋃ (f : ℤ[X]) (_ : f.natDegree ≤ d ∧ ∀ i, |f.coeff i| ≤ (B : ℤ)),
        (((f.map (algebraMap ℤ A)).roots.toFinset : Set A))).Finite

decls.name: TauCeti.IntermediateField.finite_setOf_exists_mem_eq_adjoin_simple_roots_natDegree_le_abs_intCoeff
decls.doc:
The simple subfields of an ambient field `A / ℚ` generated by roots of integer polynomials of
degree at most `d` and coefficient height at most `B` form a finite set.

This is the finiteness half of the root-to-field counting step used by the effective
Hermite--Minkowski target.
decls.statement:
theorem finite_setOf_exists_mem_eq_adjoin_simple_roots_natDegree_le_abs_intCoeff (d B : ℕ) :
    {E : IntermediateField ℚ A |
      ∃ x ∈ (⋃ (f : ℤ[X]) (_ : f.natDegree ≤ d ∧ ∀ i, |f.coeff i| ≤ (B : ℤ)),
        (((f.map (algebraMap ℤ A)).roots.toFinset : Set A))), E = ℚ⟮x⟯}.Finite

decls.name: TauCeti.IntermediateField.ncard_setOf_exists_mem_eq_adjoin_simple_roots_natDegree_le_abs_intCoeff_le
decls.doc:
The simple subfields of an ambient field `A / ℚ` generated by roots of integer polynomials of
degree at most `d` and coefficient height at most `B` number at most `(2 * B + 1) ^ (d + 1) * d`.

This is the root-to-field counting step used by the effective Hermite--Minkowski target, after
`TauCeti.Polynomial.ncard_biUnion_roots_natDegree_le_abs_intCoeff_le` has counted the possible
generators.
decls.statement:
theorem ncard_setOf_exists_mem_eq_adjoin_simple_roots_natDegree_le_abs_intCoeff_le (d B : ℕ) :
    {E : IntermediateField ℚ A |
      ∃ x ∈ (⋃ (f : ℤ[X]) (_ : f.natDegree ≤ d ∧ ∀ i, |f.coeff i| ≤ (B : ℤ)),
        (((f.map (algebraMap ℤ A)).roots.toFinset : Set A))), E = ℚ⟮x⟯}.ncard ≤
      (2 * B + 1) ^ (d + 1) * d

decls.name: TauCeti.NumberField.units_sq_index_le
decls.doc:
**Squares have small index in the unit group.** `[O_F^× : (O_F^×)²] ≤ 2^[F:ℚ]`, stated
using Mathlib's `Subgroup.square` for the subgroup of squares. By Dirichlet's unit theorem
`O_F^×` is generated by the `rank`-element fundamental system together with a torsion
generator, so `TauCeti.index_square_le_of_closure_eq_top` bounds the index by `2^(rank+1)`,
and `rank + 1 ≤ [F:ℚ]`.
decls.title: Squares have small index in the unit group
decls.statement:
theorem units_sq_index_le (F : Type*) [Field F] [NumberField F] :
    (Subgroup.square (𝓞 F)ˣ).index ≤ 2 ^ Module.finrank ℚ F

decls.name: TauCeti.NumberField.units_sq_index_le_of_finrank_le
decls.doc:
If a number field has degree at most `n`, then the square subgroup of its unit group has
index at most `2^n`. This is the monotone form of
`TauCeti.NumberField.units_sq_index_le`, useful when the degree has been bounded separately.

decls.name: TauCeti.NumberField.units_sq_index_le_of_finrank_eq
decls.doc:
Exact-degree specialization of `TauCeti.NumberField.units_sq_index_le`: if `[F : ℚ] = n`,
then `[O_F^× : (O_F^×)^2] ≤ 2^n`.

decls.name: TauCeti.NumberField.units_sq_index_le_of_finrank_eq_one
decls.doc: In a degree-one number field, the square subgroup of the unit group has index at most `2`.
decls.statement:
theorem units_sq_index_le_of_finrank_eq_one (F : Type*) [Field F] [NumberField F]
    (hF : finrank ℚ F = 1) :
    (Subgroup.square (𝓞 F)ˣ).index ≤ 2

decls.name: TauCeti.NumberField.units_sq_index_rat_le_two
decls.doc:
The square subgroup of `ℤˣ` has index at most `2`, viewed as the unit group of the ring of
integers of `ℚ`.
decls.statement:
theorem units_sq_index_rat_le_two :
    (Subgroup.square (𝓞 ℚ)ˣ).index ≤ 2

decls.name: TauCeti.NumberField.units_sq_index_le_quadratic
decls.doc: In a quadratic number field, the square subgroup of the unit group has index at most `4`.
decls.statement:
theorem units_sq_index_le_quadratic (F : Type*) [Field F] [NumberField F]
    (hF : finrank ℚ F = 2) :
    (Subgroup.square (𝓞 F)ˣ).index ≤ 4

decls.name: TauCeti.NumberField.units_sq_index_le_of_finrank_le_two
decls.doc:
If a number field has degree at most two, the square subgroup of the unit group has index at
most `4`. This is the form used when a quadratic-model argument supplies only `[F : ℚ] ≤ 2`.
decls.statement:
theorem units_sq_index_le_of_finrank_le_two (F : Type*) [Field F] [NumberField F]
    (hF : finrank ℚ F ≤ 2) :
    (Subgroup.square (𝓞 F)ˣ).index ≤ 4

decls.name: TauCeti.NumberField.card_units_elementaryTwoQuotient_le_of_finrank_le
decls.doc:
If `[F : ℚ] ≤ n`, then the elementary-2 quotient `O_F^×/(O_F^×)^2` has at most `2^n`
elements. This is just the unit-square index bound translated through
`TauCeti.card_elementaryTwoQuotient_eq_index_square`.
decls.statement:
theorem card_units_elementaryTwoQuotient_le_of_finrank_le
    (F : Type*) [Field F] [NumberField F] {n : ℕ} (hn : finrank ℚ F ≤ n) :
    Nat.card (TauCeti.ElementaryTwoQuotient (𝓞 F)ˣ) ≤ 2 ^ n

decls.name: TauCeti.NumberField.card_units_elementaryTwoQuotient_le_of_finrank_eq
decls.doc:
Exact-degree version of
`TauCeti.NumberField.card_units_elementaryTwoQuotient_le_of_finrank_le`.
decls.statement:
theorem card_units_elementaryTwoQuotient_le_of_finrank_eq
    (F : Type*) [Field F] [NumberField F] {n : ℕ} (hn : finrank ℚ F = n) :
    Nat.card (TauCeti.ElementaryTwoQuotient (𝓞 F)ˣ) ≤ 2 ^ n

decls.name: TauCeti.NumberField.card_units_elementaryTwoQuotient_le_of_finrank_eq_one
decls.doc:
In a degree-one number field, the elementary-2 quotient `O_F^×/(O_F^×)^2` has at most two

theorem card_units_elementaryTwoQuotient_le_of_finrank_eq_one

decls.doc:

decls.name: TauCeti.NumberField.WorkedExamples.instFactIrreducibleHSubPolynomialRatHPowXOfNatCoeRingHomCNeg_tauCeti
decls.doc:
`X² + 5` is irreducible over `ℚ`: a monic quadratic with no rational root (a rational
square is nonnegative, but `-5 < 0`).
decls.statement: instance : Fact (Irreducible (X ^ 2 - C (-5 : ℚ)))

decls.name: TauCeti.NumberField.WorkedExamples.classNumber_adjoinRoot_sqrt_neg_five_le
decls.doc:
**The class-number bound on `ℚ(√-5)`.** The class number of `ℚ(√-5)`, modelled as

example for the effective class-number bound.
decls.title: The class-number bound on `ℚ(√-5)`
decls.statement:
theorem classNumber_adjoinRoot_sqrt_neg_five_le :
    NumberField.classNumber (AdjoinRoot (X ^ 2 - C (-5 : ℚ))) ≤ 320

decls.name: TauCeti.NumberField.WorkedExamples.span_eq_top_of_one_mem_of_toInteger_mem
decls.doc:
The `ℤ`-span of any set containing `1` and a primitive fourth root of unity is all of `𝓞 K`:
those two elements are the vectors of the integral power basis.

decls.name: TauCeti.NumberField.WorkedExamples.discr_eq_neg_four_of_isCyclotomicExtension
decls.doc:
The discriminant of a fourth cyclotomic field is `-4`, recovered from the integral basis
`{1, i}`: the equality companion of the effective discriminant bound turns the trace-form value

decls.statement:
theorem discr_eq_neg_four_of_isCyclotomicExtension {K : Type*} [Field K]
    [NumberField K] [IsCyclotomicExtension {4} ℚ K] :
    NumberField.discr K = -4

decls.name: TauCeti.NumberField.WorkedExamples.discr_cyclotomicField_four

**The discriminant of `ℚ(i)`.** Recovering `d_{ℚ(i)} = -4` from the integral basis

decls.title: The discriminant of `ℚ(i)`
decls.statement: theorem discr_cyclotomicField_four : NumberField.discr (CyclotomicField 4 ℚ) = -4

decls.name: TauCeti.GeometryOfNumbers.box
decls.doc:
The closed polydisc of polyradius `c • r` in `ι → ℂ`: the points whose `i`-th
coordinate has norm at most `c · r i`.
decls.statement: def box (r : ι → ℝ) (c : ℝ) : Set (ι → ℂ)

decls.name: TauCeti.GeometryOfNumbers.mem_box
decls.doc: Membership in `box r c` unfolds to the coordinatewise norm bounds `‖x i‖ ≤ c · r i`.
decls.statement:
theorem mem_box {r : ι → ℝ} {c : ℝ} {x : ι → ℂ} :
    x ∈ box r c ↔ ∀ i, ‖x i‖ ≤ c * r i

decls.name: TauCeti.GeometryOfNumbers.box_mono
decls.doc:
The polydisc `box r c` is monotone in the scale `c` when every coordinate radius `r i`
is nonnegative: enlarging the scale enlarges the box.
decls.statement:
theorem box_mono {r : ι → ℝ} (hr : ∀ i, 0 ≤ r i) {c c' : ℝ} (h : c ≤ c') :
    box r c ⊆ box r c'

decls.name: TauCeti.GeometryOfNumbers.cell_index_mem
decls.doc:
Grid pigeonhole, axis bound: the cell index of a coordinate lying in the box is one of
the `⌊2√2·c/ε⌋ + 1` admissible values.
decls.statement:
theorem cell_index_mem {c ε : ℝ} (hε : 0 < ε) {ri : ℝ} (hri : 0 < ri)
    {t : ℝ} (ht : |t| ≤ c * ri) :
    ⌊(t + c * ri) / (ε * ri / Real.sqrt 2)⌋ ∈
      Finset.Icc (0 : ℤ) ((⌊2 * Real.sqrt 2 * c / ε⌋₊ : ℕ) : ℤ)

decls.name: TauCeti.GeometryOfNumbers.cell_index_diff
decls.doc:
Grid pigeonhole, cell-side bound: two coordinates in the same cell differ by less than
the cell side `ε·ri/√2`.

decls.name: TauCeti.GeometryOfNumbers.norm_lt_of_re_im_bound
decls.doc:
A complex number whose real and imaginary parts are each `< d` in absolute value has
norm `< d·√2`.
decls.statement:
theorem norm_lt_of_re_im_bound {z : ℂ} {d : ℝ} (hd : 0 ≤ d)
    (hre : |z.re| < d) (him : |z.im| < d) : ‖z‖ < d * Real.sqrt 2

decls.name: TauCeti.GeometryOfNumbers.cellCount_le
decls.doc: The per-axis cell count `⌊2√2·c/ε⌋ + 1` is at most `4·c/ε` (using `ε ≤ c`).
decls.statement:
theorem cellCount_le {c ε : ℝ} (hε : 0 < ε) (hεc : ε ≤ c) :
    ((⌊2 * Real.sqrt 2 * c / ε⌋₊ : ℕ) : ℝ) + 1 ≤ 4 * c / ε

decls.name: TauCeti.GeometryOfNumbers.cellIndexMap
decls.doc:
The cell-index map of scale `ε` for the box `box r c`: a point maps to the tuple of its
per-coordinate integer cell indices (of the real and imaginary parts), with cell side
`ε·rᵢ/√2`.
decls.statement: def cellIndexMap (r : ι → ℝ) (c ε : ℝ) : (ι → ℂ) → (ι → ℤ × ℤ)

decls.name: TauCeti.GeometryOfNumbers.injOn_cellIndexMap_of_separated
decls.doc:
The cell-index map is injective on a set whose distinct points are `ε`-separated in some
coordinate: two points sharing every cell index would differ by less than the cell diameter
`ε·rᵢ` in that coordinate, contradicting the separation.

decls.name: TauCeti.GeometryOfNumbers.finite_and_ncard_le_of_subset_box_of_separated
decls.doc:
**Grid pigeonhole / packing.** A subset of the polydisc `box r c` whose distinct points
are `ε`-separated in some coordinate (relative to `r`) is finite, of cardinality at most
`(4·c/ε) ^ (2·#ι)`.
decls.title: Grid pigeonhole / packing
decls.statement:
theorem finite_and_ncard_le_of_subset_box_of_separated (r : ι → ℝ) (hr : ∀ i, 0 < r i)
    {c ε : ℝ} (hε : 0 < ε) (hεc : ε ≤ c) {S : Set (ι → ℂ)} (hS : S ⊆ box r c)
    (hsep : ∀ x ∈ S, ∀ y ∈ S, x ≠ y → ∃ i, ε * r i < ‖x i - y i‖) :
    S.Finite ∧ (S.ncard : ℝ) ≤ (4 * c / ε) ^ (2 * Fintype.card ι)

decls.name: TauCeti.GeometryOfNumbers.addSubgroup_inter_box_finite_and_ncard_le_of_separated
decls.doc:
**Lattice points in the box.** If every nonzero element of `Λ` escapes the small polydisc
`box r ρ` in some coordinate, then `Λ ∩ box r 2` is finite of cardinality at most
`(8/ρ) ^ (2·#ι)`.
decls.title: Lattice points in the box
decls.statement:
theorem addSubgroup_inter_box_finite_and_ncard_le_of_separated (r : ι → ℝ) (hr : ∀ i, 0 < r i)
    (Λ : AddSubgroup (ι → ℂ)) {ρ : ℝ} (hρ0 : 0 < ρ) (hρ2 : ρ ≤ 2)
    (hsep : ∀ x ∈ Λ, x ≠ 0 → ∃ i, ρ * r i < ‖x i‖) :
    ((Λ : Set (ι → ℂ)) ∩ box r 2).Finite ∧
      (((Λ : Set (ι → ℂ)) ∩ box r 2).ncard : ℝ) ≤ (8 / ρ) ^ (2 * Fintype.card ι)

decls.name: TauCeti.GeometryOfNumbers.abs_sub_le_of_floor_eq
decls.doc:
Two reals lying in the same half-open floor-cell of positive width `q` (i.e.
`⌊a / q⌋ = ⌊b / q⌋`) differ by at most `q`.
decls.statement:
theorem abs_sub_le_of_floor_eq {a b q : ℝ} (hq : 0 < q) (h : ⌊a / q⌋ = ⌊b / q⌋) :
    |a - b| ≤ q

decls.name: TauCeti.GeometryOfNumbers.norm_sub_le_of_coarseCell_eq
decls.doc:
If two complex numbers share their coarse cell (side `2·ri/3`) in both the real and the
imaginary part, their distance is at most `ri`.
decls.statement:
theorem norm_sub_le_of_coarseCell_eq {ri : ℝ} (hri : 0 < ri) {z w : ℂ}
    (hre : ⌊z.re / (2 * ri / 3)⌋ = ⌊w.re / (2 * ri / 3)⌋)
    (him : ⌊z.im / (2 * ri / 3)⌋ = ⌊w.im / (2 * ri / 3)⌋) :
    ‖z - w‖ ≤ ri

decls.name: TauCeti.GeometryOfNumbers.coarseCell_mem_Icc
decls.doc:
A real of absolute value at most `2·ri` lands in one of the seven coarse cells
`Icc (-3) 3` of side `2·ri/3`.
decls.statement:
theorem coarseCell_mem_Icc {ri : ℝ} (hri : 0 < ri) {t : ℝ} (ht : |t| ≤ 2 * ri) :
    ⌊t / (2 * ri / 3)⌋ ∈ Finset.Icc (-3 : ℤ) 3

decls.name: TauCeti.GeometryOfNumbers.coarseCellMap
decls.doc:
The coarse cell index of `x` for the grid of side `2·r i/3`: per coordinate, the pair of
floor indices of the real and imaginary parts.
decls.statement: def coarseCellMap (r : ι → ℝ) (x : ι → ℂ) : ι → ℤ × ℤ

decls.name: TauCeti.GeometryOfNumbers.sub_mem_box_one_of_coarseCellMap_eq
decls.doc:
Two points sharing every coarse cell `coarseCellMap r` differ by at most `r i` in each
coordinate, so their difference lies in `box r 1`.
decls.statement:
theorem sub_mem_box_one_of_coarseCellMap_eq {r : ι → ℝ} (hr : ∀ i, 0 < r i) {y x : ι → ℂ}
    (h : coarseCellMap r y = coarseCellMap r x) : y - x ∈ box r 1

decls.name: TauCeti.GeometryOfNumbers.card_filter_le_of_sub_mem
decls.doc:
A `g`-fibre of `sA` has at most `sB.card` elements when the difference of any two
same-fibre points of `sA` lies in `sB`: translating the fibre to a fixed representative
injects it into `sB`.
decls.statement:
theorem card_filter_le_of_sub_mem {G : Type*} [AddGroup G] {σ : Type*} [DecidableEq σ]
    {sA sB : Finset G} {g : G → σ}
    (h : ∀ y ∈ sA, ∀ x ∈ sA, g y = g x → y - x ∈ sB) (b : σ) :
    (sA.filter (fun a => g a = b)).card ≤ sB.card

decls.name: TauCeti.GeometryOfNumbers.card_image_coarseCellMap_le
decls.doc:
If `s` is contained in `box r 2`, its image under `coarseCellMap r` has at most `49 ^ #ι`
elements: each coordinate part lands in the 7 cells `Icc (-3) 3`, so `7² = 49` cells per
coordinate and `49 ^ #ι` overall.
decls.statement:
theorem card_image_coarseCellMap_le {r : ι → ℝ} (hr : ∀ i, 0 < r i)
    {s : Finset (ι → ℂ)} (hs : ∀ x ∈ s, x ∈ box r 2) :
    (s.image (coarseCellMap r)).card ≤ 49 ^ Fintype.card ι

decls.name: TauCeti.GeometryOfNumbers.ncard_inter_box_two_le_pow_mul_ncard_inter_box_one
decls.doc:
**Doubling.** Assuming `Λ ∩ box r 2` is finite, counting lattice points in the double box
loses at most `49 ^ #ι` against the unit box:
`#(Λ ∩ box r 2) ≤ 49 ^ #ι · #(Λ ∩ box r 1)`.
decls.title: Doubling
decls.statement:
theorem ncard_inter_box_two_le_pow_mul_ncard_inter_box_one (r : ι → ℝ) (hr : ∀ i, 0 < r i)
    (Λ : AddSubgroup (ι → ℂ)) (hfin : ((Λ : Set (ι → ℂ)) ∩ box r 2).Finite) :
    (((Λ : Set (ι → ℂ)) ∩ box r 2).ncard : ℝ) ≤
      49 ^ Fintype.card ι * ((Λ : Set (ι → ℂ)) ∩ box r 1).ncard

decls.name: TauCeti.GeometryOfNumbers.gaussianLattice
decls.doc:
The Gaussian lattice `ℤ + ℤ·i`, realised as a rank-two additive subgroup of the plane
`Fin 1 → ℂ` (one copy of `ℂ ≅ ℝ²`): the points whose single coordinate is a Gaussian
integer.
decls.statement: def gaussianLattice : AddSubgroup (Fin 1 → ℂ)

decls.name: TauCeti.GeometryOfNumbers.mem_gaussianLattice
decls.doc:
Membership in the Gaussian lattice unfolds to the single coordinate being a Gaussian
integer.
decls.statement:
theorem mem_gaussianLattice {x : Fin 1 → ℂ} :
    x ∈ gaussianLattice ↔ ∃ m n : ℤ, x 0 = (m : ℂ) + (n : ℂ) * Complex.I

decls.name: TauCeti.GeometryOfNumbers.one_le_norm_of_mem_gaussianLattice_of_ne_zero
decls.doc:
**Minimal distance of the Gaussian lattice.** A nonzero Gaussian integer has norm at
least `1`, since its squared norm `m² + n²` is a positive integer. This is the separation
input the packing lemma needs.
decls.title: Minimal distance of the Gaussian lattice
decls.statement:
theorem one_le_norm_of_mem_gaussianLattice_of_ne_zero {x : Fin 1 → ℂ}
    (hx : x ∈ gaussianLattice) (hne : x ≠ 0) : 1 ≤ ‖x 0‖

decls.name: TauCeti.GeometryOfNumbers.gaussianLattice_separated
decls.doc:
The separation hypothesis the packing lemma consumes: every nonzero lattice point
escapes the box of scale `1/2`.
decls.statement:
theorem gaussianLattice_separated :
    ∀ x ∈ gaussianLattice, x ≠ 0 →
      ∃ i, (1 / 2 : ℝ) * (fun _ : Fin 1 => (1 : ℝ)) i < ‖x i‖

decls.name: TauCeti.GeometryOfNumbers.gaussianLattice_inter_box_two_finite
decls.doc:
**Discreteness via packing.** The Gaussian lattice meets the radius-two box in a finite
set: the engine's packing lemma discharges the finiteness hypothesis directly from the
minimal-distance bound.
decls.title: Discreteness via packing
decls.statement:
theorem gaussianLattice_inter_box_two_finite :
    ((gaussianLattice : Set (Fin 1 → ℂ)) ∩ box (fun _ => 1) 2).Finite

decls.name: TauCeti.GeometryOfNumbers.gaussianLattice_inter_box_two_ncard_le
decls.doc:
**Explicit packing count.** At most `256` Gaussian-lattice points lie in the radius-two
box, the engine's bound `(8/ρ)^(2·#ι)` evaluated at `ρ = 1/2` and `#ι = 1` (so `16² = 256`).
decls.title: Explicit packing count
decls.statement:
theorem gaussianLattice_inter_box_two_ncard_le :
    (((gaussianLattice : Set (Fin 1 → ℂ)) ∩ box (fun _ => 1) 2).ncard : ℝ) ≤ 256

decls.name: TauCeti.GeometryOfNumbers.gaussianLattice_ncard_inter_box_two_le_fortyNine_mul_ncard_inter_box_one
decls.doc:
**A concrete doubling instance.** Passing from the unit box to the double box multiplies the
Gaussian-lattice point count by at most the engine's proved factor `49^{#ι} = 49` at `#ι = 1`:
`#(Λ ∩ box 2) ≤ 49 · #(Λ ∩ box 1)`.
decls.title: A concrete doubling instance
decls.statement:
theorem gaussianLattice_ncard_inter_box_two_le_fortyNine_mul_ncard_inter_box_one :
    (((gaussianLattice : Set (Fin 1 → ℂ)) ∩ box (fun _ => 1) 2).ncard : ℝ) ≤
      49 * (((gaussianLattice : Set (Fin 1 → ℂ)) ∩ box (fun _ => 1) 1).ncard : ℝ)

decls.name: TauCeti.GeometryOfNumbers.gaussianLattice_ncard_inter_box_two_le_sixtyFour_mul_ncard_inter_box_one
decls.doc:
The same doubling instance with the rounder factor `64` — a compatibility corollary of
`gaussianLattice_ncard_inter_box_two_le_fortyNine_mul_ncard_inter_box_one`, weakening `49 ≤ 64`:
`#(Λ ∩ box 2) ≤ 64 · #(Λ ∩ box 1)`.
decls.statement:
theorem gaussianLattice_ncard_inter_box_two_le_sixtyFour_mul_ncard_inter_box_one :
    (((gaussianLattice : Set (Fin 1 → ℂ)) ∩ box (fun _ => 1) 2).ncard : ℝ) ≤
      64 * (((gaussianLattice : Set (Fin 1 → ℂ)) ∩ box (fun _ => 1) 1).ncard : ℝ)

decls.name: TauCeti.natCard_quotient_under
decls.doc:
The residue cardinality entering `AlgHom.IsArithFrobAt` over the rational prime `p` is `p`
itself: for `Q` lying over `(p)`, `Nat.card (ℤ ⧸ Q ∩ ℤ) = p`. Internal plumbing for
`apply_sqrt`.
decls.statement:
theorem natCard_quotient_under (Q : Ideal S) [Q.LiesOver (span {(p : ℤ)})] :
    Nat.card (ℤ ⧸ Q.under ℤ) = p

decls.name: TauCeti.AlgHom.IsArithFrobAt.sub_pow_mem
decls.doc:
The base Frobenius congruence over a rational prime: for an arithmetic Frobenius
`φ : S →ₐ[ℤ] S` at an ideal `Q` lying over `(p)`, `φ y ≡ y ^ p (mod Q)`, the exponent being `p`,
the cardinality of the base residue ring `ℤ ⧸ Q ∩ ℤ`. Internal plumbing for `apply_sqrt`.
decls.statement:
theorem AlgHom.IsArithFrobAt.sub_pow_mem {φ : S →ₐ[ℤ] S} (H : φ.IsArithFrobAt Q)
    [Q.LiesOver (span {(p : ℤ)})] (y : S) : φ y - y ^ p ∈ Q

decls.name: TauCeti.AlgHom.IsArithFrobAt.sub_legendreSym_smul_mem
decls.doc:
The **Frobenius congruence for a square root, refined by Euler's criterion**: for an
arithmetic Frobenius `φ : S →ₐ[ℤ] S` at `Q` lying over the odd rational prime `p`, if
`x² = d` then `φ x ≡ legendreSym p d • x (mod Q)`. Internal step of `apply_sqrt`.

decls.name: TauCeti.add_self_notMem
decls.doc:
The two square roots of `d` are **distinct modulo `Q`**: if `x² = d`, the prime `p` is odd
and `p ∤ d`, and `Q` lies over `(p)`, then `x + x ∉ Q`. (Otherwise `(x + x)² = 4d ∈ Q` would
give `p ∣ 4d`, forcing `p = 2` or `p ∣ d`.) Internal step of `apply_sqrt`.
decls.statement:
theorem add_self_notMem (hodd : p ≠ 2) (hd : ¬ (p : ℤ) ∣ d)
    [Q.LiesOver (span {(p : ℤ)})] (hx : x ^ 2 = algebraMap ℤ S d) : x + x ∉ Q

decls.name: TauCeti.AlgHom.IsArithFrobAt.apply_sqrt
decls.doc:
**An arithmetic Frobenius acts on square roots by the Legendre symbol.** Let `S` be a
domain, `Q` an ideal of `S` over the odd rational prime `p`, and `φ : S →ₐ[ℤ] S` an arithmetic
Frobenius at `Q`. If `x² = d` for an integer `d` not divisible by `p`, then
`φ x = legendreSym p d • x`: the Frobenius fixes `√d` when `d` is a quadratic residue mod `p`
and negates it otherwise. (Primality of `Q` is not needed: the sign separation comes from `S`
being a domain and `Q ∩ ℤ = (p)`.)
decls.title: An arithmetic Frobenius acts on square roots by the Legendre symbol
decls.statement:
theorem AlgHom.IsArithFrobAt.apply_sqrt {φ : S →ₐ[ℤ] S} (H : φ.IsArithFrobAt Q)
    [Q.LiesOver (span {(p : ℤ)})] (hodd : p ≠ 2) (hd : ¬ (p : ℤ) ∣ d)
    (hx : x ^ 2 = algebraMap ℤ S d) :
    φ x = legendreSym p d • x

decls.name: TauCeti.IsArithFrobAt.smul_sqrt
decls.doc:
**A Frobenius element acts on square roots by the Legendre symbol**, action form: if `σ : M`
is an arithmetic Frobenius at an ideal `Q` over the odd prime `p` and `x² = d` with `p ∤ d`,
then `σ • x = legendreSym p d • x`. Only a monoid action is needed.
decls.title: A Frobenius element acts on square roots by the Legendre symbol
decls.statement:
theorem IsArithFrobAt.smul_sqrt {M : Type*} [Monoid M] [MulSemiringAction M S]
    [SMulCommClass M ℤ S] {σ : M} (H : _root_.IsArithFrobAt ℤ σ Q)
    [Q.LiesOver (span {(p : ℤ)})] (hodd : p ≠ 2) (hd : ¬ (p : ℤ) ∣ d)
    (hx : x ^ 2 = algebraMap ℤ S d) :
    σ • x = legendreSym p d • x

decls.name: TauCeti.prime_intCast_of_fact
decls.doc: An integer prime from the ambient natural prime `p`.
decls.statement: theorem prime_intCast_of_fact : Prime (p : ℤ)

decls.name: TauCeti.dvd_mul_sq_iff
decls.doc: For `u` with `p ∤ u`, the prime `p` divides `a * u ^ 2` exactly when it divides `a`.
decls.statement:
theorem dvd_mul_sq_iff {a u : ℤ} (hu : ¬ (p : ℤ) ∣ u) :
    (p : ℤ) ∣ a * u ^ 2 ↔ (p : ℤ) ∣ a

decls.name: TauCeti.not_dvd_mul_sq_iff
decls.doc: Multiplying by `u ^ 2` with `p ∤ u` preserves non-divisibility by `p`.
decls.statement:
theorem not_dvd_mul_sq_iff {a u : ℤ} (hu : ¬ (p : ℤ) ∣ u) :
    ¬ (p : ℤ) ∣ a * u ^ 2 ↔ ¬ (p : ℤ) ∣ a

decls.name: TauCeti.legendreSym_mul_sq
decls.doc: Multiplying an integer by `u ^ 2` with `p ∤ u` does not change its Legendre symbol.
decls.statement:
theorem legendreSym_mul_sq {a u : ℤ} (hu : ¬ (p : ℤ) ∣ u) :
    legendreSym p (a * u ^ 2) = legendreSym p a

decls.name: TauCeti.forall_legendreSym_eq_of_forall_eq_mul_sq
decls.doc:
Replacing each radicand in a family by `d i * u i ^ 2` with `p ∤ u i` preserves all the
Legendre symbols pointwise.

decls.name: TauCeti.forall_legendreSym_eq_one_iff_of_forall_eq_mul_sq
decls.doc:
The quadratic-residue conditions of a family are unchanged by replacing each radicand by
`d i * u i ^ 2` with `p ∤ u i`.

decls.name: TauCeti.forall_not_dvd_iff_of_forall_eq_mul_sq
decls.doc:
The unramifiedness conditions of a family are unchanged by replacing each radicand by
`d i * u i ^ 2` with `p ∤ u i`.

decls.name: TauCeti.Multiquadratic.not_isSquare_prod_optionNeg
decls.doc:
**Adjoining a negative radicand preserves square-class independence.** Let `d : ι → K` be a
family of positive radicands in an ordered field, no nonempty subset product of which is a
square, and let `c < 0`. Index by `Option ι`, sending `none` to `c` and `some i` to `d i`. Then
no nonempty subset product of this extended family is a square: a subset that avoids `none` is a
nonempty positive non-square by hypothesis, and a subset that contains `none` has a negative
product (the negative `c` times a positive product), so it is not a square either.
decls.title: Adjoining a negative radicand preserves square-class independence
decls.statement:
theorem not_isSquare_prod_optionNeg {K : Type*} [Field K] [LinearOrder K] [IsStrictOrderedRing K]
    {ι : Type*} {d : ι → K} (hpos : ∀ i, 0 < d i)
    (hindep : ∀ S : Finset ι, S.Nonempty → ¬ IsSquare (∏ i ∈ S, d i))
    {c : K} (hc : c < 0) (S : Finset (Option ι)) (hS : S.Nonempty) :
    ¬ IsSquare (∏ x ∈ S, x.elim c d)

decls.name: TauCeti.Multiquadratic.cmRadicand
decls.doc:
The `Option ι`-indexed radicand family of a multiquadratic CM field: `none ↦ -1` (for `i`)
and `some i ↦ p i` (for `√(p i)`).
decls.statement: def cmRadicand : Option ι → ℚ

decls.name: TauCeti.Multiquadratic.cmRoot
decls.doc:
The `Option ι`-indexed generator family of a multiquadratic CM field: `none ↦ i` and
`some i ↦ √(p i)` (as a complex number).
decls.statement: def cmRoot : Option ι → ℂ

decls.name: TauCeti.Multiquadratic.cmRadicand_none
decls.statement: theorem cmRadicand_none : cmRadicand p none = -1

decls.name: TauCeti.Multiquadratic.cmRadicand_some
decls.statement: theorem cmRadicand_some (i : ι) : cmRadicand p (some i) = (p i : ℚ)

decls.name: TauCeti.Multiquadratic.cmRoot_none
decls.statement: theorem cmRoot_none : cmRoot p none = Complex.I

decls.name: TauCeti.Multiquadratic.cmRoot_some
decls.statement: theorem cmRoot_some (i : ι) : cmRoot p (some i) = ((Real.sqrt (p i) : ℝ) : ℂ)

decls.name: TauCeti.Multiquadratic.cmRoot_sq
decls.doc:
The generator family squares to the radicand family: `i² = -1` and `√(p i)² = p i`. This is
the `hroot` hypothesis the field-generic multiquadratic results consume.
decls.statement: theorem cmRoot_sq (x : Option ι) : cmRoot p x ^ 2 = algebraMap ℚ ℂ (cmRadicand p x)

decls.name: TauCeti.Multiquadratic.range_cmRoot
decls.doc:
The range of the CM generator family is the inserted generator set: `i` together with the
real square roots `√(p i)`. This identifies `adjoin ℚ (Set.range (cmRoot p))` with the named
field `ℚ(i, √p₁, …, √pₙ)`.
decls.statement:
theorem range_cmRoot :
    Set.range (cmRoot p)
      = insert Complex.I (Set.range fun i => ((Real.sqrt (p i) : ℝ) : ℂ))

decls.name: TauCeti.Multiquadratic.not_isSquare_prod_cmRadicand
decls.doc:
The CM radicand family is square-class independent: for distinct primes `p`, no nonempty
subset product of `-1, p₁, …, pₙ` is a square in `ℚ`.
decls.statement:
theorem not_isSquare_prod_cmRadicand (hp : ∀ i, (p i).Prime) (hinj : Function.Injective p)
