theorem stabilizer_eq_bot_of_forall_legendreSym_eq_one {ι : Type*} (d : ι → ℤ) (r : ι → K)
    (hr : ∀ i, r i ^ 2 = algebraMap ℤ K (d i))
    (htop : IntermediateField.adjoin ℚ (Set.range r) = ⊤)
    {p : ℕ} [Fact p.Prime] (hodd : p ≠ 2)
    (hqr : ∀ i, legendreSym p (d i) = 1)
    (Q : Ideal (𝓞 K)) [Q.IsPrime] [Q.LiesOver (span {(p : ℤ)})] :
    stabilizer (K ≃ₐ[ℚ] K) Q = ⊥

decls.name: TauCeti.NumberField.ncard_primesOver_multiquadratic_iff
decls.doc:
**The multiquadratic splitting law.** For `K = ℚ(√d₁, …, √dₙ)` generated over `ℚ` by square
roots `r i` of integers `d i`, and an odd prime `p` dividing none of the `d i`, `p` splits
completely in `K` iff every `d i` is a quadratic residue mod `p`.
decls.title: The multiquadratic splitting law
decls.statement:
theorem ncard_primesOver_multiquadratic_iff {ι : Type*} [Finite ι] (d : ι → ℤ) (r : ι → K)
    (hr : ∀ i, r i ^ 2 = algebraMap ℤ K (d i))
    (htop : IntermediateField.adjoin ℚ (Set.range r) = ⊤)
    {p : ℕ} [Fact p.Prime] (hodd : p ≠ 2) (hcop : ∀ i, ¬ (p : ℤ) ∣ d i) :
    (primesOver (span {(p : ℤ)}) (𝓞 K)).ncard = finrank ℚ K ↔
      ∀ i, legendreSym p (d i) = 1

decls.name: TauCeti.Multiquadratic.oddPrimeDiscriminant
decls.doc:
The odd prime discriminant `p*`: `p` when `p % 4 = 1` and `-p` otherwise (so the value is
`-p` for every `p` with `p % 4 ≠ 1`, including even inputs). The `p ≡ 3 (mod 4)` reading of the
second case is the intended one for odd primes. The primality hypothesis is not part of the
definition so that the expression rewrites by computation; the API below supplies the
prime-specific facts.
decls.statement: def oddPrimeDiscriminant (p : ℕ) : ℤ

decls.name: TauCeti.Multiquadratic.oddPrimeDiscriminant_def
decls.doc: The defining `if` expression for the odd prime discriminant.
decls.statement:
theorem oddPrimeDiscriminant_def (p : ℕ) :
    oddPrimeDiscriminant p = if p % 4 = 1 then (p : ℤ) else -(p : ℤ)

decls.name: TauCeti.Multiquadratic.oddPrimeDiscriminant_of_mod_four_eq_one
decls.doc: If `p ≡ 1 (mod 4)`, its odd prime discriminant is `p`.
decls.statement:
theorem oddPrimeDiscriminant_of_mod_four_eq_one {p : ℕ} (hp : p % 4 = 1) :
    oddPrimeDiscriminant p = p

decls.name: TauCeti.Multiquadratic.oddPrimeDiscriminant_of_mod_four_ne_one
decls.doc:
If `p ≠ 1 (mod 4)`, its odd prime discriminant is `-p`. For an odd prime this is the
`p ≡ 3 (mod 4)` case.
decls.statement:
theorem oddPrimeDiscriminant_of_mod_four_ne_one {p : ℕ} (hp : p % 4 ≠ 1) :
    oddPrimeDiscriminant p = -(p : ℤ)

decls.name: TauCeti.Multiquadratic.oddPrimeDiscriminant_of_mod_four_eq_three
decls.doc: If `p ≡ 3 (mod 4)`, its odd prime discriminant is `-p`.
decls.statement:
theorem oddPrimeDiscriminant_of_mod_four_eq_three {p : ℕ} (hp : p % 4 = 3) :
    oddPrimeDiscriminant p = -(p : ℤ)

decls.name: TauCeti.Multiquadratic.oddPrimeDiscriminant_natAbs
decls.doc: The absolute value of the odd prime discriminant is the underlying natural number.
decls.statement:
theorem oddPrimeDiscriminant_natAbs (p : ℕ) :
    (oddPrimeDiscriminant p).natAbs = p

decls.name: TauCeti.Multiquadratic.oddPrimeDiscriminant_ne_zero
decls.doc: The odd prime discriminant is nonzero exactly when `p` is nonzero.
decls.statement:
theorem oddPrimeDiscriminant_ne_zero {p : ℕ} :
    oddPrimeDiscriminant p ≠ 0 ↔ p ≠ 0

decls.name: TauCeti.Multiquadratic.prime_oddPrimeDiscriminant
decls.doc: The odd prime discriminant of a natural prime is a prime integer.
decls.statement:
theorem prime_oddPrimeDiscriminant {p : ℕ} (hp : p.Prime) :
    Prime (oddPrimeDiscriminant p)

decls.name: TauCeti.Multiquadratic.squarefree_oddPrimeDiscriminant
decls.doc: The odd prime discriminant of a squarefree natural number is squarefree.
decls.statement:
theorem squarefree_oddPrimeDiscriminant {p : ℕ} (hp : Squarefree p) :
    Squarefree (oddPrimeDiscriminant p)

decls.name: TauCeti.Multiquadratic.oddPrimeDiscriminant_dvd_iff
decls.doc: The odd prime discriminant divides an integer exactly when `p` does.
decls.statement:
theorem oddPrimeDiscriminant_dvd_iff {p : ℕ} {D : ℤ} :
    oddPrimeDiscriminant p ∣ D ↔ (p : ℤ) ∣ D

decls.name: TauCeti.Multiquadratic.dvd_oddPrimeDiscriminant_iff
decls.doc:
An integer divides an odd prime discriminant exactly when it divides the underlying
natural number. This form is convenient when checking the unramifiedness side of the
splitting law.
decls.statement:
theorem dvd_oddPrimeDiscriminant_iff {p : ℕ} {q : ℤ} :
    q ∣ oddPrimeDiscriminant p ↔ q ∣ (p : ℤ)

decls.name: TauCeti.Multiquadratic.not_dvd_oddPrimeDiscriminant_iff
decls.doc:
An integer does not divide an odd prime discriminant exactly when it does not divide the
underlying natural number.
The negated form is convenient for the unramifiedness side of the splitting law.
decls.statement:
theorem not_dvd_oddPrimeDiscriminant_iff {p : ℕ} {q : ℤ} :
    ¬ q ∣ oddPrimeDiscriminant p ↔ ¬ q ∣ (p : ℤ)

decls.name: TauCeti.Multiquadratic.forall_not_dvd_oddPrimeDiscriminant_iff
decls.doc:
Family form of unramifiedness for odd prime discriminants: an integer divides none of
the `p i*` exactly when it divides none of the underlying `p i`.
decls.statement:
theorem forall_not_dvd_oddPrimeDiscriminant_iff {ι : Type*} (p : ι → ℕ) {q : ℤ} :
    (∀ i, ¬ q ∣ oddPrimeDiscriminant (p i)) ↔
      ∀ i, ¬ q ∣ (p i : ℤ)

decls.name: TauCeti.Multiquadratic.odd_oddPrimeDiscriminant
decls.doc: The odd prime discriminant of an odd natural number is odd.
decls.statement:
theorem odd_oddPrimeDiscriminant {p : ℕ} (hp : Odd p) :
    Odd (oddPrimeDiscriminant p)

decls.name: TauCeti.Multiquadratic.mod_four_eq_one_or_three_of_odd
decls.doc: An odd natural number is `1` or `3` modulo `4`.
decls.statement:
theorem mod_four_eq_one_or_three_of_odd {p : ℕ} (hp : Odd p) :
    p % 4 = 1 ∨ p % 4 = 3

decls.name: TauCeti.Multiquadratic.oddPrimeDiscriminant_mod_four_eq_one
decls.doc: For an odd `p`, the odd prime discriminant is congruent to `1` modulo `4`.
decls.statement:
theorem oddPrimeDiscriminant_mod_four_eq_one {p : ℕ} (hp : Odd p) :
    oddPrimeDiscriminant p % 4 = 1

decls.name: TauCeti.Multiquadratic.oddPrimeDiscriminant_eq_or_eq_neg
decls.doc: The odd prime discriminant is always either `p` or `-p`.
decls.statement:
theorem oddPrimeDiscriminant_eq_or_eq_neg {p : ℕ} :
    oddPrimeDiscriminant p = (p : ℤ) ∨ oddPrimeDiscriminant p = -(p : ℤ)

decls.name: TauCeti.Multiquadratic.oddPrimeDiscriminant_pos_iff
decls.doc: The sign of the odd prime discriminant is controlled by `p mod 4`.
decls.statement:
theorem oddPrimeDiscriminant_pos_iff {p : ℕ} :
    0 < oddPrimeDiscriminant p ↔ p % 4 = 1

decls.name: TauCeti.Multiquadratic.oddPrimeDiscriminant_neg_iff
decls.doc: The odd prime discriminant is negative exactly in the `p ≡ 3 (mod 4)` case.
decls.statement:
theorem oddPrimeDiscriminant_neg_iff {p : ℕ} (hp : Odd p) :
    oddPrimeDiscriminant p < 0 ↔ p % 4 = 3

decls.name: TauCeti.Multiquadratic.oddPrimeDiscriminant_eq_neg_one_pow_div_two_mul
decls.doc: The odd prime discriminant in the standard notation `p* = (-1)^(p/2) p`.
decls.statement:
theorem oddPrimeDiscriminant_eq_neg_one_pow_div_two_mul {p : ℕ} (hp : Odd p) :
    oddPrimeDiscriminant p = (-1 : ℤ) ^ (p / 2) * p

decls.name: TauCeti.Multiquadratic.oddPrimeDiscriminant_eq_neg_one_pow_pred_div_two_mul
decls.doc:
The odd prime discriminant in the standard notation
`p* = (-1)^((p - 1)/2) p`.
decls.statement:
theorem oddPrimeDiscriminant_eq_neg_one_pow_pred_div_two_mul {p : ℕ} (hp : Odd p) :
    oddPrimeDiscriminant p = (-1 : ℤ) ^ ((p - 1) / 2) * p

decls.name: TauCeti.NumberField.not_intCast_prime_dvd_neg_four
decls.statement:
theorem not_intCast_prime_dvd_neg_four {p : ℕ} [Fact p.Prime] (hodd : p ≠ 2) :
    ¬ (p : ℤ) ∣ (-4 : ℤ)

decls.name: TauCeti.NumberField.forall_not_dvd_negFourFivePrimeDiscriminants
decls.statement:
theorem forall_not_dvd_negFourFivePrimeDiscriminants {p : ℕ} [Fact p.Prime]
    (hodd : p ≠ 2) (hfive : p ≠ 5) :
    ∀ i, ¬ (p : ℤ) ∣ TauCeti.Multiquadratic.negFourFivePrimeDiscriminants i

decls.name: TauCeti.NumberField.forall_not_dvd_negFourNegThreeNegSevenPrimeDiscriminants
decls.statement:
theorem forall_not_dvd_negFourNegThreeNegSevenPrimeDiscriminants {p : ℕ} [Fact p.Prime]
    (hodd : p ≠ 2) (hthree : p ≠ 3) (hseven : p ≠ 7) :
    ∀ i, ¬ (p : ℤ) ∣
      TauCeti.Multiquadratic.negFourNegThreeNegSevenPrimeDiscriminants i

decls.name: TauCeti.NumberField.ncard_primesOver_neg_four_five_iff
decls.doc:
**Complete splitting for the `ℚ(√-5)` genus-field generator list.** Let `K` be generated
by square roots of the radicands attached to `[-4, 5]`, namely `-1` and `5`. An odd prime
`p ≠ 5` splits completely in `K` exactly under the two character conditions
`p ≡ 1 (mod 4)` and `(p / 5) = 1`.
decls.title: Complete splitting for the `ℚ(√-5)` genus-field generator list
decls.statement:
theorem ncard_primesOver_neg_four_five_iff (r : Fin 2 → K)
    (hr : ∀ i, r i ^ 2 = algebraMap ℤ K
      (TauCeti.Multiquadratic.primeDiscriminantRadicand
        (TauCeti.Multiquadratic.negFourFivePrimeDiscriminants i)))
    (htop : IntermediateField.adjoin ℚ (Set.range r) = ⊤)
    {p : ℕ} [Fact p.Prime] (hodd : p ≠ 2) (hfive : p ≠ 5) :
    (primesOver (span {(p : ℤ)}) (RingOfIntegers K)).ncard = finrank ℚ K ↔
      p % 4 = 1 ∧ @legendreSym 5 ⟨by decide⟩ (p : ℤ) = 1

decls.name: TauCeti.NumberField.ncard_primesOver_neg_four_neg_three_neg_seven_iff
decls.doc:
**Complete splitting for the `ℚ(√-21)` genus-field generator list.** Let `K` be generated
by square roots of the radicands attached to `[-4, -3, -7]`, namely `-1`, `-3`, and `-7`.
An odd prime `p` not among `3` and `7` splits completely in `K` exactly under the three
character conditions `p ≡ 1 (mod 4)`, `(p / 3) = 1`, and `(p / 7) = 1`.
decls.title: Complete splitting for the `ℚ(√-21)` genus-field generator list
decls.statement:
theorem ncard_primesOver_neg_four_neg_three_neg_seven_iff (r : Fin 3 → K)
    (hr : ∀ i, r i ^ 2 = algebraMap ℤ K
      (TauCeti.Multiquadratic.primeDiscriminantRadicand
        (TauCeti.Multiquadratic.negFourNegThreeNegSevenPrimeDiscriminants i)))
    (htop : IntermediateField.adjoin ℚ (Set.range r) = ⊤)
    {p : ℕ} [Fact p.Prime] (hodd : p ≠ 2) (hthree : p ≠ 3) (hseven : p ≠ 7) :
    (primesOver (span {(p : ℤ)}) (RingOfIntegers K)).ncard = finrank ℚ K ↔
      p % 4 = 1 ∧ @legendreSym 3 ⟨by decide⟩ (p : ℤ) = 1 ∧
        @legendreSym 7 ⟨by decide⟩ (p : ℤ) = 1

decls.name: TauCeti.Multiquadratic.negFourFivePrimeDiscriminants
decls.doc: The prime-discriminant list `[-4, 5]` for the genus-field generators of `ℚ(√-5)`.
decls.statement: abbrev negFourFivePrimeDiscriminants : Fin 2 → ℤ

decls.name: TauCeti.Multiquadratic.negFourNegThreeNegSevenPrimeDiscriminants
decls.doc:
The prime-discriminant list `[-4, -3, -7]` for the genus-field generators of
`ℚ(√-21)`.
decls.statement: abbrev negFourNegThreeNegSevenPrimeDiscriminants : Fin 3 → ℤ

decls.name: TauCeti.Multiquadratic.isPrimeDiscriminant_negFourNegThreeNegSevenPrimeDiscriminants
decls.doc: Each entry of the `[-4, -3, -7]` list is a prime discriminant.
decls.statement:
theorem isPrimeDiscriminant_negFourNegThreeNegSevenPrimeDiscriminants :
    ∀ i : Fin 3, IsPrimeDiscriminant (negFourNegThreeNegSevenPrimeDiscriminants i)

decls.name: TauCeti.Multiquadratic.injective_negFourNegThreeNegSevenPrimeDiscriminants
decls.doc: The `[-4, -3, -7]` list has no repeated entries.
decls.statement:
theorem injective_negFourNegThreeNegSevenPrimeDiscriminants :
    Function.Injective negFourNegThreeNegSevenPrimeDiscriminants

decls.name: TauCeti.Multiquadratic.not_all_three_evenPrimeDiscriminants_negFourNegThreeNegSevenPrimeDiscriminants
decls.doc: The `[-4, -3, -7]` list does not contain all three even prime discriminants.
decls.statement:
theorem not_all_three_evenPrimeDiscriminants_negFourNegThreeNegSevenPrimeDiscriminants :
    ¬ ((∃ i : Fin 3, negFourNegThreeNegSevenPrimeDiscriminants i = -4) ∧
      (∃ i : Fin 3, negFourNegThreeNegSevenPrimeDiscriminants i = 8) ∧
        (∃ i : Fin 3, negFourNegThreeNegSevenPrimeDiscriminants i = -8))

decls.name: TauCeti.Multiquadratic.galoisGroupEquivPrimeDiscriminantRadicands
decls.doc:
**The Galois group from prime-discriminant radicands is `(ℤ/2)ⁿ`.** For an injective
family of prime discriminants `D : ι → ℤ` which does not contain all three even prime
discriminants `-4`, `8`, and `-8`, and chosen roots of their squarefree radicands, the Galois
group of the generated multiquadratic field is `Multiplicative (ι → ZMod 2)`. This is the
prime-discriminant instance of the field-generic `galoisGroupEquiv`.
decls.title: The Galois group from prime-discriminant radicands is `(ℤ/2)ⁿ`

decls.name: TauCeti.Multiquadratic.galoisGroupEquivPrimeDiscriminantRadicands_apply
decls.doc:
The prime-discriminant Galois equivalence sends an automorphism to its sign pattern on the
chosen radicand roots.
decls.statement:
theorem galoisGroupEquivPrimeDiscriminantRadicands_apply
    (σ : adjoin ℚ (Set.range root) ≃ₐ[ℚ] adjoin ℚ (Set.range root)) :
    galoisGroupEquivPrimeDiscriminantRadicands D hD hinj heven root hroot σ =
      Multiplicative.ofAdd (signPattern root σ)

decls.name: TauCeti.Multiquadratic.galoisGroupEquivPrimeDiscriminantRadicands_symm_apply_gen
decls.doc:
The inverse prime-discriminant Galois equivalence realizes a sign pattern by sending each
chosen generator to `(-1)^(ε i)` times that generator.
decls.statement:
theorem galoisGroupEquivPrimeDiscriminantRadicands_symm_apply_gen
    (ε : ι → ZMod 2) (i : ι) :
    ((galoisGroupEquivPrimeDiscriminantRadicands D hD hinj heven root hroot).symm
        (Multiplicative.ofAdd ε)) (gen root i)
      = (-1) ^ (ε i).val * gen root i

decls.name: TauCeti.Multiquadratic.card_aut_adjoin_roots_primeDiscriminantRadicands
decls.doc:
**Cardinality of the Galois group from prime-discriminant radicands.** Under the same
prime-discriminant hypotheses, `|Gal(ℚ(rootᵢ : i)/ℚ)| = 2^|ι|`.
decls.title: Cardinality of the Galois group from prime-discriminant radicands
decls.statement:
theorem card_aut_adjoin_roots_primeDiscriminantRadicands :
    Nat.card (adjoin ℚ (Set.range root) ≃ₐ[ℚ] adjoin ℚ (Set.range root)) =
      2 ^ Nat.card ι

decls.name: TauCeti.Multiquadratic.root_neg_four_five_sq
decls.doc:
The complex square root data for the two prime discriminants `-4` and `5`: the associated
radicands are `-1` and `5`, with roots `i` and `√5`.
decls.statement:
theorem root_neg_four_five_sq (i : Fin 2) :
    (fun i : Fin 2 => ![Complex.I, ((Real.sqrt 5 : ℝ) : ℂ)] i) i ^ 2 =
      algebraMap ℚ ℂ
        (((primeDiscriminantRadicand (![(-4 : ℤ), 5] i) : ℤ) : ℚ))

decls.name: TauCeti.Multiquadratic.card_aut_adjoin_I_sqrt_five
decls.doc:
**Worked example: `|Gal(ℚ(i, √5)/ℚ)| = 4`.** This is the Galois group of the
multiquadratic field generated by the radicands attached to the prime discriminants `-4` and
`5`, the genus-field generators for `ℚ(√-5)`.
decls.title: Worked example: `|Gal(ℚ(i, √5)/ℚ)| = 4`
decls.statement:
theorem card_aut_adjoin_I_sqrt_five :
    Nat.card
      ((adjoin ℚ ({Complex.I, ((Real.sqrt 5 : ℝ) : ℂ)} : Set ℂ) :
          IntermediateField ℚ ℂ)
          ≃ₐ[ℚ]
        (adjoin ℚ ({Complex.I, ((Real.sqrt 5 : ℝ) : ℂ)} : Set ℂ) :
          IntermediateField ℚ ℂ))
      = 4

decls.name: TauCeti.Multiquadratic.prod_primeDiscriminantRadicands_ne_neg_one
decls.doc: Products over odd prime-discriminant radicands, with no `-4` radicand, are not `-1`.

decls.name: TauCeti.Multiquadratic.squarefree_prod_primeDiscriminantRadicands_of_pairwise_isCoprime
decls.doc:
Products over prime-discriminant radicands are squarefree when the selected radicands are
pairwise coprime.

decls.name: TauCeti.Multiquadratic.not_isSquare_prod_primeDiscriminantRadicands_of_pairwise_isCoprime
decls.doc:
Products over pairwise coprime prime-discriminant radicands are not rational squares, provided
the selected product is not the empty product in disguise.

decls.name: TauCeti.Multiquadratic.prod_primeDiscriminantRadicands_ne_one_of_nonempty
decls.doc:
A product of prime-discriminant radicands is not `1` as soon as the discriminant family is
injective and the selected set is nonempty.

decls.name: TauCeti.Multiquadratic.isCoprime_primeDiscriminantRadicand
decls.doc:
**Coprimality of distinct prime-discriminant radicands.** The radicands of two distinct prime
discriminants are coprime except for the ordered exceptional pairs `8`, `-8` and `-8`, `8`.
Their absolute values are `1`, `2` (the even radicands), or distinct odd primes (the odd ones);
the only non-coprime distinct even radicands are `2` and `-2`.
decls.title: Coprimality of distinct prime-discriminant radicands
decls.statement:
theorem isCoprime_primeDiscriminantRadicand {D E : ℤ}
    (hD : IsPrimeDiscriminant D) (hE : IsPrimeDiscriminant E) (hDE : D ≠ E)
    (hnot : ¬ ((D = 8 ∧ E = -8) ∨ (D = -8 ∧ E = 8))) :
    IsCoprime (primeDiscriminantRadicand D) (primeDiscriminantRadicand E)

decls.name: TauCeti.Multiquadratic.not_isSquare_prod_primeDiscriminantRadicands_of_mem_eight_neg_eight
decls.doc:
Square-class independence in the exceptional even case where `S` carries indices for both `8`
and `-8` but none for `-4`: the product of the radicands `primeDiscriminantRadicand (D i)` over `S`
is not a rational square.
decls.statement:
theorem not_isSquare_prod_primeDiscriminantRadicands_of_mem_eight_neg_eight {ι : Type*}
    {D : ι → ℤ} (hD : ∀ i, IsPrimeDiscriminant (D i)) (hinj : Function.Injective D)
    {S : Finset ι} (hno4S : ∀ i ∈ S, D i ≠ -4)
    (hboth : (∃ i ∈ S, D i = 8) ∧ (∃ i ∈ S, D i = -8)) :
    ¬ IsSquare (∏ i ∈ S, ((primeDiscriminantRadicand (D i) : ℤ) : ℚ))

decls.name: TauCeti.Multiquadratic.not_isSquare_prod_primeDiscriminantRadicands
decls.doc:
**Square-class independence of prime discriminants.** Let `D : ι → ℤ` be an injective family
of prime discriminants which does not contain all three even prime discriminants `-4`, `8`, and
`-8`. Then no nonempty subset product of the radicands `primeDiscriminantRadicand (D i)` is a
rational square. This is the `hindep` hypothesis the multiquadratic degree theorem
`finrank_adjoin_range` consumes, applied to the genus-field generators.
decls.title: Square-class independence of prime discriminants
decls.statement:
theorem not_isSquare_prod_primeDiscriminantRadicands {ι : Type*} (D : ι → ℤ)
    (hD : ∀ i, IsPrimeDiscriminant (D i)) (hinj : Function.Injective D)
    (heven : ¬ ((∃ i, D i = -4) ∧ (∃ i, D i = 8) ∧ (∃ i, D i = -8))) :
    ∀ S : Finset ι, S.Nonempty →
      ¬ IsSquare (∏ i ∈ S, ((primeDiscriminantRadicand (D i) : ℤ) : ℚ))

decls.name: TauCeti.Multiquadratic.not_all_three_evenPrimeDiscriminants_of_forall_isEvenPrimeDiscriminant_eq
decls.doc:
A prime-discriminant family with at most one even prime discriminant cannot contain the three
even prime discriminants `-4`, `8`, and `-8` simultaneously.

The hypothesis is stated extensionally: any two indices whose discriminants are even prime
discriminants must carry the same discriminant value. This is the form supplied by the
prime-discriminant factorization of a quadratic discriminant, where there is only one 2-adic
factor.

decls.name: TauCeti.Multiquadratic.not_isSquare_prod_primeDiscriminantRadicands_of_forall_isEvenPrimeDiscriminant_eq
decls.doc:
**Square-class independence for prime-discriminant families with at most one even factor.**
Let `D : ι → ℤ` be an injective family of prime discriminants, and assume any two even prime
discriminants in the family are equal as integers. Then no nonempty subset product of the
associated radicands `primeDiscriminantRadicand (D i)` is a rational square.

This is the genus-field specialization of
`not_isSquare_prod_primeDiscriminantRadicands`: the prime discriminants dividing a quadratic
discriminant have at most one even member, so the exceptional product
`(-1) * 2 * (-2) = 4` cannot occur.
decls.title: Square-class independence for prime-discriminant families with at most one even factor
decls.statement:
theorem not_isSquare_prod_primeDiscriminantRadicands_of_forall_isEvenPrimeDiscriminant_eq
    {ι : Type*} (D : ι → ℤ) (hD : ∀ i, IsPrimeDiscriminant (D i))
    (hinj : Function.Injective D)
    (heven_unique : ∀ i j,
      IsEvenPrimeDiscriminant (D i) → IsEvenPrimeDiscriminant (D j) → D i = D j) :
    ∀ S : Finset ι, S.Nonempty →
      ¬ IsSquare (∏ i ∈ S, ((primeDiscriminantRadicand (D i) : ℤ) : ℚ))

decls.name: TauCeti.Multiquadratic.finrank_adjoin_roots_primeDiscriminantRadicands
decls.doc:
**Full degree for adjoining roots of prime-discriminant radicands.** Over any field `L ⊇ ℚ`
carrying square roots `root i` of the radicands of an injective family of prime discriminants not
containing all three even prime discriminants, the compositum `ℚ(root i : i)` has degree `2^|ι|`.
In a later genus-field specialization, the chosen roots will be identified with the genus-field
generators. This is the prime-discriminant instance of `finrank_adjoin_range`, fed the
square-class independence `not_isSquare_prod_primeDiscriminantRadicands`.
decls.title: Full degree for adjoining roots of prime-discriminant radicands
decls.statement:
theorem finrank_adjoin_roots_primeDiscriminantRadicands {ι : Type*} [Finite ι]
    {L : Type*} [Field L] [Algebra ℚ L] (D : ι → ℤ)
    (hD : ∀ i, IsPrimeDiscriminant (D i)) (hinj : Function.Injective D)
    (heven : ¬ ((∃ i, D i = -4) ∧ (∃ i, D i = 8) ∧ (∃ i, D i = -8)))
    (root : ι → L)
    (hroot : ∀ i, root i ^ 2 = algebraMap ℚ L ((primeDiscriminantRadicand (D i) : ℤ) : ℚ)) :
    Module.finrank ℚ (IntermediateField.adjoin ℚ (Set.range root)) = 2 ^ Nat.card ι

decls.name: TauCeti.Multiquadratic.finrank_adjoin_roots_primeDiscriminantRadicands_of_forall_isEvenPrimeDiscriminant_eq
decls.doc:
**Full degree for adjoining roots of prime-discriminant radicands with at most one even
factor.** If `D : ι → ℤ` is an injective finite family of prime discriminants with at most one
even member, then adjoining square roots of the associated radicands gives a multiquadratic field
of degree `2 ^ Nat.card ι`.

This is the degree theorem in the form needed for genus-field generator lists coming from prime
discriminants of a quadratic discriminant.
decls.statement:
theorem finrank_adjoin_roots_primeDiscriminantRadicands_of_forall_isEvenPrimeDiscriminant_eq
    {ι : Type*} [Finite ι] {L : Type*} [Field L] [Algebra ℚ L] (D : ι → ℤ)
    (hD : ∀ i, IsPrimeDiscriminant (D i)) (hinj : Function.Injective D)
    (heven_unique : ∀ i j,
      IsEvenPrimeDiscriminant (D i) → IsEvenPrimeDiscriminant (D j) → D i = D j)
    (root : ι → L)
    (hroot : ∀ i, root i ^ 2 = algebraMap ℚ L ((primeDiscriminantRadicand (D i) : ℤ) : ℚ)) :
    Module.finrank ℚ (IntermediateField.adjoin ℚ (Set.range root)) = 2 ^ Nat.card ι

decls.name: TauCeti.Multiquadratic.finrank_adjoin_range_over_prodRootMem_univ_of_primeDiscriminants
decls.doc:
**Relative degree of the prime-discriminant compositum over its `ℚ(√d)` base.** Let `D : ι → ℤ`
be a nonempty, injective family of prime discriminants with at most one even member (the shape
supplied by the prime-discriminant factorization of a quadratic discriminant), and let `root i` be
chosen square roots of their radicands in a field `L ⊇ ℚ`. Then the compositum
`M = ℚ(root i : i)` — the candidate genus field — has degree `2 ^ (|ι| - 1)` over the quadratic
subfield `ℚ(∏ᵢ root i)` generated by the product of all the roots.

That product root squares to `∏ᵢ radicand (D i)`; when the `D i` are the prime discriminants of the
fundamental discriminant of a squarefree `d` this product is `d`, so the base is the copy of
`ℚ(√d)` inside `M` and the statement is `[K_gen : ℚ(√d)] = 2 ^ (t - 1)`. This is the field-generic
form of `finrank_candidateGenusField_over_sqrtNegTwentyOneSubfield`.
decls.title: Relative degree of the prime-discriminant compositum over its `ℚ(√d)` base
decls.statement:
theorem finrank_adjoin_range_over_prodRootMem_univ_of_primeDiscriminants
    {ι : Type*} [Fintype ι] [Nonempty ι] {L : Type*} [Field L] [Algebra ℚ L]
    (D : ι → ℤ) (hD : ∀ i, IsPrimeDiscriminant (D i)) (hinj : Function.Injective D)
    (heven_unique : ∀ i j,
      IsEvenPrimeDiscriminant (D i) → IsEvenPrimeDiscriminant (D j) → D i = D j)
    (root : ι → L)
    (hroot : ∀ i, root i ^ 2 = algebraMap ℚ L ((primeDiscriminantRadicand (D i) : ℤ) : ℚ)) :
    Module.finrank
        (adjoin ℚ {prodRootMem (K := ℚ) root (Finset.univ : Finset ι)})
        (adjoin ℚ (Set.range root)) = 2 ^ (Nat.card ι - 1)

decls.name: TauCeti.NumberField.ncard_primesOver_primeDiscriminantRadicands_iff
decls.doc:
**Prime-discriminant-radicand multiquadratic splitting law.** Let `K` be generated over
`ℚ` by square roots of the radicands attached to a finite family of integers `D`. For an odd
prime `p` dividing none of the `D i`, `p` splits completely in `K` exactly when every `D i` is
a quadratic residue modulo `p`.
decls.title: Prime-discriminant-radicand multiquadratic splitting law
decls.statement:
theorem ncard_primesOver_primeDiscriminantRadicands_iff {ι : Type*} [Finite ι]
    (D : ι → ℤ) (r : ι → K)
    (hr : ∀ i, r i ^ 2 =
      algebraMap ℤ K (TauCeti.Multiquadratic.primeDiscriminantRadicand (D i)))
    (htop : IntermediateField.adjoin ℚ (Set.range r) = ⊤)
    {p : ℕ} [Fact p.Prime] (hodd : p ≠ 2) (hcop : ∀ i, ¬ (p : ℤ) ∣ D i) :
    (primesOver (span {(p : ℤ)}) (𝓞 K)).ncard = finrank ℚ K ↔
      ∀ i, legendreSym p (D i) = 1

decls.name: TauCeti.NumberField.ncard_primesOver_primeDiscriminantRadicands_iff_congruences
decls.doc:
**Prime-discriminant-radicand multiquadratic splitting law, congruence form.** Let `K`
be generated over `ℚ` by square roots of the radicands attached to a finite family of prime
discriminants `D`. For an odd prime `p` dividing none of the `D i`, `p` splits completely in
`K` exactly when each even prime discriminant satisfies the corresponding supplementary
congruence condition, and each odd prime discriminant satisfies the reciprocal Legendre-symbol
condition.
decls.title: Prime-discriminant-radicand multiquadratic splitting law, congruence form
decls.statement:
theorem ncard_primesOver_primeDiscriminantRadicands_iff_congruences {ι : Type*} [Finite ι]
    (D : ι → ℤ) (hD : ∀ i, TauCeti.Multiquadratic.IsPrimeDiscriminant (D i)) (r : ι → K)
    (hr : ∀ i, r i ^ 2 =
      algebraMap ℤ K (TauCeti.Multiquadratic.primeDiscriminantRadicand (D i)))
    (htop : IntermediateField.adjoin ℚ (Set.range r) = ⊤)
    {p : ℕ} [Fact p.Prime] (hodd : p ≠ 2) (hcop : ∀ i, ¬ (p : ℤ) ∣ D i) :
    (primesOver (span {(p : ℤ)}) (𝓞 K)).ncard = finrank ℚ K ↔
      ∀ i,
        (TauCeti.Multiquadratic.IsEvenPrimeDiscriminant (D i) ∧
          (if D i = -4 then p % 4 = 1
          else if D i = 8 then p % 8 = 1 ∨ p % 8 = 7
          else p % 8 = 1 ∨ p % 8 = 3)) ∨
        ∃ q : ℕ, ∃ hq : q.Prime, Odd q ∧
          D i = TauCeti.Multiquadratic.oddPrimeDiscriminant q ∧
          @legendreSym q ⟨hq⟩ (p : ℤ) = 1

decls.name: TauCeti.Multiquadratic.intermediateFieldEquivSubmodulePrimeDiscriminantRadicands
decls.doc:
**The subfield lattice from prime-discriminant radicands.** For an injective family of prime
discriminants not containing the dependent even triple `-4`, `8`, and `-8`, the intermediate
fields of the multiquadratic extension generated by roots of `primeDiscriminantRadicand (D i)`
correspond, order-reversingly, to the `𝔽₂`-subspaces of `ι → ℤ/2`.
decls.title: The subfield lattice from prime-discriminant radicands

decls.name: TauCeti.Multiquadratic.mem_intermediateFieldEquivSubmodulePrimeDiscriminantRadicands_apply_ofDual_iff
decls.doc:
A sign vector belongs to the subspace attached to an intermediate field of a
prime-discriminant multiquadratic field exactly when it is the sign pattern of an automorphism
fixing that field.
decls.statement:
theorem mem_intermediateFieldEquivSubmodulePrimeDiscriminantRadicands_apply_ofDual_iff
    (F : IntermediateField ℚ (adjoin ℚ (Set.range root))) (v : ι → ZMod 2) :
    v ∈ (intermediateFieldEquivSubmodulePrimeDiscriminantRadicands
        D hD hinj heven root hroot F).ofDual ↔
      ∃ σ ∈ F.fixingSubgroup, signPattern root σ = v

decls.name: TauCeti.Multiquadratic.mem_intermediateFieldEquivSubmodulePrimeDiscriminantRadicands_symm_apply_iff
decls.doc:
The intermediate field attached to a subspace in the prime-discriminant dictionary is the
fixed field of the automorphisms whose sign patterns lie in that subspace.
decls.statement:
theorem mem_intermediateFieldEquivSubmodulePrimeDiscriminantRadicands_symm_apply_iff
    (U : Submodule (ZMod 2) (ι → ZMod 2)) (x : adjoin ℚ (Set.range root)) :
    x ∈ (intermediateFieldEquivSubmodulePrimeDiscriminantRadicands
        D hD hinj heven root hroot).symm (OrderDual.toDual U) ↔
      ∀ σ, signPattern root σ ∈ U → σ x = x

decls.name: TauCeti.Multiquadratic.card_intermediateField_adjoin_roots_primeDiscriminantRadicands
decls.doc:
**The number of subfields from prime-discriminant radicands.** Under the prime-discriminant
independence hypotheses, the intermediate fields are counted by the `𝔽₂`-subspaces of
`ι → ℤ/2`.
decls.title: The number of subfields from prime-discriminant radicands
decls.statement:
theorem card_intermediateField_adjoin_roots_primeDiscriminantRadicands :
    Nat.card (IntermediateField ℚ (adjoin ℚ (Set.range root)))
      = Nat.card (Submodule (ZMod 2) (ι → ZMod 2))

decls.name: TauCeti.Multiquadratic.finrank_mul_card_intermediateFieldEquivSubmodulePrimeDiscriminantRadicands
decls.doc:
**Degree/subspace-size relation in prime-discriminant form.** For an intermediate field `F`
of a prime-discriminant multiquadratic field, `[F : ℚ]` times the size of its attached subspace is
`2 ^ |ι|`.
decls.title: Degree/subspace-size relation in prime-discriminant form
decls.statement:
theorem finrank_mul_card_intermediateFieldEquivSubmodulePrimeDiscriminantRadicands
    (F : IntermediateField ℚ (adjoin ℚ (Set.range root))) :
    Module.finrank ℚ F
        * Nat.card (intermediateFieldEquivSubmodulePrimeDiscriminantRadicands
          D hD hinj heven root hroot F).ofDual
      = 2 ^ Nat.card ι

decls.name: TauCeti.Multiquadratic.finrank_intermediateField_primeDiscriminantRadicands_eq_two_pow
decls.doc:
**Degree of a prime-discriminant intermediate field.** The degree of an intermediate field
is `2` to the codimension of its attached subspace.
decls.title: Degree of a prime-discriminant intermediate field
decls.statement:
theorem finrank_intermediateField_primeDiscriminantRadicands_eq_two_pow
    (F : IntermediateField ℚ (adjoin ℚ (Set.range root))) :
    Module.finrank ℚ F =
      2 ^ (Nat.card ι - Module.finrank (ZMod 2)
        (intermediateFieldEquivSubmodulePrimeDiscriminantRadicands
          D hD hinj heven root hroot F).ofDual)

decls.name: TauCeti.Multiquadratic.finrank_intermediateField_primeDiscriminantRadicands_eq_two_iff
decls.doc:
**Quadratic subfields in prime-discriminant form.** An intermediate field has degree `2`
exactly when its attached subspace is a hyperplane.
decls.title: Quadratic subfields in prime-discriminant form
decls.statement:
theorem finrank_intermediateField_primeDiscriminantRadicands_eq_two_iff
    (F : IntermediateField ℚ (adjoin ℚ (Set.range root))) :
    Module.finrank ℚ F = 2 ↔
      Module.finrank (ZMod 2)
          (intermediateFieldEquivSubmodulePrimeDiscriminantRadicands
            D hD hinj heven root hroot F).ofDual + 1 = Nat.card ι

decls.name: TauCeti.Multiquadratic.IsPrimeDiscriminant
decls.doc:
The prime discriminants: the even prime discriminants `-4`, `8`, `-8`, together with
the odd prime discriminants `p*` for odd natural primes `p`.
decls.statement: def IsPrimeDiscriminant (D : ℤ) : Prop

decls.name: TauCeti.Multiquadratic.isPrimeDiscriminant_iff
decls.doc: The defining disjunction for `IsPrimeDiscriminant`.
decls.statement:
theorem isPrimeDiscriminant_iff {D : ℤ} :
    IsPrimeDiscriminant D ↔
      IsEvenPrimeDiscriminant D ∨ ∃ p : ℕ, p.Prime ∧ Odd p ∧ D = oddPrimeDiscriminant p

decls.name: TauCeti.Multiquadratic.IsEvenPrimeDiscriminant.isPrimeDiscriminant
decls.doc: Every even prime discriminant is a prime discriminant.

decls.name: TauCeti.Multiquadratic.isPrimeDiscriminant_neg_four
decls.doc: The discriminant `-4` is a prime discriminant.
decls.statement:
theorem isPrimeDiscriminant_neg_four :
    IsPrimeDiscriminant (-4)

decls.name: TauCeti.Multiquadratic.isPrimeDiscriminant_eight
decls.doc: The discriminant `8` is a prime discriminant.
decls.statement:
theorem isPrimeDiscriminant_eight :
    IsPrimeDiscriminant 8

decls.name: TauCeti.Multiquadratic.isPrimeDiscriminant_neg_eight
decls.doc: The discriminant `-8` is a prime discriminant.
decls.statement:
theorem isPrimeDiscriminant_neg_eight :
    IsPrimeDiscriminant (-8)

decls.name: TauCeti.Multiquadratic.isPrimeDiscriminant_oddPrimeDiscriminant
decls.doc: The odd prime discriminant attached to an odd natural prime is a prime discriminant.
decls.statement:
theorem isPrimeDiscriminant_oddPrimeDiscriminant {p : ℕ} (hp : p.Prime) (hodd : Odd p) :
    IsPrimeDiscriminant (oddPrimeDiscriminant p)

decls.name: TauCeti.Multiquadratic.not_isEvenPrimeDiscriminant_oddPrimeDiscriminant
decls.doc: An odd prime discriminant is not one of the even prime discriminants.

decls.name: TauCeti.Multiquadratic.primeDiscriminantRadicand
decls.doc:
The squarefree radicand attached to a prime discriminant. In the even cases this divides by
`4`; in the odd cases the discriminant is already squarefree and is used as its own radicand.
decls.statement: def primeDiscriminantRadicand (D : ℤ) : ℤ

decls.name: TauCeti.Multiquadratic.primeDiscriminantRadicand_def
decls.doc: The defining equation for the prime-discriminant radicand.
decls.statement:
theorem primeDiscriminantRadicand_def (D : ℤ) :
    primeDiscriminantRadicand D =
      if D = -4 ∨ D = 8 ∨ D = -8 then evenPrimeDiscriminantRadicand D else D

decls.name: TauCeti.Multiquadratic.primeDiscriminantRadicand_neg_four
decls.doc: The prime-discriminant radicand of `-4` is `-1`.
decls.statement:
theorem primeDiscriminantRadicand_neg_four :
    primeDiscriminantRadicand (-4) = -1

decls.name: TauCeti.Multiquadratic.primeDiscriminantRadicand_eight
decls.doc: The prime-discriminant radicand of `8` is `2`.
decls.statement:
theorem primeDiscriminantRadicand_eight :
    primeDiscriminantRadicand 8 = 2

decls.name: TauCeti.Multiquadratic.primeDiscriminantRadicand_neg_eight
decls.doc: The prime-discriminant radicand of `-8` is `-2`.
decls.statement:
theorem primeDiscriminantRadicand_neg_eight :
    primeDiscriminantRadicand (-8) = -2

decls.name: TauCeti.Multiquadratic.primeDiscriminantRadicand_of_isEvenPrimeDiscriminant
decls.doc: The radicand attached to an even prime discriminant is its even-prime radicand.

decls.name: TauCeti.Multiquadratic.primeDiscriminantRadicand_oddPrimeDiscriminant
decls.doc: The radicand attached to an odd prime discriminant is the discriminant itself.

decls.name: TauCeti.Multiquadratic.primeDiscriminant_eq_radicand_or_eq_four_mul_radicand
decls.doc:
A prime discriminant is either its own radicand, or four times its radicand in the even
cases.

decls.name: TauCeti.Multiquadratic.dvd_primeDiscriminant_iff_dvd_radicand
decls.doc:
Away from `2`, divisibility of an integer is the same as divisibility of its associated
prime-discriminant radicand. In the even-prime cases the two differ by the square factor
`4`; in all other cases they are equal. Not a `simp` lemma: the right-hand side is again of
the form `(q : ℤ) ∣ _`, so as a rewrite rule it matches its own output and loops.
decls.statement:
theorem dvd_primeDiscriminant_iff_dvd_radicand (D : ℤ) (hq : q ≠ 2) :
    (q : ℤ) ∣ D ↔ (q : ℤ) ∣ primeDiscriminantRadicand D

decls.name: TauCeti.Multiquadratic.forall_not_dvd_primeDiscriminant_iff_radicand
decls.doc:
Away from `2`, an indexed family of integers and its associated prime-discriminant
radicands have the same unramifiedness condition at `q`.
decls.statement:
theorem forall_not_dvd_primeDiscriminant_iff_radicand {ι : Type*} (D : ι → ℤ)
    (hq : q ≠ 2) :
    (∀ i, ¬ (q : ℤ) ∣ D i) ↔
      ∀ i, ¬ (q : ℤ) ∣ primeDiscriminantRadicand (D i)

decls.name: TauCeti.Multiquadratic.primeDiscriminantRadicand_ne_zero
decls.doc: The radicand attached to a prime discriminant is nonzero.

decls.name: TauCeti.Multiquadratic.squarefree_primeDiscriminantRadicand
decls.doc: The radicand attached to a prime discriminant is squarefree.

decls.name: TauCeti.Multiquadratic.not_isSquare_primeDiscriminantRadicand_rat
decls.doc: The radicand attached to a prime discriminant is not a rational square.

decls.name: TauCeti.Multiquadratic.primeDiscriminantRadicand_mod_four_eq_one_of_odd
decls.doc: An odd prime discriminant has odd radicand congruent to `1` modulo `4`.

decls.name: TauCeti.Multiquadratic.primeDiscriminantRadicand_mod_four_eq_three_or_two_of_even
decls.doc: An even prime discriminant has radicand congruent to `3` or `2` modulo `4`.

decls.name: TauCeti.Multiquadratic.isEvenPrimeDiscriminant_or_primeDiscriminantRadicand_mod_four_eq_one
decls.doc:
A prime discriminant is either even, or its associated radicand is congruent to `1`
modulo `4`.

decls.name: TauCeti.Multiquadratic.primeDiscriminantRadicand_natAbs_eq_one_iff
decls.doc:
The only prime discriminant whose radicand has absolute value `1` is `-4`. This is the
small exceptional case in the radicand map: the odd prime-discriminant radicands have prime
absolute value, and the other even prime-discriminant radicands have absolute value `2`.

decls.name: TauCeti.Multiquadratic.primeDiscriminantRadicand_eq_neg_one_iff
decls.doc:
Among prime discriminants, radicand `-1` comes only from the even prime discriminant
`-4`.

decls.name: TauCeti.Multiquadratic.primeDiscriminantRadicand_eq_two_iff
decls.doc: Among prime discriminants, radicand `2` comes only from the even prime discriminant `8`.

decls.name: TauCeti.Multiquadratic.primeDiscriminantRadicand_eq_neg_two_iff
decls.doc:
Among prime discriminants, radicand `-2` comes only from the even prime discriminant
`-8`.

decls.name: TauCeti.Multiquadratic.eq_of_primeDiscriminantRadicand_eq
decls.doc:
The radicand map is injective on prime discriminants. This is the bookkeeping that lets
later genus-field code pass between a list of prime discriminants and the corresponding
multiquadratic radicands without identifying two different quadratic factors.
decls.statement:
theorem eq_of_primeDiscriminantRadicand_eq {D E : ℤ}
    (hD : IsPrimeDiscriminant D) (hE : IsPrimeDiscriminant E)
    (h : primeDiscriminantRadicand D = primeDiscriminantRadicand E) :
    D = E

decls.name: TauCeti.Multiquadratic.injOn_primeDiscriminantRadicand
decls.doc: `primeDiscriminantRadicand` is injective on the set of prime discriminants.
decls.statement:
theorem injOn_primeDiscriminantRadicand :
    Set.InjOn primeDiscriminantRadicand {D : ℤ | IsPrimeDiscriminant D}

decls.name: TauCeti.Multiquadratic.injective_primeDiscriminantRadicand_comp_iff
decls.doc:
For a family of prime discriminants, injectivity is unchanged after replacing each
discriminant by its multiquadratic radicand.
decls.statement:
theorem injective_primeDiscriminantRadicand_comp_iff {ι : Type*} {D : ι → ℤ}
    (hD : ∀ i, IsPrimeDiscriminant (D i)) :
    Function.Injective (fun i => primeDiscriminantRadicand (D i)) ↔
      Function.Injective D

decls.name: TauCeti.Multiquadratic.galoisGroupEquivSqrtPrimes
decls.doc:
**The Galois group of a prime-radicand multiquadratic field is `(ℤ/2)ⁿ`.** For a finite family
of distinct primes `p : ι → ℕ`, the field generated over `ℚ` by their real square roots has Galois
group isomorphic to `Multiplicative (ι → ℤ/2)`. This is the prime-indexed corollary of the
field-generic isomorphism `galoisGroupEquiv`.
decls.title: The Galois group of a prime-radicand multiquadratic field is `(ℤ/2)ⁿ`
decls.statement:
def galoisGroupEquivSqrtPrimes :
    (adjoin ℚ (Set.range fun i => (Real.sqrt (p i) : ℝ)) ≃ₐ[ℚ]
        adjoin ℚ (Set.range fun i => (Real.sqrt (p i) : ℝ))) ≃*
      Multiplicative (ι → ZMod 2)

decls.name: TauCeti.Multiquadratic.galoisGroupEquivSqrtPrimes_apply
decls.doc:
The prime-radicand Galois equivalence sends an automorphism to its sign pattern on the
generators `√(p i)`.
decls.statement:
theorem galoisGroupEquivSqrtPrimes_apply
    (σ : adjoin ℚ (Set.range fun i => (Real.sqrt (p i) : ℝ)) ≃ₐ[ℚ]
        adjoin ℚ (Set.range fun i => (Real.sqrt (p i) : ℝ))) :
    galoisGroupEquivSqrtPrimes p hp hinj σ =
      Multiplicative.ofAdd (signPattern (fun i => (Real.sqrt (p i) : ℝ)) σ)

decls.name: TauCeti.Multiquadratic.galoisGroupEquivSqrtPrimes_symm_apply_gen
decls.doc:
The inverse prime-radicand Galois equivalence realizes a sign pattern by sending each
generator `√(p i)` to `(-1)^(ε i) · √(p i)`.
decls.statement:
theorem galoisGroupEquivSqrtPrimes_symm_apply_gen (ε : ι → ZMod 2) (i : ι) :
    ((galoisGroupEquivSqrtPrimes p hp hinj).symm (Multiplicative.ofAdd ε))
        (gen (fun i => (Real.sqrt (p i) : ℝ)) i)
      = (-1) ^ (ε i).val * gen (fun i => (Real.sqrt (p i) : ℝ)) i

decls.name: TauCeti.Multiquadratic.card_aut_adjoin_sqrt_primes
decls.doc:
**Cardinality of the Galois group of a prime-radicand multiquadratic field.** For a finite
family of distinct primes `p : ι → ℕ`, `|Gal(ℚ(√p₁, …, √pₙ)/ℚ)| = 2^|ι|`.
decls.title: Cardinality of the Galois group of a prime-radicand multiquadratic field
decls.statement:
theorem card_aut_adjoin_sqrt_primes :
    Nat.card (adjoin ℚ (Set.range fun i => (Real.sqrt (p i) : ℝ)) ≃ₐ[ℚ]
        adjoin ℚ (Set.range fun i => (Real.sqrt (p i) : ℝ))) = 2 ^ Nat.card ι

decls.name: TauCeti.Multiquadratic.card_aut_adjoin_sqrt_two_three
decls.doc:
**Worked example: `|Gal(ℚ(√2, √3)/ℚ)| = 4`.** The two-prime field obtained from
`card_aut_adjoin_sqrt_primes` with the primes `2` and `3`.
decls.title: Worked example: `|Gal(ℚ(√2, √3)/ℚ)| = 4`
decls.statement:
theorem card_aut_adjoin_sqrt_two_three :
    Nat.card ((adjoin ℚ {Real.sqrt 2, Real.sqrt 3} : IntermediateField ℚ ℝ) ≃ₐ[ℚ]
        (adjoin ℚ {Real.sqrt 2, Real.sqrt 3} : IntermediateField ℚ ℝ)) = 4

decls.name: TauCeti.NumberField.forall_not_intCast_prime_dvd_natPrimes
decls.doc:
A rational prime `q` different from every prime in a family `p` divides none of the
corresponding integer radicands.
decls.statement:
theorem forall_not_intCast_prime_dvd_natPrimes {ι : Type*} (p : ι → ℕ)
    (hp : ∀ i, (p i).Prime) {q : ℕ} [Fact q.Prime] (hne : ∀ i, q ≠ p i) :
    ∀ i, ¬ (q : ℤ) ∣ (p i : ℤ)

decls.name: TauCeti.NumberField.ncard_primesOver_sqrt_primes_iff
decls.doc:
**Prime-radicand multiquadratic splitting law.** Let `K` be generated over `ℚ` by square
roots of a finite family of rational primes `p i`. If `q` is an odd rational prime distinct from
every `p i`, then `q` splits completely in `K` exactly when every `p i` is a quadratic residue
modulo `q`.
decls.title: Prime-radicand multiquadratic splitting law
decls.statement:
theorem ncard_primesOver_sqrt_primes_iff {ι : Type*} [Finite ι] (p : ι → ℕ)
    (hp : ∀ i, (p i).Prime) (r : ι → K)
    (hr : ∀ i, r i ^ 2 = algebraMap ℤ K (p i : ℤ))
    (htop : IntermediateField.adjoin ℚ (Set.range r) = ⊤)
    {q : ℕ} [Fact q.Prime] (hodd : q ≠ 2) (hne : ∀ i, q ≠ p i) :
    (primesOver (span {(q : ℤ)}) (𝓞 K)).ncard = finrank ℚ K ↔
      ∀ i, legendreSym q (p i : ℤ) = 1

decls.name: TauCeti.NumberField.forall_legendreSym_two_three_eq_one_iff_mod_eight
decls.doc:
The character condition for the radicands `2` and `3`, with the `√2` condition expanded
using the supplementary law for `2`.
decls.statement:
theorem forall_legendreSym_two_three_eq_one_iff_mod_eight {q : ℕ} [Fact q.Prime]
    (htwo : q ≠ 2) :
    (∀ i : Fin 2, legendreSym q ((![2, 3] : Fin 2 → ℕ) i : ℤ) = 1) ↔
      (q % 8 = 1 ∨ q % 8 = 7) ∧ legendreSym q (3 : ℤ) = 1

decls.name: TauCeti.NumberField.ncard_primesOver_sqrt_two_three_iff
decls.doc:
**Complete splitting for `ℚ(√2, √3)`.** Let `K` be generated over `ℚ` by square roots of
`2` and `3`. A rational prime `q` different from `2` and `3` splits completely in `K` exactly
when both `2` and `3` are quadratic residues modulo `q`.
decls.title: Complete splitting for `ℚ(√2, √3)`
decls.statement:
theorem ncard_primesOver_sqrt_two_three_iff (r : Fin 2 → K)
    (hr : ∀ i, r i ^ 2 = algebraMap ℤ K ((![2, 3] : Fin 2 → ℕ) i : ℤ))
    (htop : IntermediateField.adjoin ℚ (Set.range r) = ⊤)
    {q : ℕ} [Fact q.Prime] (htwo : q ≠ 2) (hthree : q ≠ 3) :
    (primesOver (span {(q : ℤ)}) (𝓞 K)).ncard = finrank ℚ K ↔
      legendreSym q (2 : ℤ) = 1 ∧ legendreSym q (3 : ℤ) = 1

decls.name: TauCeti.NumberField.ncard_primesOver_sqrt_two_three_iff_mod_eight
decls.doc:
**Complete splitting for `ℚ(√2, √3)`, with the `√2` character expanded.** Let `K` be
generated over `ℚ` by square roots of `2` and `3`. A rational prime `q` different from `2` and
`3` splits completely in `K` exactly when `q ≡ 1` or `7` modulo `8` and `3` is a quadratic
residue modulo `q`.
decls.title: Complete splitting for `ℚ(√2, √3)`, with the `√2` character expanded
decls.statement:
theorem ncard_primesOver_sqrt_two_three_iff_mod_eight (r : Fin 2 → K)
    (hr : ∀ i, r i ^ 2 = algebraMap ℤ K ((![2, 3] : Fin 2 → ℕ) i : ℤ))
    (htop : IntermediateField.adjoin ℚ (Set.range r) = ⊤)
    {q : ℕ} [Fact q.Prime] (htwo : q ≠ 2) (hthree : q ≠ 3) :
    (primesOver (span {(q : ℤ)}) (𝓞 K)).ncard = finrank ℚ K ↔
      (q % 8 = 1 ∨ q % 8 = 7) ∧ legendreSym q (3 : ℤ) = 1

decls.name: TauCeti.Multiquadratic.not_isSquare_prod_primes
decls.doc:
**Square-class independence of distinct primes.** If the selected `p i` are prime and pairwise
distinct, then no nonempty subset product `∏_{i ∈ S} (p i : ℚ)` is a square in `ℚ`. This is the
hypothesis the multiquadratic degree theorem `finrank_adjoin_range` consumes.
decls.title: Square-class independence of distinct primes
decls.statement:
theorem not_isSquare_prod_primes {ι : Type*} (p : ι → ℕ) {S : Finset ι}
    (hp : ∀ i ∈ S, (p i).Prime)
    (hdist : Set.Pairwise (S : Set ι) (fun i j => p i ≠ p j))
    (hS : S.Nonempty) :
    ¬ IsSquare (∏ i ∈ S, (p i : ℚ))

decls.name: TauCeti.Multiquadratic.sq_sqrt_natCast
decls.doc:
The real square root of a natural number squares back to its rational value, in the form
`(√n)² = algebraMap ℚ ℝ n`. This supplies the `hroot` hypothesis that the multiquadratic degree and
Galois-group theorems consume for the family of square roots of a prime family. It is the `0 ≤ n`
special case of `sq_sqrt_intCast`.
decls.statement:
theorem sq_sqrt_natCast (n : ℕ) :
    (Real.sqrt n) ^ 2 = algebraMap ℚ ℝ (n : ℚ)

decls.name: TauCeti.Multiquadratic.not_isSquare_prod_primes_of_injective
decls.doc:
**Square-class independence of an injective family of primes.** If `p : ι → ℕ` is injective and
each `p i` is prime, then no nonempty subset product `∏_{i ∈ S} (p i : ℚ)` is a square. This is the
`hindep` hypothesis the multiquadratic degree and Galois-group theorems consume directly.
decls.title: Square-class independence of an injective family of primes
decls.statement:
theorem not_isSquare_prod_primes_of_injective {ι : Type*} (p : ι → ℕ)
    (hp : ∀ i, (p i).Prime) (hinj : Function.Injective p) :
    ∀ S : Finset ι, S.Nonempty → ¬ IsSquare (∏ i ∈ S, (p i : ℚ))

decls.name: TauCeti.Multiquadratic.finrank_adjoin_sqrt_primes
decls.doc:
**Degree of a prime-radicand multiquadratic field.** For a finite family of distinct primes
`p : ι → ℕ`, the field generated over `ℚ` by their real square roots has degree `2^|ι|`. This is the
prime-indexed corollary of the field-generic degree theorem `finrank_adjoin_range`.
decls.title: Degree of a prime-radicand multiquadratic field
decls.statement:
theorem finrank_adjoin_sqrt_primes {ι : Type*} [Finite ι] (p : ι → ℕ)
    (hp : ∀ i, (p i).Prime) (hinj : Function.Injective p) :
    Module.finrank ℚ
        (IntermediateField.adjoin ℚ (Set.range fun i => (Real.sqrt (p i) : ℝ)))
      = 2 ^ Nat.card ι

decls.name: TauCeti.Multiquadratic.finrank_adjoin_sqrt_two_three
decls.doc:
**Worked example: `[ℚ(√2, √3) : ℚ] = 4`.** The smallest nontrivial multiquadratic degree,
obtained from `finrank_adjoin_sqrt_primes` with the primes `2` and `3`.
decls.title: Worked example: `[ℚ(√2, √3) : ℚ] = 4`
decls.statement:
theorem finrank_adjoin_sqrt_two_three :
    Module.finrank ℚ
      (IntermediateField.adjoin ℚ {Real.sqrt 2, Real.sqrt 3} : IntermediateField ℚ ℝ) = 4

decls.name: TauCeti.Multiquadratic.card_quadratic_intermediateField_adjoin_sqrt_primes
decls.doc:
**The number of quadratic subfields of `ℚ(√p₁, …, √pₙ)` is `2ⁿ - 1`.** For a finite family of
distinct primes `p : ι → ℕ`, the multiquadratic field `ℚ(√p₁, …, √pₙ)`, of degree `2 ^ |ι|` over
`ℚ`, has exactly `2 ^ |ι| - 1` intermediate fields of degree `2` over `ℚ`. This is the
prime-radicand specialization of `card_quadratic_intermediateField_adjoin_range`.
decls.title: The number of quadratic subfields of `ℚ(√p₁, …, √pₙ)` is `2ⁿ - 1`
decls.statement:
theorem card_quadratic_intermediateField_adjoin_sqrt_primes [Finite ι] (p : ι → ℕ)
    (hp : ∀ i, (p i).Prime) (hinj : Function.Injective p) :
    Nat.card {F : IntermediateField ℚ (adjoin ℚ (Set.range fun i => (Real.sqrt (p i) : ℝ))) //
        Module.finrank ℚ F = 2} = 2 ^ Nat.card ι - 1

decls.name: TauCeti.Multiquadratic.intermediateFieldEquivSubmoduleSqrtPrimes_apply_ofDual_eq
decls.doc:
The subspace attached by the public prime-radicand dictionary is extensionally the same as
the generic dictionary fed the prime-family square-class independence proof. This lets consumers
use the degree theorems from `SubfieldDegree` with
`intermediateFieldEquivSubmoduleSqrtPrimes` without a parallel prime-specific degree API.
decls.statement:
theorem intermediateFieldEquivSubmoduleSqrtPrimes_apply_ofDual_eq
    (F : IntermediateField ℚ (adjoin ℚ (Set.range fun i => (Real.sqrt (p i) : ℝ)))) :
    (intermediateFieldEquivSubmoduleSqrtPrimes p hp hinj F).ofDual =
      (intermediateFieldEquivSubmodule (fun i => sq_sqrt_natCast (p i))
        (not_isSquare_prod_primes_of_injective p hp hinj) F).ofDual

decls.name: TauCeti.Multiquadratic.finrank_mul_card_intermediateFieldEquivSubmoduleSqrtPrimes
decls.doc:
**Degree/subspace-size relation for `ℚ(√p₁, …, √pₙ)`.** For an intermediate field `F`
of a prime-radicand multiquadratic field, `[F : ℚ]` times the size of its attached subspace is
`2 ^ |ι|`.
decls.title: Degree/subspace-size relation for `ℚ(√p₁, …, √pₙ)`
decls.statement:
theorem finrank_mul_card_intermediateFieldEquivSubmoduleSqrtPrimes
    (F : IntermediateField ℚ (adjoin ℚ (Set.range fun i => (Real.sqrt (p i) : ℝ)))) :
    Module.finrank ℚ F
        * Nat.card (intermediateFieldEquivSubmoduleSqrtPrimes p hp hinj F).ofDual
      = 2 ^ Nat.card ι

decls.name: TauCeti.Multiquadratic.finrank_intermediateField_sqrtPrimes_eq_two_pow
decls.doc:
**Degree of a prime-radicand intermediate field.** The degree of an intermediate field of
`ℚ(√p₁, …, √pₙ)` is `2` to the codimension of its attached prime-radicand subspace.
decls.title: Degree of a prime-radicand intermediate field
decls.statement:
theorem finrank_intermediateField_sqrtPrimes_eq_two_pow
    (F : IntermediateField ℚ (adjoin ℚ (Set.range fun i => (Real.sqrt (p i) : ℝ)))) :
    Module.finrank ℚ F =
      2 ^ (Nat.card ι - Module.finrank (ZMod 2)
        (intermediateFieldEquivSubmoduleSqrtPrimes p hp hinj F).ofDual)

decls.name: TauCeti.Multiquadratic.finrank_intermediateField_sqrtPrimes_eq_two_iff
decls.doc:
**Quadratic subfields of `ℚ(√p₁, …, √pₙ)`.** An intermediate field has degree `2` exactly
when its attached prime-radicand subspace is a hyperplane.
decls.title: Quadratic subfields of `ℚ(√p₁, …, √pₙ)`
decls.statement:
theorem finrank_intermediateField_sqrtPrimes_eq_two_iff
    (F : IntermediateField ℚ (adjoin ℚ (Set.range fun i => (Real.sqrt (p i) : ℝ)))) :
    Module.finrank ℚ F = 2 ↔
      Module.finrank (ZMod 2)
          (intermediateFieldEquivSubmoduleSqrtPrimes p hp hinj F).ofDual + 1 = Nat.card ι

decls.name: TauCeti.Multiquadratic.intermediateFieldEquivSubmoduleSqrtPrimes
decls.doc:
**The subfield lattice of `ℚ(√p₁, …, √pₙ)`.** For a finite family of distinct primes
`p : ι → ℕ`, the intermediate fields of `ℚ(√p₁, …, √pₙ)/ℚ` correspond, order-reversingly, to the
`𝔽₂`-subspaces of `ι → ℤ/2`. This is the prime-radicand specialization of
`intermediateFieldEquivSubmodule`, a genus-theory input.
decls.title: The subfield lattice of `ℚ(√p₁, …, √pₙ)`

decls.name: TauCeti.Multiquadratic.mem_intermediateFieldEquivSubmoduleSqrtPrimes_apply_ofDual_iff
decls.doc:
A sign vector belongs to the subspace attached to an intermediate field of
`ℚ(√p₁, …, √pₙ)` exactly when it is the sign pattern of an automorphism fixing that field.
decls.statement:
theorem mem_intermediateFieldEquivSubmoduleSqrtPrimes_apply_ofDual_iff
    (F : IntermediateField ℚ (adjoin ℚ (Set.range fun i => (Real.sqrt (p i) : ℝ))))
    (v : ι → ZMod 2) :
    v ∈ (intermediateFieldEquivSubmoduleSqrtPrimes p hp hinj F).ofDual ↔
      ∃ σ ∈ F.fixingSubgroup, signPattern (fun i => (Real.sqrt (p i) : ℝ)) σ = v

decls.name: TauCeti.Multiquadratic.mem_intermediateFieldEquivSubmoduleSqrtPrimes_symm_apply_iff
decls.doc:
The intermediate field attached to a subspace in the prime-radicand dictionary is the fixed
field of the automorphisms whose sign patterns lie in that subspace.
decls.statement:
theorem mem_intermediateFieldEquivSubmoduleSqrtPrimes_symm_apply_iff
    (U : Submodule (ZMod 2) (ι → ZMod 2))
    (x : adjoin ℚ (Set.range fun i => (Real.sqrt (p i) : ℝ))) :
    x ∈ (intermediateFieldEquivSubmoduleSqrtPrimes p hp hinj).symm (OrderDual.toDual U) ↔
      ∀ σ, signPattern (fun i => (Real.sqrt (p i) : ℝ)) σ ∈ U → σ x = x

decls.name: TauCeti.Multiquadratic.card_intermediateField_adjoin_sqrt_primes
decls.doc:
**The number of subfields of `ℚ(√p₁, …, √pₙ)`.** For a finite family of distinct primes, the
intermediate fields of `ℚ(√p₁, …, √pₙ)/ℚ` are in bijection with the `𝔽₂`-subspaces of `ι → ℤ/2`.
decls.title: The number of subfields of `ℚ(√p₁, …, √pₙ)`
decls.statement:
theorem card_intermediateField_adjoin_sqrt_primes :
    Nat.card (IntermediateField ℚ (adjoin ℚ (Set.range fun i => (Real.sqrt (p i) : ℝ))))
      = Nat.card (Submodule (ZMod 2) (ι → ZMod 2))

decls.name: TauCeti.Multiquadratic.prod_root_sq
decls.doc:
**The square of a subset-product root.** The product `∏_{i ∈ S} root i` of the chosen roots
over a finite subset `S` squares to the subset product `∏_{i ∈ S} d i` of the radicands.
decls.title: The square of a subset-product root
decls.statement:
theorem prod_root_sq (hroot : ∀ i, root i ^ 2 = algebraMap K L (d i)) (S : Finset ι) :
    (∏ i ∈ S, root i) ^ 2 = algebraMap K L (∏ i ∈ S, d i)

decls.name: TauCeti.Multiquadratic.prod_root_mem_adjoin
decls.doc:
**A subset-product root lies in the multiquadratic field.** Each `∏_{i ∈ S} root i` is a
product of generators of `M = K(rootᵢ : i)`, hence a member of `M`.
decls.title: A subset-product root lies in the multiquadratic field
decls.statement:
theorem prod_root_mem_adjoin (S : Finset ι) :
    (∏ i ∈ S, root i) ∈ IntermediateField.adjoin K (Set.range root)

decls.name: TauCeti.Multiquadratic.prod_root_notMem_bot
decls.doc:
**A subset-product root whose radicand product is not a square lies outside `K`.** If
`∏_{i ∈ S} root i` were in `⊥`, its square `∏_{i ∈ S} d i` would be a square in `K`.
decls.title: A subset-product root whose radicand product is not a square lies outside `K`
decls.statement:
theorem prod_root_notMem_bot (hroot : ∀ i, root i ^ 2 = algebraMap K L (d i))
    {S : Finset ι} (hSsq : ¬ IsSquare (∏ i ∈ S, d i)) :
    (∏ i ∈ S, root i) ∉ (⊥ : IntermediateField K L)

decls.name: TauCeti.Multiquadratic.finrank_adjoin_prod_root
decls.doc:
**A nonempty subset-product root generates a quadratic subfield.** When the subset product
`∏_{i ∈ S} d i` of the radicands is not a square, the subset-product root of `S` lies outside `K`
yet squares into `K`, so `[K(∏_{i ∈ S} root i) : K] = 2`.
decls.title: A nonempty subset-product root generates a quadratic subfield
decls.statement:
theorem finrank_adjoin_prod_root [NeZero (2 : K)]
    (hroot : ∀ i, root i ^ 2 = algebraMap K L (d i))
    {S : Finset ι} (hSsq : ¬ IsSquare (∏ i ∈ S, d i)) :
    Module.finrank K (IntermediateField.adjoin K {∏ i ∈ S, root i}) = 2

decls.name: TauCeti.Multiquadratic.adjoin_prod_root_le
decls.doc:
**A subset-product subfield sits inside the multiquadratic field.** For any subset `S`, the
simple extension generated by `∏_{i ∈ S} root i` is contained in `M = K(rootᵢ : i)`.
decls.title: A subset-product subfield sits inside the multiquadratic field
decls.statement:
theorem adjoin_prod_root_le (S : Finset ι) :
    IntermediateField.adjoin K {∏ i ∈ S, root i} ≤
      IntermediateField.adjoin K (Set.range root)

decls.name: TauCeti.Multiquadratic.eq_of_adjoin_prod_root_eq
decls.doc:
**Distinct subsets give distinct quadratic subfields.** Under square-class independence the map
`S ↦ K(∏_{i ∈ S} root i)` from the nonempty subsets of the index type to the quadratic subfields of
`M` is injective: if two nonempty subsets generate the same subfield, they are equal.
decls.title: Distinct subsets give distinct quadratic subfields
decls.statement:
theorem eq_of_adjoin_prod_root_eq [NeZero (2 : K)]
    (hroot : ∀ i, root i ^ 2 = algebraMap K L (d i))
    (hindep : ∀ S : Finset ι, S.Nonempty → ¬ IsSquare (∏ i ∈ S, d i))
    {S T : Finset ι} (hS : S.Nonempty)
    (hST : IntermediateField.adjoin K {∏ i ∈ S, root i}
        = IntermediateField.adjoin K {∏ i ∈ T, root i}) :
    S = T

decls.name: TauCeti.Multiquadratic.finrank_intermediateField_mul_finrank_top
decls.doc:
**The tower identity `[F : K] · [M : F] = 2ⁿ`.** Under square-class independence, an
intermediate field `F` of `M = K(rootᵢ : i)` and the whole multiquadratic field multiply their
degrees to the full degree `2 ^ |ι|`: the absolute degree `[F : K]` times the relative degree
`[M : F]`.
decls.title: The tower identity `[F : K] · [M : F] = 2ⁿ`
decls.statement:
theorem finrank_intermediateField_mul_finrank_top [Finite ι] [NeZero (2 : K)]
    (hroot : ∀ i, root i ^ 2 = algebraMap K L (d i))
    (hindep : ∀ S : Finset ι, S.Nonempty → ¬ IsSquare (∏ i ∈ S, d i))
    (F : IntermediateField K (adjoin K (Set.range root))) :
    Module.finrank K F * Module.finrank F (adjoin K (Set.range root)) = 2 ^ Nat.card ι

decls.name: TauCeti.Multiquadratic.finrank_top_over_intermediateField
decls.doc:
**The relative degree of a multiquadratic field over an intermediate field.** Under square-class
independence, the whole multiquadratic field `M = K(rootᵢ : i)` has degree `2 ^ dim U` over an
intermediate field `F`, where `U` is the `𝔽₂`-subspace of `ι → ℤ/2` attached to `F`. This is the
reciprocal partner of `TauCeti.Multiquadratic.finrank_intermediateField_eq_two_pow`: `[F : K]` reads
the codimension of `U`, `[M : F]` reads its dimension, and their product is the full degree.
decls.title: The relative degree of a multiquadratic field over an intermediate field
decls.statement:
theorem finrank_top_over_intermediateField [Finite ι] [NeZero (2 : K)]
    (hroot : ∀ i, root i ^ 2 = algebraMap K L (d i))
    (hindep : ∀ S : Finset ι, S.Nonempty → ¬ IsSquare (∏ i ∈ S, d i))
    (F : IntermediateField K (adjoin K (Set.range root))) :
    Module.finrank F (adjoin K (Set.range root))
      = 2 ^ Module.finrank (ZMod 2) (intermediateFieldEquivSubmodule hroot hindep F).ofDual

decls.name: TauCeti.Multiquadratic.finrank_top_over_intermediateField_eq_two_iff
decls.doc:
**`M` is quadratic over `F` exactly when its subspace is a line.** Under square-class
independence, the multiquadratic field `M = K(rootᵢ : i)` has degree `2` over an intermediate field
`F` exactly when the `𝔽₂`-subspace `U` of `ι → ℤ/2` attached to `F` is a line, `dim U = 1`. This is
the dual of "the quadratic subfields are the hyperplanes"
(`TauCeti.Multiquadratic.finrank_intermediateField_eq_two_iff`).
decls.title: `M` is quadratic over `F` exactly when its subspace is a line
decls.statement:
theorem finrank_top_over_intermediateField_eq_two_iff [Finite ι] [NeZero (2 : K)]
    (hroot : ∀ i, root i ^ 2 = algebraMap K L (d i))
    (hindep : ∀ S : Finset ι, S.Nonempty → ¬ IsSquare (∏ i ∈ S, d i))
    (F : IntermediateField K (adjoin K (Set.range root))) :
    Module.finrank F (adjoin K (Set.range root)) = 2 ↔
      Module.finrank (ZMod 2) (intermediateFieldEquivSubmodule hroot hindep F).ofDual = 1

decls.name: TauCeti.Multiquadratic.finrank_top_over_intermediateField_of_finrank_eq_two
decls.doc:
**The relative degree over a quadratic subfield is `2 ^ (n - 1)`.** Under square-class
independence, over any quadratic subfield `F` of the degree-`2ⁿ` multiquadratic field
`M = K(rootᵢ : i)`, the multiquadratic field itself has degree `2 ^ (|ι| - 1)`. This is the relative
degree that the genus-field constructions read off over the quadratic base.
decls.title: The relative degree over a quadratic subfield is `2 ^ (n - 1)`
decls.statement:
theorem finrank_top_over_intermediateField_of_finrank_eq_two [Finite ι] [NeZero (2 : K)]
    (hroot : ∀ i, root i ^ 2 = algebraMap K L (d i))
    (hindep : ∀ S : Finset ι, S.Nonempty → ¬ IsSquare (∏ i ∈ S, d i))
    (F : IntermediateField K (adjoin K (Set.range root)))
    (hF : Module.finrank K F = 2) :
    Module.finrank F (adjoin K (Set.range root)) = 2 ^ (Nat.card ι - 1)

decls.name: TauCeti.Multiquadratic.sqrtTower
decls.doc: Iterated multiquadratic tower `K(root₀, …, rootₙ₋₁) ⊆ L`.
decls.statement: def sqrtTower (root : ℕ → L) (n : ℕ) : IntermediateField K L

decls.name: TauCeti.Multiquadratic.sqrtTower_def
decls.doc: The defining adjoin presentation of `sqrtTower`.
decls.statement:
theorem sqrtTower_def (root : ℕ → L) (n : ℕ) :
    sqrtTower (K := K) root n = IntermediateField.adjoin K (root '' Set.Iio n)

decls.name: TauCeti.Multiquadratic.mem_sqrtTower_iff
decls.doc: Membership in `sqrtTower` in terms of the defining adjoin.
decls.statement:
theorem mem_sqrtTower_iff (root : ℕ → L) (n : ℕ) (x : L) :
    x ∈ sqrtTower (K := K) root n ↔
      x ∈ IntermediateField.adjoin K (root '' Set.Iio n)

decls.name: TauCeti.Multiquadratic.sqrtTower_zero
decls.doc: The zeroth multiquadratic tower is the base field.
decls.statement: theorem sqrtTower_zero (root : ℕ → L) : sqrtTower (K := K) root 0 = ⊥

decls.name: TauCeti.Multiquadratic.sqrtTower_succ
decls.doc: Adjoining the next square root gives the successor stage of `sqrtTower`.

decls.name: TauCeti.Multiquadratic.sqrtTower_le_iff
decls.doc:
The universal property of `sqrtTower`: it is the smallest intermediate field containing
the first `n` chosen roots.
decls.statement:
theorem sqrtTower_le_iff (root : ℕ → L) (n : ℕ) (F : IntermediateField K L) :
    sqrtTower (K := K) root n ≤ F ↔ ∀ j, j < n → root j ∈ F

decls.name: TauCeti.Multiquadratic.sqrtTower_eq_adjoin_fin_range
decls.doc: The first `n` roots may equivalently be indexed by `Fin n`.
decls.statement:
theorem sqrtTower_eq_adjoin_fin_range (root : ℕ → L) (n : ℕ) :
    sqrtTower (K := K) root n =
      IntermediateField.adjoin K (Set.range fun j : Fin n => root j)

decls.name: TauCeti.Multiquadratic.sqrtTower_le_iff_fin
decls.doc: The universal property of `sqrtTower` using the finite index type `Fin n`.
decls.statement:
theorem sqrtTower_le_iff_fin (root : ℕ → L) (n : ℕ) (F : IntermediateField K L) :
    sqrtTower (K := K) root n ≤ F ↔ ∀ j : Fin n, root j ∈ F

decls.name: TauCeti.Multiquadratic.sqrtTower_root_mem
decls.doc: A chosen root indexed before `n` lies in `sqrtTower root n`.
decls.statement:
theorem sqrtTower_root_mem (root : ℕ → L) {j n : ℕ} (hj : j < n) :
    root j ∈ sqrtTower (K := K) root n

decls.name: TauCeti.Multiquadratic.sqrtTower_sq_mem
decls.doc:
The square of a listed root lies in `sqrtTower root n` as soon as its radicand is in the
base field.
decls.statement:
theorem sqrtTower_sq_mem (root : ℕ → L) (d : ℕ → K)
    (hroot : ∀ j, root j ^ 2 = algebraMap K L (d j)) {j n : ℕ} :
    root j ^ 2 ∈ sqrtTower (K := K) root n

decls.name: TauCeti.Multiquadratic.sqrtTower_sup_adjoin_eq_of_mem
TauCeti.Multiquadratic.eq_sq_mul_prod_insert_of_mul_radicand
decls.doc:
Square-class reconstruction across one tower level: from `r * dₙ = s² * ∏_T dⱼ` with
`dₙ ≠ 0` and `n ∉ T`, the radicand `r` equals `(s / dₙ)²` times the product over `insert n T`.
decls.statement:
theorem eq_sq_mul_prod_insert_of_mul_radicand {d : ℕ → K} {n : ℕ} {r s : K}
    {T : Finset ℕ} (hnT : n ∉ T) (hdn : d n ≠ 0)
    (hmul : r * d n = s ^ 2 * ∏ j ∈ T, d j) :
    r = (s / d n) ^ 2 * ∏ j ∈ insert n T, d j

decls.name: TauCeti.Multiquadratic.radicand_ne_zero_of_root_notMem
decls.doc:
If the chosen square root of `d n` lies outside the `n`-th tower, then `d n ≠ 0`: a zero
radicand has `root n = 0`, which lies in every tower.

decls.name: TauCeti.Multiquadratic.exists_sq_mul_prod_of_eq_mul_root
decls.doc:
Descent step of `squareClass_of_sq_mem` in the branch where `y = b · rootₙ` with `b` in the
`n`-th tower — the `a = 0` case left by the vanishing cross term. Then `y · rootₙ` lies in the
`n`-th tower and squares to `r · dₙ`, so the level-`n` descent hypothesis produces a
representation of `r` over `Set.Iio (n + 1)` with `n` adjoined to the subset.
decls.statement:
theorem exists_sq_mul_prod_of_eq_mul_root (d : ℕ → K) (root : ℕ → L)
    {n : ℕ} {r : K} {y b : L}
    (hroot : root n ^ 2 = algebraMap K L (d n)) (hdn0 : d n ≠ 0)
    (hb : b ∈ sqrtTower (K := K) root n) (heq : y = b * root n)
    (hy : y ^ 2 = algebraMap K L r)
    (ih : ∀ r : K, ∀ y : L, y ^ 2 = algebraMap K L r → y ∈ sqrtTower (K := K) root n →
      ∃ (T : Finset ℕ) (s : K), ↑T ⊆ Set.Iio n ∧ r = s ^ 2 * ∏ j ∈ T, d j) :
    ∃ (T : Finset ℕ) (s : K), ↑T ⊆ Set.Iio (n + 1) ∧ r = s ^ 2 * ∏ j ∈ T, d j

decls.name: TauCeti.Multiquadratic.squareClass_of_sq_mem
decls.doc:
**Square-class descent.** In characteristic not two, if `y² = r` over `K` and
`y ∈ K(root₀, …, rootₙ₋₁)`, where `root j` is a chosen square root of `d j`, then `r` is a
square times a subset product of the `d j` with `j < n`.
decls.title: Square-class descent
decls.statement:
theorem squareClass_of_sq_mem (d : ℕ → K) (root : ℕ → L)
    (hroot : ∀ j, root j ^ 2 = algebraMap K L (d j)) [NeZero (2 : K)] :
    ∀ n, ∀ r : K, ∀ y : L, y ^ 2 = algebraMap K L r → y ∈ sqrtTower (K := K) root n →
      ∃ (T : Finset ℕ) (s : K), ↑T ⊆ Set.Iio n ∧
        r = s ^ 2 * ∏ j ∈ T, d j

decls.name: TauCeti.Multiquadratic.squareClass_of_sq_mem_fin
decls.doc:
**Finite-index square-class descent.** If `y² = r` over `K` and
`y ∈ K(root i | i : Fin n)`, where `root i` is a chosen square root of `d i`, then `r`
is a square times a subset product of the `d i`.
decls.title: Finite-index square-class descent
decls.statement:
theorem squareClass_of_sq_mem_fin {n : ℕ} (d : Fin n → K) (root : Fin n → L)
    (hroot : ∀ j, root j ^ 2 = algebraMap K L (d j)) [NeZero (2 : K)]
    {r : K} {y : L} (hy : y ^ 2 = algebraMap K L r)
    (hmem : y ∈ IntermediateField.adjoin K (Set.range root)) :
    ∃ (T : Finset (Fin n)) (s : K), r = s ^ 2 * ∏ j ∈ T, d j

decls.name: TauCeti.Multiquadratic.squareClass_of_sq_mem_fintype
decls.doc:
**Arbitrary finite-index square-class descent.** If `y² = r` over `K` and
`y ∈ K(root i | i : ι)` for a finite index type `ι`, where `root i` is a chosen square
root of `d i`, then `r` is a square times a subset product of the `d i`.
decls.title: Arbitrary finite-index square-class descent
decls.statement:
theorem squareClass_of_sq_mem_fintype {ι : Type*} [Finite ι] (d : ι → K) (root : ι → L)
    (hroot : ∀ j, root j ^ 2 = algebraMap K L (d j)) [NeZero (2 : K)]
    {r : K} {y : L} (hy : y ^ 2 = algebraMap K L r)
    (hmem : y ∈ IntermediateField.adjoin K (Set.range root)) :
    ∃ (T : Finset ι) (s : K), r = s ^ 2 * ∏ j ∈ T, d j

decls.name: TauCeti.Multiquadratic.squareClass_of_sqrt_mem
decls.doc:
**Square-class descent for real rational square roots.** If `r` is a nonnegative
rational with `√r ∈ ℚ(√c₀, …, √cₙ₋₁)` and every `c j` is nonnegative, then `r` is a
rational square times a subset product of the `c j`.
decls.title: Square-class descent for real rational square roots
decls.statement:
theorem squareClass_of_sqrt_mem (c : ℕ → ℚ) (hc : ∀ j, 0 ≤ c j) :
    ∀ n, ∀ r : ℚ, 0 ≤ r → (Real.sqrt r : ℝ) ∈ sqrtTower (K := ℚ) (fun j => Real.sqrt (c j)) n →
      ∃ (T : Finset ℕ) (s : ℚ), ↑T ⊆ Set.Iio n ∧
        r = s ^ 2 * ∏ j ∈ T, c j

decls.name: TauCeti.Multiquadratic.sq_sqrt_intCast
decls.doc:
The real square root of a nonnegative integer squares back to its rational value, in the form
`(√n)² = algebraMap ℚ ℝ n`. This supplies the `hroot` hypothesis of the degree theorem for the real
square roots of integer radicands. The natural-number form `sq_sqrt_natCast` is the special case
`0 ≤ n`.
decls.statement:
theorem sq_sqrt_intCast {n : ℤ} (hn : 0 ≤ n) :
    (Real.sqrt n) ^ 2 = algebraMap ℚ ℝ (n : ℚ)

decls.name: TauCeti.Multiquadratic.isSquare_units_val_iff
decls.doc: A unit is a square iff its underlying field element is.
decls.statement: theorem isSquare_units_val_iff {u : Kˣ} : IsSquare (u : K) ↔ IsSquare u

decls.name: TauCeti.Multiquadratic.finrank_adjoin_range_of_linearIndependent
decls.doc:
**The multiquadratic degree theorem, restated via linear independence.** If the square classes
of the radicands `d : ι → Kˣ` are `ZMod 2`-linearly independent, then the field generated over `K`
by their square roots `root i` has degree `2^|ι|`. This is `finrank_adjoin_range` consuming the
structural form of square-class independence.
decls.title: The multiquadratic degree theorem, restated via linear independence
decls.statement:
theorem finrank_adjoin_range_of_linearIndependent {ι : Type*} [Finite ι] {d : ι → Kˣ}
    {root : ι → L} (hroot : ∀ i, root i ^ 2 = algebraMap K L (d i)) [NeZero (2 : K)]
    (hli : LinearIndependent (ZMod 2) (fun i => squareClass (d i))) :
    Module.finrank K (IntermediateField.adjoin K (Set.range root)) = 2 ^ Nat.card ι

decls.name: TauCeti.Multiquadratic.prodRootMem
decls.doc:
The subset-product root of `S`, as an element of the multiquadratic field
`M = K(rootᵢ : i)`.
decls.statement:
def prodRootMem (root : ι → L) (S : Finset ι) :
    ↥(adjoin K (Set.range root))

decls.name: TauCeti.Multiquadratic.prodRootMem_coe
decls.statement:
theorem prodRootMem_coe (S : Finset ι) :
    (prodRootMem (K := K) root S : L) = ∏ i ∈ S, root i

decls.name: TauCeti.Multiquadratic.finrank_adjoin_prodRootMem
decls.doc:
**A nonempty subset-product subfield of `M` is quadratic.** Computed inside `M`, the simple
extension `K(∏_{i ∈ S} root i)` has the same degree as its `L`-level counterpart, which is `2`
when the radicand product `∏_{i ∈ S} d i` is not a square.
decls.title: A nonempty subset-product subfield of `M` is quadratic
decls.statement:
theorem finrank_adjoin_prodRootMem [NeZero (2 : K)]
    (hroot : ∀ i, root i ^ 2 = algebraMap K L (d i))
    {S : Finset ι} (hSsq : ¬ IsSquare (∏ i ∈ S, d i)) :
    Module.finrank K (adjoin K {prodRootMem (K := K) root S}) = 2

decls.name: TauCeti.Multiquadratic.quadraticSubfieldOfFinset
decls.doc:
**The subset-product quadratic subfield of `M` attached to a nonempty subset.** Under
square-class independence, each nonempty subset `S` of the index type names the quadratic subfield
`K(∏_{i ∈ S} root i)` of `M = K(rootᵢ : i)`.
decls.title: The subset-product quadratic subfield of `M` attached to a nonempty subset

decls.name: TauCeti.Multiquadratic.quadraticSubfieldOfFinset_val
decls.doc:
The subfield underlying `quadraticSubfieldOfFinset hroot hindep S` is
`K(∏_{i ∈ S} root i)`.

decls.name: TauCeti.Multiquadratic.quadraticSubfieldOfFinset_injective
decls.doc:
**Distinct nonempty subsets give distinct quadratic subfields.** The subset-product assignment
`quadraticSubfieldOfFinset` is injective: this is the `M`-level reading of
`eq_of_adjoin_prod_root_eq`, transported across the lift.
decls.title: Distinct nonempty subsets give distinct quadratic subfields
decls.statement:
theorem quadraticSubfieldOfFinset_injective [NeZero (2 : K)] :
    Function.Injective (quadraticSubfieldOfFinset hroot hindep)

decls.name: TauCeti.Multiquadratic.quadraticSubfieldOfFinset_bijective
decls.doc:
**The subset-product assignment is a bijection.** Injective by
`quadraticSubfieldOfFinset_injective`, its domain (the nonempty subsets) and codomain (the
quadratic subfields) both have cardinality `2ⁿ - 1`, so the injection is a bijection.
decls.title: The subset-product assignment is a bijection
decls.statement:
theorem quadraticSubfieldOfFinset_bijective [Finite ι] [NeZero (2 : K)] :
    Function.Bijective (quadraticSubfieldOfFinset hroot hindep)

decls.name: TauCeti.Multiquadratic.exists_finset_of_finrank_two
decls.doc:
**Classification of the quadratic subfields.** Under square-class independence, every quadratic
subfield `F` of the multiquadratic field `M = K(rootᵢ : i)` is a subset-product subfield: there is a
nonempty subset `S` with `F = K(∏_{i ∈ S} root i)`. (The subset is in fact unique, by
`quadraticSubfieldOfFinset_bijective`, but this statement asserts only existence.)
decls.title: Classification of the quadratic subfields

decls.name: TauCeti.Multiquadratic.nonemptyFinsetEquivQuadraticSubfield
decls.doc:
**The quadratic subfields of `M` are indexed by the nonempty subsets.** The bijection
`quadraticSubfieldOfFinset`, packaged as an equivalence between the nonempty subsets of the index
type and the quadratic subfields of the multiquadratic field.
decls.title: The quadratic subfields of `M` are indexed by the nonempty subsets

decls.name: TauCeti.Multiquadratic.nonemptyFinsetEquivQuadraticSubfield_apply
decls.doc:
`nonemptyFinsetEquivQuadraticSubfield` sends a nonempty subset `S` to the subset-product
subfield `quadraticSubfieldOfFinset hroot hindep S`.
decls.statement:
theorem nonemptyFinsetEquivQuadraticSubfield_apply [Finite ι] [NeZero (2 : K)]
    (S : {S : Finset ι // S.Nonempty}) :
    nonemptyFinsetEquivQuadraticSubfield hroot hindep S
      = quadraticSubfieldOfFinset hroot hindep S

decls.name: TauCeti.Multiquadratic.card_submodule_finrank_eq_one
decls.doc:
**Lines of an `𝔽₂`-space are counted by its nonzero vectors.** Over `𝔽₂` the only nonzero
scalar is `1`, so distinct nonzero vectors span distinct lines and every line is spanned by a
nonzero vector; hence the `1`-dimensional subspaces of a finite `𝔽₂`-space `M` number
`|M| - 1`.
decls.title: Lines of an `𝔽₂`-space are counted by its nonzero vectors
decls.statement:
theorem card_submodule_finrank_eq_one [Fintype M] :
    Nat.card {W : Submodule (ZMod 2) M // finrank (ZMod 2) W = 1} = Fintype.card M - 1

decls.name: TauCeti.Multiquadratic.card_hyperplane
decls.doc:
**The hyperplanes of an `n`-dimensional `𝔽₂`-space number `2ⁿ - 1`.** A subspace `U` is a
hyperplane (`dim U + 1 = dim V`) exactly when its dual annihilator is a line; the dual-annihilator
order isomorphism turns the hyperplanes of `V` into the lines of its dual, which
`card_submodule_finrank_eq_one` counts.
decls.title: The hyperplanes of an `n`-dimensional `𝔽₂`-space number `2ⁿ - 1`
decls.statement:
theorem card_hyperplane (n : ℕ) (hn : finrank (ZMod 2) V = n) :
    Nat.card {U : Submodule (ZMod 2) V // finrank (ZMod 2) U + 1 = n} = 2 ^ n - 1

decls.name: TauCeti.Multiquadratic.card_quadratic_intermediateField_adjoin_range
decls.doc:
**The number of quadratic subfields of a multiquadratic field is `2ⁿ - 1`.** Under
square-class independence (and `2 ≠ 0`), the multiquadratic field `M = K(rootᵢ : i)`, of degree
`2 ^ |ι|` over `K`, has exactly `2 ^ |ι| - 1` intermediate fields of degree `2` over `K`. The count
is that of the hyperplanes of the `𝔽₂`-subspace lattice.
decls.title: The number of quadratic subfields of a multiquadratic field is `2ⁿ - 1`
decls.statement:
theorem card_quadratic_intermediateField_adjoin_range [Finite ι] [NeZero (2 : K)]
    (hroot : ∀ i, root i ^ 2 = algebraMap K L (d i))
    (hindep : ∀ S : Finset ι, S.Nonempty → ¬ IsSquare (∏ i ∈ S, d i)) :
    Nat.card {F : IntermediateField K (adjoin K (Set.range root)) // Module.finrank K F = 2}
      = 2 ^ Nat.card ι - 1

decls.name: TauCeti.Multiquadratic.card_quadratic_intermediateField_adjoin_sqrt_two_three
decls.doc:
**Worked example: `ℚ(√2, √3)` has exactly `3` quadratic subfields.** The smallest nontrivial
multiquadratic field, of degree `4`, has `2² - 1 = 3` subfields of degree `2` over `ℚ`. The
radicands `2` and `3` are coprime, squarefree, and not units, so
`card_quadratic_intermediateField_adjoin_range` applies through
`not_isSquare_prod_of_coprime_squarefree_rat`.
decls.title: Worked example: `ℚ(√2, √3)` has exactly `3` quadratic subfields
decls.statement:
theorem card_quadratic_intermediateField_adjoin_sqrt_two_three :
    Nat.card {F : IntermediateField ℚ
        (adjoin ℚ {Real.sqrt 2, Real.sqrt 3} : IntermediateField ℚ ℝ) //
          Module.finrank ℚ F = 2} = 3

decls.name: TauCeti.Multiquadratic.card_submodule_eq_pow_finrank
decls.doc: The cardinality of an `𝔽₂`-subspace `U` of `ι → ℤ/2` is `2` to its dimension.
decls.statement:
theorem card_submodule_eq_pow_finrank [Finite ι]
    (U : Submodule (ZMod 2) (ι → ZMod 2)) :
    Nat.card U = 2 ^ Module.finrank (ZMod 2) U

decls.name: TauCeti.Multiquadratic.card_intermediateFieldEquivSubmodule_ofDual
decls.doc:
The subspace attached to an intermediate field `F` of `M = K(rootᵢ : i)` has the same
cardinality as the fixing subgroup of `F`: both reinterpret the same set of automorphisms, one as a
subgroup of `Gal(M/K)` and one as an `𝔽₂`-subspace of `ι → ℤ/2`.
decls.statement:
theorem card_intermediateFieldEquivSubmodule_ofDual [Finite ι] [NeZero (2 : K)]
    (hroot : ∀ i, root i ^ 2 = algebraMap K L (d i))
    (hindep : ∀ S : Finset ι, S.Nonempty → ¬ IsSquare (∏ i ∈ S, d i))
    (F : IntermediateField K (adjoin K (Set.range root))) :
    Nat.card (intermediateFieldEquivSubmodule hroot hindep F).ofDual
      = Nat.card F.fixingSubgroup

decls.name: TauCeti.Multiquadratic.finrank_mul_card_intermediateFieldEquivSubmodule
decls.doc:
**The degree of an intermediate field times the size of its subspace is `2ⁿ`.** Under
square-class independence, an intermediate field `F` of `M = K(rootᵢ : i)` and its subspace
`U = (intermediateFieldEquivSubmodule F).ofDual` of `ι → ℤ/2` satisfy `[F : K] · |U| = 2 ^ |ι|`.
The Galois correspondence is order-reversing, so a larger subfield matches a smaller subspace and
the two sizes multiply to the full degree.
decls.title: The degree of an intermediate field times the size of its subspace is `2ⁿ`
decls.statement:
theorem finrank_mul_card_intermediateFieldEquivSubmodule [Finite ι] [NeZero (2 : K)]
    (hroot : ∀ i, root i ^ 2 = algebraMap K L (d i))
    (hindep : ∀ S : Finset ι, S.Nonempty → ¬ IsSquare (∏ i ∈ S, d i))
    (F : IntermediateField K (adjoin K (Set.range root))) :
    Module.finrank K F
        * Nat.card (intermediateFieldEquivSubmodule hroot hindep F).ofDual
      = 2 ^ Nat.card ι

decls.name: TauCeti.Multiquadratic.finrank_mul_two_pow_finrank_intermediateFieldEquivSubmodule
decls.doc:
**The degree of an intermediate field through the dimension of its subspace.** The reciprocal
relation `[F : K] · |U| = 2ⁿ` read with `|U| = 2 ^ dim U`: `[F : K] · 2 ^ dim U = 2 ^ |ι|`.
decls.title: The degree of an intermediate field through the dimension of its subspace
decls.statement:
theorem finrank_mul_two_pow_finrank_intermediateFieldEquivSubmodule [Finite ι] [NeZero (2 : K)]
    (hroot : ∀ i, root i ^ 2 = algebraMap K L (d i))
    (hindep : ∀ S : Finset ι, S.Nonempty → ¬ IsSquare (∏ i ∈ S, d i))
    (F : IntermediateField K (adjoin K (Set.range root))) :
    Module.finrank K F
        * 2 ^ Module.finrank (ZMod 2) (intermediateFieldEquivSubmodule hroot hindep F).ofDual
      = 2 ^ Nat.card ι

decls.name: TauCeti.Multiquadratic.finrank_intermediateField_eq_two_pow
decls.doc:
**The degree of an intermediate field is `2` to the codimension of its subspace.** Under
square-class independence, an intermediate field `F` of `M = K(rootᵢ : i)` has
`[F : K] = 2 ^ (|ι| - dim U)`, where `U` is the `𝔽₂`-subspace attached to `F`. This is the
explicit-power form of the reciprocal relation `[F : K] · |U| = 2ⁿ`.
decls.title: The degree of an intermediate field is `2` to the codimension of its subspace
decls.statement:
theorem finrank_intermediateField_eq_two_pow [Finite ι] [NeZero (2 : K)]
    (hroot : ∀ i, root i ^ 2 = algebraMap K L (d i))
    (hindep : ∀ S : Finset ι, S.Nonempty → ¬ IsSquare (∏ i ∈ S, d i))
    (F : IntermediateField K (adjoin K (Set.range root))) :
    Module.finrank K F = 2 ^ (Nat.card ι
