        - Module.finrank (ZMod 2) (intermediateFieldEquivSubmodule hroot hindep F).ofDual)

decls.name: TauCeti.Multiquadratic.finrank_intermediateField_eq_two_iff
decls.doc:
**The quadratic subfields are the hyperplanes.** Under square-class independence, an
intermediate field `F` of `M = K(rootᵢ : i)` has degree `2` over `K` exactly when its subspace
`U` of `ι → ℤ/2` is a hyperplane, i.e. `dim U + 1 = |ι|`. This is the lattice reading of "the
quadratic subfields of a multiquadratic field".
decls.title: The quadratic subfields are the hyperplanes
decls.statement:
theorem finrank_intermediateField_eq_two_iff [Finite ι] [NeZero (2 : K)]
    (hroot : ∀ i, root i ^ 2 = algebraMap K L (d i))
    (hindep : ∀ S : Finset ι, S.Nonempty → ¬ IsSquare (∏ i ∈ S, d i))
    (F : IntermediateField K (adjoin K (Set.range root))) :
    Module.finrank K F = 2 ↔
      Module.finrank (ZMod 2) (intermediateFieldEquivSubmodule hroot hindep F).ofDual + 1
        = Nat.card ι

decls.name: TauCeti.Multiquadratic.intermediateFieldEquivSubmodule
decls.doc:
**The subfield lattice of a multiquadratic field is the `𝔽₂`-subspace lattice of `(ℤ/2)ⁿ`.**
If no nonempty subset product of the radicands `d i` is a square in `K` (and `2 ≠ 0`), then the
intermediate fields of `M = K(rootᵢ : i)` over `K` correspond, order-reversingly, to the
`𝔽₂`-subspaces of `ι → ℤ/2`: a larger subfield is fixed by a smaller group, hence matches a
smaller subspace.

The bijection is the composite of Mathlib's Galois correspondence
`IsGalois.intermediateFieldEquivSubgroup` (intermediate fields ↔ subgroups of the Galois group,
dualised), the Galois-group isomorphism `galoisGroupEquiv` (`Gal(M/K) ≃ Multiplicative (ι → ℤ/2)`),
and the identification of subgroups of an `𝔽₂`-vector space with its subspaces.
decls.title: The subfield lattice of a multiquadratic field is the `𝔽₂`-subspace lattice of `(ℤ/2)ⁿ`
decls.statement:
def intermediateFieldEquivSubmodule [Finite ι] [NeZero (2 : K)]
    (hroot : ∀ i, root i ^ 2 = algebraMap K L (d i))
    (hindep : ∀ S : Finset ι, S.Nonempty → ¬ IsSquare (∏ i ∈ S, d i)) :
    IntermediateField K (adjoin K (Set.range root)) ≃o
      (Submodule (ZMod 2) (ι → ZMod 2))ᵒᵈ

decls.name: TauCeti.Multiquadratic.intermediateFieldEquivSubmodule_apply_ofDual
decls.doc:
The subspace attached to an intermediate field is the image of its fixing subgroup under the
sign-pattern Galois-group equivalence.
decls.statement:
theorem intermediateFieldEquivSubmodule_apply_ofDual [Finite ι] [NeZero (2 : K)]
    (hroot : ∀ i, root i ^ 2 = algebraMap K L (d i))
    (hindep : ∀ S : Finset ι, S.Nonempty → ¬ IsSquare (∏ i ∈ S, d i))
    (F : IntermediateField K (adjoin K (Set.range root))) :
    (intermediateFieldEquivSubmodule hroot hindep F).ofDual =
      AddSubgroup.toZModSubmodule 2
        (Subgroup.toAddSubgroup'
          ((galoisGroupEquiv hroot hindep).mapSubgroup F.fixingSubgroup))

decls.name: TauCeti.Multiquadratic.mem_intermediateFieldEquivSubmodule_apply_ofDual_iff
decls.doc:
A sign vector belongs to the subspace attached to an intermediate field exactly when it is the
sign pattern of an automorphism fixing that field.
decls.statement:
theorem mem_intermediateFieldEquivSubmodule_apply_ofDual_iff [Finite ι] [NeZero (2 : K)]
    (hroot : ∀ i, root i ^ 2 = algebraMap K L (d i))
    (hindep : ∀ S : Finset ι, S.Nonempty → ¬ IsSquare (∏ i ∈ S, d i))
    (F : IntermediateField K (adjoin K (Set.range root))) (v : ι → ZMod 2) :
    v ∈ (intermediateFieldEquivSubmodule hroot hindep F).ofDual ↔
      ∃ σ ∈ F.fixingSubgroup, signPattern root σ = v

decls.name: TauCeti.Multiquadratic.mem_intermediateFieldEquivSubmodule_symm_apply_iff
decls.doc:
The intermediate field attached to a subspace is the fixed field of the automorphisms whose
sign patterns lie in that subspace.
decls.statement:
theorem mem_intermediateFieldEquivSubmodule_symm_apply_iff [Finite ι] [NeZero (2 : K)]
    (hroot : ∀ i, root i ^ 2 = algebraMap K L (d i))
    (hindep : ∀ S : Finset ι, S.Nonempty → ¬ IsSquare (∏ i ∈ S, d i))
    (U : Submodule (ZMod 2) (ι → ZMod 2)) (x : adjoin K (Set.range root)) :
    x ∈ (intermediateFieldEquivSubmodule hroot hindep).symm (OrderDual.toDual U) ↔
      ∀ σ, signPattern root σ ∈ U → σ x = x

decls.name: TauCeti.Multiquadratic.card_intermediateField_adjoin_range
decls.doc:
**The number of subfields of a multiquadratic field.** Under square-class independence, the
intermediate fields of `M = K(rootᵢ : i)` over `K` are in bijection with the `𝔽₂`-subspaces of
`ι → ℤ/2`, so there are exactly as many of them. (For `|ι| = n` this count is the number of
subspaces of `𝔽₂ⁿ`, the Galois number `Gₙ`.)
decls.title: The number of subfields of a multiquadratic field
decls.statement:
theorem card_intermediateField_adjoin_range [Finite ι] [NeZero (2 : K)]
    (hroot : ∀ i, root i ^ 2 = algebraMap K L (d i))
    (hindep : ∀ S : Finset ι, S.Nonempty → ¬ IsSquare (∏ i ∈ S, d i)) :
    Nat.card (IntermediateField K (adjoin K (Set.range root)))
      = Nat.card (Submodule (ZMod 2) (ι → ZMod 2))

decls.name: TauCeti.NumberField.card_classGroupElementaryTwoQuotient_dvd_classNumber
decls.doc: The cardinality of `Cl(𝓞 K) / Cl(𝓞 K)²` divides the class number.
decls.statement:
theorem card_classGroupElementaryTwoQuotient_dvd_classNumber [NumberField K] :
    Nat.card (TauCeti.ClassGroup.ElementaryTwoQuotient (𝓞 K)) ∣ NumberField.classNumber K

decls.name: TauCeti.NumberField.card_classGroupElementaryTwoQuotient_le_classNumber
decls.doc:
The elementary-2 quotient of a number-field class group has cardinality at most the class
number.
decls.statement:
theorem card_classGroupElementaryTwoQuotient_le_classNumber [NumberField K] :
    Nat.card (TauCeti.ClassGroup.ElementaryTwoQuotient (𝓞 K)) ≤ NumberField.classNumber K

decls.name: TauCeti.NumberField.two_pow_classGroupTwoRank_dvd_classNumber
decls.doc:
The rank form of `card_classGroupElementaryTwoQuotient_dvd_classNumber`:
`2 ^ TauCeti.ClassGroup.twoRank (𝓞 K)` divides the class number.
decls.statement:
theorem two_pow_classGroupTwoRank_dvd_classNumber [NumberField K] :
    2 ^ TauCeti.ClassGroup.twoRank (𝓞 K) ∣ NumberField.classNumber K

decls.name: TauCeti.NumberField.two_pow_classGroupTwoRank_le_classNumber
decls.doc:
The rank form of `card_classGroupElementaryTwoQuotient_le_classNumber`:
`2 ^ TauCeti.ClassGroup.twoRank (𝓞 K)` is bounded by the class number.
decls.statement:
theorem two_pow_classGroupTwoRank_le_classNumber [NumberField K] :
    2 ^ TauCeti.ClassGroup.twoRank (𝓞 K) ≤ NumberField.classNumber K

decls.name: TauCeti.NumberField.exists_isArithFrobAt
decls.doc:
**Frobenius elements exist.** For a Galois number field `K/ℚ` and a *nonzero* prime `Q` of
`𝓞 K`, some `σ ∈ Gal(K/ℚ)` is an arithmetic Frobenius at `Q`. This is Mathlib's
`IsArithFrobAt.exists_of_isInvariant` with the number-field side conditions discharged (a
nonzero prime of `𝓞 K` is maximal, with finite residue field).
decls.title: Frobenius elements exist
decls.statement:
theorem exists_isArithFrobAt [IsGalois ℚ K] (Q : Ideal (𝓞 K)) [Q.IsPrime] (hQ : Q ≠ ⊥) :
    ∃ σ : K ≃ₐ[ℚ] K, IsArithFrobAt ℤ σ Q

decls.name: TauCeti.NumberField.exists_isArithFrobAt_of_liesOver
decls.doc:
A Frobenius exists at every prime of `𝓞 K` lying over a rational prime — the form used when
`Q` is presented by a `LiesOver` instance rather than a nonvanishing hypothesis.
decls.statement:
theorem exists_isArithFrobAt_of_liesOver [IsGalois ℚ K] {p : ℕ} [Fact p.Prime]
    (Q : Ideal (𝓞 K)) [Q.IsPrime] [Q.LiesOver (span {(p : ℤ)})] :
    ∃ σ : K ≃ₐ[ℚ] K, IsArithFrobAt ℤ σ Q

decls.name: TauCeti.NumberField.isArithFrobAt_apply_sqrt
decls.doc:
**A Frobenius acts on square roots by the Legendre symbol.** Let `K` be a number field,
`p` an odd prime, and `σ ∈ Gal(K/ℚ)` an arithmetic Frobenius at an ideal `Q` of `𝓞 K` above
`p`. If `x ∈ K` satisfies `x² = d` for an integer `d` with `p ∤ d`, then

`σ x = legendreSym p d • x`:

the Frobenius fixes `√d` when `d` is a quadratic residue mod `p` and negates it otherwise.
decls.title: A Frobenius acts on square roots by the Legendre symbol
decls.statement:
theorem isArithFrobAt_apply_sqrt (hodd : p ≠ 2) {d : ℤ} (hd : ¬ (p : ℤ) ∣ d)
    {x : K} (hx : x ^ 2 = algebraMap ℤ K d)
    (Q : Ideal (𝓞 K)) [Q.LiesOver (span {(p : ℤ)})]
    {σ : K ≃ₐ[ℚ] K} (hσ : IsArithFrobAt ℤ σ Q) :
    σ x = legendreSym p d • x

decls.name: TauCeti.NumberField.isArithFrobAt_apply_sqrt_eq_self_iff
decls.doc:
**A Frobenius fixes `√d` iff `d` is a quadratic residue mod `p`.** Under the hypotheses of
`TauCeti.NumberField.isArithFrobAt_apply_sqrt`, `σ x = x` exactly when `legendreSym p d = 1`
(the other case being `σ x = -x`, `legendreSym p d = -1`). This reads the characteristic
biconditional off the `•` form, using that `x ≠ 0` (as `d ≠ 0`).
decls.title: A Frobenius fixes `√d` iff `d` is a quadratic residue mod `p`
decls.statement:
theorem isArithFrobAt_apply_sqrt_eq_self_iff (hodd : p ≠ 2) {d : ℤ} (hd : ¬ (p : ℤ) ∣ d)
    {x : K} (hx : x ^ 2 = algebraMap ℤ K d)
    (Q : Ideal (𝓞 K)) [Q.LiesOver (span {(p : ℤ)})]
    {σ : K ≃ₐ[ℚ] K} (hσ : IsArithFrobAt ℤ σ Q) :
    σ x = x ↔ legendreSym p d = 1

decls.name: TauCeti.NumberField.integralSqrt
decls.doc:
A square root `x` of an integer `d`, packaged as an element of the ring of integers: since
`x ^ 2 = d` is the image of an integer, it is integral over `ℤ` (`IsIntegral.of_pow`).
decls.statement: def integralSqrt (hx : x ^ 2 = algebraMap ℤ K d) : 𝓞 K

decls.name: TauCeti.NumberField.algebraMap_integralSqrt
decls.doc: Under `𝓞 K ↪ K`, `TauCeti.NumberField.integralSqrt hx` maps back to `x`.
decls.statement:
theorem algebraMap_integralSqrt (hx : x ^ 2 = algebraMap ℤ K d) :
    algebraMap (𝓞 K) K (integralSqrt hx) = x

decls.name: TauCeti.NumberField.integralSqrt_sq
decls.doc: `TauCeti.NumberField.integralSqrt hx` squares to the radicand `d` in `𝓞 K`.
decls.statement:
theorem integralSqrt_sq (hx : x ^ 2 = algebraMap ℤ K d) :
    integralSqrt hx ^ 2 = algebraMap ℤ (𝓞 K) d

decls.name: TauCeti.NumberField.Internal.not_intCast_prime_dvd_natPrime
decls.doc: Distinct rational primes remain coprime after casting to integers.
decls.statement:
theorem not_intCast_prime_dvd_natPrime {p l : ℕ} [Fact p.Prime]
    (hl : l.Prime) (hne : p ≠ l) : ¬ (p : ℤ) ∣ (l : ℤ)

decls.name: TauCeti.NumberField.Internal.exists_basis_eq_one_self_of_notMem_range_of_isIntegral
decls.doc:
In a quadratic number field, an integral non-rational element `x` gives the `ℚ`-basis
`{1, x}` of algebraic integers.
decls.statement:
theorem exists_basis_eq_one_self_of_notMem_range_of_isIntegral {K : Type*} [Field K]
    [NumberField K] {x : K} (hfin : finrank ℚ K = 2)
    (hx : x ∉ (algebraMap ℚ K).range) (hxint : IsIntegral ℤ x) :
    ∃ b : Module.Basis (Fin 2) ℚ K, ⇑b = ![1, x] ∧ ∀ i, IsIntegral ℤ (b i)

decls.name: TauCeti.NumberField.minpoly_rat_quadratic
decls.doc:
The minimal polynomial of `θ` over `ℚ` is `X² - d`, obtained from its minimal polynomial over
`ℤ` by base change along `ℤ → ℚ`.
decls.statement:
theorem minpoly_rat_quadratic {θ : 𝓞 K} {d : ℤ} (hmin : minpoly ℤ θ = X ^ 2 - C d) :
    minpoly ℚ (θ : K) = X ^ 2 - C ((d : ℤ) : ℚ)

decls.name: TauCeti.NumberField.X_pow_two_sub_C_comp_neg
decls.doc: `X² - C a` is invariant under negating the variable: it is an even polynomial.
decls.statement:
theorem X_pow_two_sub_C_comp_neg (a : ℚ) :
    (X ^ 2 - C a).comp (-X) = X ^ 2 - C a

decls.name: TauCeti.NumberField.minpoly_rat_eq_neg
decls.doc: `θ` and `-θ` have the same minimal polynomial over `ℚ` (both `X² - d`, an even polynomial).
decls.statement:
theorem minpoly_rat_eq_neg (hmin : minpoly ℤ θ = X ^ 2 - C d) :
    minpoly ℚ (θ : K) = minpoly ℚ (-(θ : K))

decls.name: TauCeti.NumberField.quadraticPowerBasis
decls.doc: The power basis `1, θ` of the quadratic field `K` over `ℚ`.
decls.statement:
def quadraticPowerBasis (hgen : Algebra.adjoin ℚ {(θ : K)} = ⊤) :
    PowerBasis ℚ K

decls.name: TauCeti.NumberField.quadraticPowerBasis_gen
decls.statement:
theorem quadraticPowerBasis_gen (hgen : Algebra.adjoin ℚ {(θ : K)} = ⊤) :
    (quadraticPowerBasis hgen).gen = (θ : K)

decls.name: TauCeti.NumberField.adjoin_neg_eq_top
decls.doc: `-θ` also generates `K` over `ℚ`, so it too carries a power basis.
decls.statement:
theorem adjoin_neg_eq_top (hgen : Algebra.adjoin ℚ {(θ : K)} = ⊤) :
    Algebra.adjoin ℚ {(-(θ : K))} = ⊤

decls.name: TauCeti.NumberField.quadraticPowerBasisNeg
decls.doc: The power basis `1, -θ` of `K` over `ℚ`.
decls.statement:
def quadraticPowerBasisNeg (hgen : Algebra.adjoin ℚ {(θ : K)} = ⊤) :
    PowerBasis ℚ K

decls.name: TauCeti.NumberField.quadraticPowerBasisNeg_gen
decls.statement:
theorem quadraticPowerBasisNeg_gen (hgen : Algebra.adjoin ℚ {(θ : K)} = ⊤) :
    (quadraticPowerBasisNeg hgen).gen = -(θ : K)

decls.name: TauCeti.NumberField.quadraticConj
decls.doc:
**Quadratic conjugation.** The nontrivial `ℚ`-automorphism of the quadratic field `K = ℚ(√d)`,
characterised by `θ ↦ -θ`. Since `θ` and `-θ` share a minimal polynomial, it is the
`PowerBasis.equivOfMinpoly` between their power bases.
decls.title: Quadratic conjugation
decls.statement:
def quadraticConj (hmin : minpoly ℤ θ = X ^ 2 - C d)
    (hgen : Algebra.adjoin ℚ {(θ : K)} = ⊤) : K ≃ₐ[ℚ] K

decls.name: TauCeti.NumberField.quadraticConj_gen
decls.doc: Quadratic conjugation sends the generator `θ` to `-θ`.
decls.statement:
theorem quadraticConj_gen (hmin : minpoly ℤ θ = X ^ 2 - C d)
    (hgen : Algebra.adjoin ℚ {(θ : K)} = ⊤) :
    quadraticConj hmin hgen (θ : K) = -(θ : K)

decls.name: TauCeti.NumberField.quadraticConj_involutive
decls.doc: Quadratic conjugation is an involution on `K` (applying it twice is the identity).
decls.statement:
theorem quadraticConj_involutive (hmin : minpoly ℤ θ = X ^ 2 - C d)
    (hgen : Algebra.adjoin ℚ {(θ : K)} = ⊤) :
    Function.Involutive (quadraticConj hmin hgen)

decls.name: TauCeti.NumberField.ringOfIntegersQuadraticConj
decls.doc:
**Quadratic conjugation on the ring of integers.** The restriction of `quadraticConj` to
`𝓞 K`, a ring automorphism `𝓞 K ≃+* 𝓞 K`. This is the automorphism whose action on
`ClassGroup (𝓞 K)` is by inversion (the genus-theoretic fact that `I · σI` is principal).
decls.title: Quadratic conjugation on the ring of integers
decls.statement:
def ringOfIntegersQuadraticConj (hmin : minpoly ℤ θ = X ^ 2 - C d)
    (hgen : Algebra.adjoin ℚ {(θ : K)} = ⊤) : 𝓞 K ≃+* 𝓞 K

decls.name: TauCeti.NumberField.coe_ringOfIntegersQuadraticConj
decls.doc: Passing to `K`, `ringOfIntegersQuadraticConj x` is `quadraticConj` of the image of `x`.
decls.statement:
theorem coe_ringOfIntegersQuadraticConj (hmin : minpoly ℤ θ = X ^ 2 - C d)
    (hgen : Algebra.adjoin ℚ {(θ : K)} = ⊤) (x : 𝓞 K) :
    (ringOfIntegersQuadraticConj hmin hgen x : K) = quadraticConj hmin hgen (x : K)

decls.name: TauCeti.NumberField.ringOfIntegersQuadraticConj_gen
decls.doc: Quadratic conjugation on `𝓞 K` sends the generator `θ` to `-θ`.
decls.statement:
theorem ringOfIntegersQuadraticConj_gen (hmin : minpoly ℤ θ = X ^ 2 - C d)
    (hgen : Algebra.adjoin ℚ {(θ : K)} = ⊤) :
    ringOfIntegersQuadraticConj hmin hgen θ = -θ

decls.name: TauCeti.NumberField.ringOfIntegersQuadraticConj_involutive
decls.doc: Quadratic conjugation is an involution on `𝓞 K` (applying it twice is the identity).
decls.statement:
theorem ringOfIntegersQuadraticConj_involutive (hmin : minpoly ℤ θ = X ^ 2 - C d)
    (hgen : Algebra.adjoin ℚ {(θ : K)} = ⊤) :
    Function.Involutive (ringOfIntegersQuadraticConj hmin hgen)

decls.name: TauCeti.NumberField.mulEquiv_ringOfIntegersQuadraticConj_involutive
decls.doc:
Quadratic conjugation acts as an **involution on the class group** `Cl(𝓞 K)`. This is the
group-action shadow of `ringOfIntegersQuadraticConj_involutive`, and the first step towards the
genus-theoretic fact that the induced action is inversion (hence trivial on `Cl/Cl²`).
decls.statement:
theorem mulEquiv_ringOfIntegersQuadraticConj_involutive (hmin : minpoly ℤ θ = X ^ 2 - C d)
    (hgen : Algebra.adjoin ℚ {(θ : K)} = ⊤) :
    Function.Involutive (ClassGroup.mulEquiv (ringOfIntegersQuadraticConj hmin hgen))

decls.name: TauCeti.NumberField.algebraMap_four_mul_mem_conductor
decls.doc:
The power-basis discriminant `4d` lies in the conductor: for `θ` generating `K` over `ℚ`
with minimal polynomial `X² - d` over `ℤ`, the image of `4 * d` in `𝓞 K` belongs to
`conductor ℤ θ`. This is the crux of the conductor bound, since it forces the conductor
exponent of `θ` to divide `4d`.

decls.name: TauCeti.NumberField.not_dvd_exponent_of_minpoly_quadratic
decls.doc:
**Conductor bound.** If `θ` generates `K` and has minimal polynomial `X² - d`, then an odd
prime not dividing `d` does not divide the conductor exponent of `θ`.
decls.title: Conductor bound
decls.statement:
theorem not_dvd_exponent_of_minpoly_quadratic {θ : 𝓞 K} {d : ℤ}
    (hmin : minpoly ℤ θ = X ^ 2 - C d)
    (hgen : Algebra.adjoin ℚ {(θ : K)} = ⊤) {p : ℕ} [Fact p.Prime] (hodd : p ≠ 2)
    (hcop : ¬ (p : ℤ) ∣ d) : ¬ p ∣ exponent θ

decls.name: TauCeti.NumberField.card_monicFactorsMod_quadratic_iff
decls.doc:
**Factor count mod p.** `X² - d` has two monic irreducible factors mod `p` (for `p` odd,
`p ∤ d`) iff `d` is a square mod `p`.
decls.title: Factor count mod p
decls.statement:
theorem card_monicFactorsMod_quadratic_iff {θ : 𝓞 K} {d : ℤ}
    (hmin : minpoly ℤ θ = X ^ 2 - C d) {p : ℕ} [Fact p.Prime] (hodd : p ≠ 2)
    (hcop : ¬ (p : ℤ) ∣ d) :
    (monicFactorsMod θ p).card = 2 ↔ legendreSym p d = 1

decls.name: TauCeti.NumberField.ncard_primesOver_quadratic_iff
decls.doc:
**The quadratic splitting law.** For `K = ℚ(√d)` (`θ` a square root of the integer `d`
generating `K`) and an odd prime `p ∤ d`, `p` splits completely in `K` iff `d` is a quadratic
residue mod `p`. This is the `n = 1` case of the multiquadratic prime-splitting law.
decls.title: The quadratic splitting law
decls.statement:
theorem ncard_primesOver_quadratic_iff {θ : 𝓞 K} {d : ℤ}
    (hmin : minpoly ℤ θ = X ^ 2 - C d) (hgen : Algebra.adjoin ℚ {(θ : K)} = ⊤)
    {p : ℕ} [Fact p.Prime] (hodd : p ≠ 2) (hcop : ¬ (p : ℤ) ∣ d) :
    (primesOver (span {(p : ℤ)}) (𝓞 K)).ncard = finrank ℚ K ↔ legendreSym p d = 1

decls.name: TauCeti.NumberField.ncard_primesOver_eq_finrank_iff_of_isGalois
decls.statement:
theorem ncard_primesOver_eq_finrank_iff_of_isGalois {A : Type*} [CommRing A]
    [IsDedekindDomain A] [Algebra A (𝓞 L)] [Module.Finite A (𝓞 L)]
    [IsTorsionFree A (𝓞 L)] [IsGaloisGroup Gal(L/K) A (𝓞 L)] (P : Ideal A)
    [P.IsMaximal] :
    (primesOver P (𝓞 L)).ncard = finrank K L ↔
      P.ramificationIdxIn (𝓞 L) = 1 ∧ P.inertiaDegIn (𝓞 L) = 1

decls.name: TauCeti.NumberField.ncard_primesOver_eq_finrank_iff
decls.doc:
In a Galois number field, a rational prime `p` splits completely (there are `[K : ℚ]` primes
of `𝓞 K` above `p`) iff its ramification index and inertia degree are both `1`.
decls.statement:
theorem ncard_primesOver_eq_finrank_iff (K : Type*) [Field K] [NumberField K] [IsGalois ℚ K]
    (p : ℕ) [Fact p.Prime] :
    (primesOver (span {(p : ℤ)}) (𝓞 K)).ncard = finrank ℚ K ↔
      (span {(p : ℤ)}).ramificationIdxIn (𝓞 K) = 1 ∧
        (span {(p : ℤ)}).inertiaDegIn (𝓞 K) = 1

decls.name: TauCeti.NumberField.ncard_primesOver_eq_finrank_iff_stabilizer_eq_bot
decls.doc:
**Splitting completely ⟺ decomposition group trivial.** For a Galois number field `L` and a
prime `Q` of `𝓞 L` above the rational prime `p`, the prime `p` splits completely (there are
`[L : ℚ]` primes above it) iff the decomposition group of `Q` — its stabilizer under `Gal(L/ℚ)` —
is trivial.
decls.title: Splitting completely ⟺ decomposition group trivial
decls.statement:
theorem ncard_primesOver_eq_finrank_iff_stabilizer_eq_bot (L : Type*) [Field L]
    [NumberField L] [IsGalois ℚ L] {p : ℕ} [Fact p.Prime] (Q : Ideal (𝓞 L)) [Q.IsPrime]
    [Q.LiesOver (span {(p : ℤ)})] :
    (primesOver (span {(p : ℤ)}) (𝓞 L)).ncard = finrank ℚ L ↔
      stabilizer (L ≃ₐ[ℚ] L) Q = ⊥

decls.name: TauCeti.NumberField.torsionProdMultiplicativeToUnits
decls.doc:
The homomorphism realizing a pair (root of unity, exponent vector) as a unit, the underlying
map of `TauCeti.NumberField.unitsMulEquivTorsionProdMultiplicative`. Kept private; the public
interface is the equivalence.
decls.statement:
def torsionProdMultiplicativeToUnits :
    torsion F × Multiplicative (Fin (rank F) → ℤ) →* (𝓞 F)ˣ

decls.name: TauCeti.NumberField.torsionProdMultiplicativeToUnits_apply
decls.statement:
theorem torsionProdMultiplicativeToUnits_apply
    (ζ : torsion F) (e : Multiplicative (Fin (rank F) → ℤ)) :
    torsionProdMultiplicativeToUnits F (ζ, e) =
      (ζ : (𝓞 F)ˣ) * ∏ i, fundSystem F i ^ Multiplicative.toAdd e i

decls.name: TauCeti.NumberField.torsionProdMultiplicativeToUnits_bijective
decls.doc:
Dirichlet's unit theorem in its unique-decomposition form says exactly that realizing a pair
(root of unity, exponent vector) as a unit is bijective.
decls.statement:
theorem torsionProdMultiplicativeToUnits_bijective :
    Function.Bijective (torsionProdMultiplicativeToUnits F)

decls.name: TauCeti.NumberField.unitsMulEquivTorsionProdMultiplicative
decls.doc:
**Dirichlet's unit theorem, structural form.** The unit group of the ring of integers of a
number field is the product of its torsion subgroup and the free abelian group generated by the
fundamental system: a unit corresponds to its unique decomposition as a root of unity times a
product of powers of fundamental units (`NumberField.Units.exist_unique_eq_mul_prod`).
decls.title: Dirichlet's unit theorem, structural form
decls.statement:
def unitsMulEquivTorsionProdMultiplicative :
    (𝓞 F)ˣ ≃* torsion F × Multiplicative (Fin (rank F) → ℤ)

decls.name: TauCeti.NumberField.unitsMulEquivTorsionProdMultiplicative_symm_apply
decls.doc:
The inverse of `TauCeti.NumberField.unitsMulEquivTorsionProdMultiplicative` sends a pair to
the root of unity times the product of powers of fundamental units.
decls.statement:
theorem unitsMulEquivTorsionProdMultiplicative_symm_apply
    (ζ : torsion F) (e : Multiplicative (Fin (rank F) → ℤ)) :
    (unitsMulEquivTorsionProdMultiplicative F).symm (ζ, e) =
      (ζ : (𝓞 F)ˣ) * ∏ i, fundSystem F i ^ Multiplicative.toAdd e i

decls.name: TauCeti.NumberField.unitsMulEquivTorsionProdMultiplicative_apply
decls.doc:
The forward map of `TauCeti.NumberField.unitsMulEquivTorsionProdMultiplicative` reads off the
Dirichlet decomposition: a unit presented as a root of unity `ζ` times a product of powers of the
fundamental system is sent to the pair `(ζ, e)`.
decls.statement:
theorem unitsMulEquivTorsionProdMultiplicative_apply
    (ζ : torsion F) (e : Fin (rank F) → ℤ) :
    unitsMulEquivTorsionProdMultiplicative F
        ((ζ : (𝓞 F)ˣ) * ∏ i, fundSystem F i ^ e i) = (ζ, Multiplicative.ofAdd e)

decls.name: TauCeti.NumberField.even_card_torsion
decls.doc:
Mathlib's `NumberField.Units.torsionOrder` is by definition `Nat.card (torsion F)`, so
`even_torsionOrder` supplies the parity of `Nat.card (torsion F)` that the cyclic even-order
count expects.
decls.statement: theorem even_card_torsion : Even (Nat.card (torsion F))

decls.name: TauCeti.NumberField.card_elementaryTwoQuotient_units
decls.doc:
**The unit group of a number field has `2 ^ (rank + 1)` square classes.** The torsion
subgroup is cyclic of even order (it contains `-1`), contributing one factor of `2`, and the
free part of Dirichlet rank contributes `2 ^ rank`.
decls.title: The unit group of a number field has `2 ^ (rank + 1)` square classes
decls.statement:
theorem card_elementaryTwoQuotient_units :
    Nat.card (TauCeti.ElementaryTwoQuotient (𝓞 F)ˣ) = 2 ^ (rank F + 1)

decls.name: TauCeti.NumberField.instFiniteElementaryTwoQuotientUnitsRingOfIntegers
decls.doc: The elementary-2 quotient of the unit group of a number field is finite.
decls.statement: instance : Finite (TauCeti.ElementaryTwoQuotient (𝓞 F)ˣ)

decls.name: TauCeti.NumberField.twoRank_units
decls.doc: The 2-rank of the unit group of a number field is `rank F + 1`.
decls.statement: theorem twoRank_units : TauCeti.twoRank (𝓞 F)ˣ = rank F + 1

decls.name: TauCeti.NumberField.units_sq_index_eq
decls.doc:
**The exact unit-square index of genus theory.** For a number field `F`,
`[𝓞 F^× : (𝓞 F^×)²] = 2 ^ (rank F + 1)`. This is the subgroup-index reading of
`TauCeti.NumberField.card_elementaryTwoQuotient_units`; it sharpens the degree bound
`TauCeti.NumberField.units_sq_index_le` to an equality.
decls.title: The exact unit-square index of genus theory
decls.statement:
theorem units_sq_index_eq :
    (Subgroup.square (𝓞 F)ˣ).index = 2 ^ (rank F + 1)

decls.name: TauCeti.RamificationInertia.ncard_primesOver_eq_natCard_iff_of_isGaloisGroup
decls.doc:
In a finite flat Galois extension of domains, the number of primes over a prime ideal
equals the order of the Galois group iff the common ramification index and inertia degree are
both `1`.
decls.statement:
theorem ncard_primesOver_eq_natCard_iff_of_isGaloisGroup {A B : Type*}
    [CommRing A] [IsDomain A] [CommRing B] [IsDomain B] [Algebra A B] [Module.Finite A B]
    [Module.Flat A B] (G : Type*) [Group G] [Finite G] [MulSemiringAction G B]
    [IsGaloisGroup G A B] (P : Ideal A) [P.IsPrime] :
    (primesOver P B).ncard = Nat.card G ↔
      P.ramificationIdxIn B = 1 ∧ P.inertiaDegIn B = 1
